scone-scotland.s: Scone, near Perth in central Scotland, was the inauguration place of the kings of Scots, an important royal centre of the Pictish and Gaelic kings from at least the 9th century. Kings were enthroned on the Moot Hill on the Stone of Scone, which Edward I of England took to…

sharuhen.s: Sharuhen was a fortified town in southern Canaan, near Gaza, which served as a refuge of the Hyksos after their expulsion from Egypt. According to the tomb biography of the soldier Ahmose son of Ebana, the pharaoh Ahmose I besieged it for three years before taking it, around…

serdica.s: Serdica was the ancient and medieval city on the site of modern Sofia, the capital of Bulgaria. Named after the Thracian Serdi, it became a Roman city and the capital of the province of Dacia Mediterranea, and hosted a church council in 343.

simeon-i-of-bulgaria.s: Simeon I, known as Simeon the Great, ruled the First Bulgarian Empire from 893 to 927. Educated in Constantinople, he waged repeated wars against the Byzantine Empire, won a great victory at Achelous in 917 and claimed the title of tsar.

sohar.s: Sohar is a port city on the Batinah coast of northern Oman. In the early Islamic centuries it was one of the great ports of the Indian Ocean trade, linking the Gulf with India, East Africa and China, and it is often linked with the stories of Sindbad the Sailor.

sambandar.s: Sambandar, Thirugnana Sambandar, was a Tamil Shaiva poet-saint of the 7th century, one of the most revered of the Nayanars. Tradition says he began composing hymns to Shiva as a small child and died young; his hymns form the first three books of the Tevaram.

san-fernando-pampanga.s: San Fernando is a city in central Luzon, Philippines, the capital of Pampanga province. During the Philippine–American War the government of the First Philippine Republic moved there from Malolos in 1899 before retreating north.

sittaung-river.s: The Sittaung is a river of central and southern Myanmar, flowing south for about 420 km between the Bago Yoma hills and the Shan Plateau into the Gulf of Martaban. The town of Toungoo on its middle course was the cradle of the Toungoo dynasty.

stamford-lincolnshire.s: Stamford is a market town in southern Lincolnshire, England, on the River Welland. In the Viking Age it was one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw, submitting to Edward the Elder in 918.

stamford-connecticut.s: Stamford is a city in south-western Connecticut, United States, on Long Island Sound. It was founded in 1641 by Puritan settlers from Wethersfield on land bought from local Native Americans and joined the New Haven Colony, before the colony merged into Connecticut in 1665.

st-marys-church-lubeck.s: St. Mary's Church in Lübeck is a brick Gothic church built by the city's merchants between about 1250 and 1350 beside the town hall. Its soaring nave became the model for many churches around the Baltic and expressed the wealth of the Hanseatic League.

st-pauls-church-frankfurt.s: St. Paul's Church, the Paulskirche, is a former Lutheran church in Frankfurt am Main, built between 1789 and 1833. From May 1848 to May 1849 it was the meeting place of the Frankfurt Parliament, the first freely elected all-German national assembly, which drafted a…

salins-les-bains.s: Salins-les-Bains is a town in the Jura in eastern France whose salt springs were exploited from the Middle Ages and made it one of the richest places of the Free County of Burgundy. Its brine was piped to the Royal Saltworks at Arc-et-Senans, built in the 1770s, and the great…

saint-martin-island.s: Saint Martin is an island in the north-eastern Caribbean, divided by the Treaty of Concordia of 1648 between a French northern part and a Dutch southern part, Sint Maarten. The French part was owned by the Knights Hospitaller from 1651 to 1665, together with Saint Kitts and…

steiff.s: Steiff is a German toy company based in Giengen an der Brenz, founded by Margarete Steiff in 1880. It is best known for its plush teddy bears, first made in the early 1900s, which carry its trademark button in the ear.

sebastian-lotzer.s: Sebastian Lotzer was a furrier's journeyman and lay preacher in Memmingen who wrote Reformation pamphlets. In March 1525, as secretary of the Upper Swabian peasant army, he drafted the Twelve Articles, the demands of the German Peasants' War, with Christoph Schappeler.

st-georg-nordlingen.s: St. Georg is the main church of Nördlingen in Bavaria, one of the largest late Gothic hall churches in southern Germany, built between 1427 and 1505, with its tower completed in 1539. The tower, about 90 metres high and known as the Daniel, overlooks the town's intact ring of…

swabian-alemannic-fastnacht.s: Swabian-Alemannic Fastnacht, or Fasnet, is the traditional carnival of south-western Germany, northern Switzerland, Alsace and Vorarlberg, held before Lent. Figures in carved wooden masks and costumes parade through the streets, and the Narrensprung of Rottweil is one of the…

second-margrave-war.s: The Second Margrave War was a conflict of 1552 to 1554 in Franconia, in which Margrave Albert Alcibiades of Brandenburg-Kulmbach plundered the bishoprics of Bamberg and Würzburg and attacked Nuremberg. An alliance of princes and Franconian powers, led by Maurice of Saxony,…

schworbrief.s: The Schwörbrief is the constitution of the imperial city of Ulm, granted in 1397, which gave the guilds a majority on the city council. The mayor swore an annual oath to uphold it before the citizens, a custom still renewed on Schwörmontag each July.

schum-cities.s: The SchUM cities are Speyer, Worms and Mainz, whose Jewish communities formed a federation in the Middle Ages and were leading centres of Ashkenazi learning. The name comes from the initial Hebrew letters of the cities' names.

susak.s: Sušak is the eastern part of the Croatian city of Rijeka, across the Rječina river from the old town. Under the Treaty of Rome of 1924 it went to Yugoslavia while Fiume became Italian, so the river formed the border, and it grew as a Yugoslav port.

states-of-germany.s: The states of Germany, or Länder, are the sixteen federated states of the Federal Republic of Germany, each with its own constitution, parliament and government. They hold powers over education, policing and culture and take part in federal law-making through the Bundesrat.

suhl.s: Suhl is a town in the Thuringian Forest in southern Thuringia, Germany, known since the 16th century for gun-making and metalworking. In East Germany it was the capital of the Suhl district from 1952 to 1990.

setif-and-guelma-massacre.s: The Sétif and Guelma massacre followed demonstrations on 8 May 1945, VE Day, in the town of Sétif in French Algeria, where nationalist marchers clashed with police and rioting killed about a hundred Europeans. French troops, aircraft and settler militias answered with weeks of…

setif.s: Sétif is a city on the high plains of north-eastern Algeria, capital of Sétif Province. It stands on the site of the Roman colony of Sitifis, capital of the late Roman province of Mauretania Sitifensis.

sanliurfa.s: Şanlıurfa, commonly called Urfa, is a city in south-eastern Turkey on the site of ancient Edessa, a centre of early Syriac Christianity and capital of the crusader County of Edessa. After the First World War it was occupied by British and then French troops until a local…

sourou-migan-apithy.s: Sourou Migan Apithy was a Dahomeyan politician whose base was Porto-Novo and the south-east. Elected to the French Constituent Assemblies in 1945–1946 and then the National Assembly, he was the first prime minister of Dahomey in 1958–1959, vice-president under Hubert Maga and…

st-johns-river.s: The St Johns River is the longest river in Florida, flowing north for about 500 km before turning east to the Atlantic near Jacksonville. Jean Ribault named it the River of May in 1562, and in 1564 French Huguenots built Fort Caroline near its mouth, destroyed by the Spanish…

saturiwa.s: Saturiwa was a chief of the Timucua people near the mouth of the St Johns River in north-eastern Florida in the 1560s. He at first allied with the French Huguenots of Fort Caroline, supplying them with food, but relations deteriorated amid the colonists' hunger and demands.

susu-people.s: The Susu are a Mande-speaking people of coastal Guinea and north-western Sierra Leone. Moving towards the coast from the Futa Jallon highlands, partly under pressure from the Fula, they became traders and rice farmers and largely embraced Islam.

siem-reap.s: Siem Reap is a city in north-western Cambodia, capital of Siem Reap Province, near the ruins of Angkor. The province was ruled by Siam from the late 18th century until the Franco-Siamese treaty of 1907 returned it to Cambodia under French protection.

sino-french-war.s: The Sino-French War was fought between France and Qing China from August 1884 to April 1885 over control of Tonkin in northern Vietnam. France destroyed the Chinese Fujian fleet at Fuzhou and fought in Tonkin and on Taiwan, but a reverse at Lạng Sơn in March 1885 brought down…

sudanese-union-african-democratic-rally.s: The Sudanese Union – African Democratic Rally (US-RDA) was a political party in French Sudan, now Mali, founded in 1946 as the local section of the African Democratic Rally. Led by Mamadou Konaté and Modibo Keïta, it won the elections of the 1950s, led the territory to…

sangro.s: The Sangro is a river of central Italy, about 117 km long, rising in the Abruzzo Apennines and flowing into the Adriatic south of Ortona. In antiquity its lower valley lay in the land of the Frentani.

second-samnite-war.s: The Second Samnite War was fought between the Roman Republic and the Samnites from 326 to 304 BCE for control of Campania and central Italy. The Romans suffered a humiliating surrender at the Caudine Forks in 321 BCE but recovered, built the Via Appia and won over neighbouring…

schieringers.s: The Schieringers were one of two rival factions in late medieval Frisia, opposed to the Vetkopers, in feuds that lasted from the 14th to the end of the 15th century. Rooted in rivalries between chieftain families, monasteries and towns, the conflict weakened the Frisian Freedom.

seven-sealands.s: The Seven Sealands were the self-governing coastal lands of medieval Frisia between the Zuiderzee and the Weser, which formed a loose league during the Frisian Freedom. Their delegates met at the Upstalsboom near Aurich to settle disputes and agree common laws, the best known…

sallust.s: Sallust (Gaius Sallustius Crispus) was a Roman politician and historian. A partisan of Julius Caesar, he became the first governor of Africa Nova, the former Numidian kingdom, after 46 BCE and was accused of enriching himself there.

sarala-das.s: Sarala Das was a 15th-century Odia poet, often called the father of Odia literature. Writing in the reign of the Gajapati king Kapilendra Deva, he composed an Odia version of the Mahabharata that freely retells the epic with local legends and settings, as well as the Vilanka…

saloninus.s: Saloninus was the younger son of the Roman emperor Gallienus. Left at Cologne as Caesar under the guardianship of the prefect Silvanus, he was proclaimed Augustus in 260 when the general Postumus revolted.

sundargarh.s: Sundargarh is a town in northern Odisha, India, and the headquarters of Sundargarh district. It was the capital of the princely state of Gangpur, which merged into Orissa in 1948 and, with neighbouring Bonai, formed the district.

second-carib-war.s: The Second Carib War was fought on Saint Vincent from 1795 to 1797 between the British and the Garifuna, or Black Caribs, who were encouraged by revolutionary France. Led at first by Joseph Chatoyer, who was killed in March 1795, the Garifuna and their French allies overran…

safi-morocco.s: Safi is a port city on the Atlantic coast of Morocco, between El Jadida and Essaouira. Portugal held it from 1508 to 1541 and built a sea fortress there, the Dar el-Bahar, before the advance of the Saadi Sultanate forced its abandonment.

samson.s: Samson is a hero of the Book of Judges in the Hebrew Bible, a Nazirite of the tribe of Dan endowed with great strength. His exploits are set against the Philistines, who captured and blinded him after Delilah learned the secret of his hair.

sarhili.s: Sarhili was king of the Gcaleka Xhosa from 1835, succeeding his father Hintsa. He supported the cattle-killing movement inspired by Nongqawuse in 1856 and 1857, which ruined his people, and was driven across the Mbashe river by Cape forces.

shahnameh.s: The Shahnameh, or Book of Kings, is the national epic of Iran, completed by the poet Ferdowsi in about 1010 after some thirty years of work. In about 50,000 couplets of Persian verse it tells the history of Iran from the mythical first king to the Arab conquest of the Sasanian…

somnath-temple.s: The Somnath temple is a Hindu temple of Shiva on the coast of Saurashtra in Gujarat, India, revered as the first of the twelve jyotirlingas. Mahmud of Ghazni sacked it in 1025, and it was rebuilt and destroyed several times in the following centuries.

second-battle-of-tarain.s: The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 near Taraori in present-day Haryana, India, a year after the first. Muhammad of Ghor, using mounted archers and feigned retreats, defeated the much larger army of Prithviraj Chauhan, who was captured and later executed.

sosurim-of-goguryeo.s: Sosurim was king of Goguryeo from 371 to 384. He came to the throne after his father Gogugwon was killed fighting Baekje and set about rebuilding the state: in 372 he adopted Buddhism, brought from the Former Qin, and founded the Taehak, a Confucian academy, and in 373 he…

sangju.s: Sangju is a city in North Gyeongsang province, South Korea, on the upper Nakdong river. An ancient settlement and long one of the region's administrative centres, it gave half its name to Gyeongsang province, formed from the names of Gyeongju and Sangju.

spillings-hoard.s: The Spillings Hoard is the largest Viking Age silver hoard ever found, discovered on a farm at Spillings in northern Gotland in 1999. Buried around 870, it contains about 67 kilograms of silver, including more than 14,000 coins, mostly Islamic dirhams, with arm rings and…

san-salvador-de-jujuy.s: San Salvador de Jujuy is a city in far north-western Argentina, the capital of Jujuy Province, on the route from Tucumán to Upper Peru. Founded in 1593 by Francisco de Argañarás after earlier attempts failed, it was a stopping place for the mule trade to Potosí.

salta.s: Salta is a city in north-western Argentina, capital of Salta Province, in the Lerma valley. Founded in 1582 by Hernando de Lerma, it grew as a market for the mules sent to the silver mines of Potosí.

san-miguel-de-tucuman.s: San Miguel de Tucumán is a city in north-western Argentina, capital of Tucumán Province. Founded in 1565 by Diego de Villarroel and moved to its present site in 1685, it hosted the Congress of Tucumán, which declared the independence of the United Provinces of South America on…

sultan-hasanuddin.s: Sultan Hasanuddin was the sixteenth ruler of the Makassarese kingdom of Gowa in South Sulawesi, reigning from 1653 to 1669. He resisted the Dutch East India Company's attempts to monopolise the spice trade, but was defeated by a VOC force under Cornelis Speelman allied with…

san-people.s: The San are indigenous hunter-gatherer peoples of southern Africa, living today mainly in Botswana, Namibia and South Africa and speaking click languages of several families. Their rock art spans thousands of years.

state-of-cauca.s: The State of Cauca was a federal state of Colombia created in 1857 within the Granadine Confederation, covering a vast area of the south-west from the Pacific coast to the Amazon, with its capital at Popayán. Its governor Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera rebelled against the…

santander-spain.s: Santander is a port city on the Bay of Biscay in northern Spain and the capital of Cantabria. A medieval fishing and trading town, it grew in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries as Castile's port for wool and the colonial trade.

starkenburg.s: Starkenburg was the southern province of the Grand Duchy of Hesse and the People's State of Hesse from 1803 to 1937, lying east of the Rhine between the Main and the Neckar, with Darmstadt as its seat. It took its name from Starkenburg castle above Heppenheim, and its lands…

saint-sava.s: Saint Sava, born Rastko Nemanjić, was the youngest son of the Serbian ruler Stefan Nemanja. He became a monk on Mount Athos, where with his father he founded Hilandar monastery in 1198, and in 1219 he obtained self-governing status for the Serbian Church from the Patriarch of…

studenica-monastery.s: Studenica Monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery in central Serbia, founded by Stefan Nemanja around 1190 and his burial place. Its Church of the Virgin, faced with white marble, combines Romanesque and Byzantine styles and holds frescoes of 1209, and the monastery was the…

sibiu.s: Sibiu, German Hermannstadt, is a city in central Romania, in southern Transylvania. Founded by German settlers, the Transylvanian Saxons, in the twelfth century, it became their chief town and one of the strongest walled cities of the region, and in the eighteenth century it…

samuel-von-brukenthal.s: Samuel von Brukenthal was a Transylvanian Saxon nobleman and statesman who governed the Grand Principality of Transylvania for Maria Theresa and Joseph II from the 1770s to 1787. A collector of paintings, books and minerals, he built a baroque palace in Hermannstadt (Sibiu)…

stare-mesto-uherske-hradiste-district.s: Staré Město is a town in south-eastern Moravia, Czech Republic, beside Uherské Hradiště on the Morava river. Excavations there have uncovered a large ninth-century settlement of Great Moravia with churches, workshops and extensive cemeteries, and it has sometimes been…

svatopluk-i-of-moravia.s: Svatopluk I was ruler of Great Moravia from 870 to 894, under whom the state reached its greatest extent, including Bohemia, parts of southern Poland and Pannonia. He came to power by betraying his uncle Rastislav to the Franks and later favoured the Latin clergy, expelling…

stephen-of-perm.s: Stephen of Perm was a Russian missionary monk from Ustyug who converted many of the Komi people to Christianity from 1379 and became the first bishop of Perm in 1383. He created the Old Permic alphabet for the Komi language and translated liturgical texts into it.

sun-dance.s: The Sun Dance is a major religious ceremony of many Plains Indigenous peoples, including the Lakota, Cheyenne, Arapaho and Blackfoot. Held in summer around a central pole, it involves fasting, prayer, dancing and, among some nations, ritual piercing, as an offering for the…

sun-kewang.s: Sun Kewang was a Chinese military leader and an adopted son of the rebel Zhang Xianzhong. After Zhang's death in 1647 he and Li Dingguo led the remnants of his army into Yunnan and Guizhou and allied with the Southern Ming.

skagerrak.s: The Skagerrak is a strait between southern Norway, south-western Sweden and the Jutland peninsula of Denmark, linking the North Sea with the Kattegat and the Baltic. It has long been a major shipping route and fishing ground, and the coastal districts of Agder, Telemark and…

skien.s: Skien is a town in Telemark in south-eastern Norway, on the Skienselva river near the coast. It grew in the Middle Ages as a trading place, received town rights in the 14th century and later prospered from the export of timber.

skienselva.s: The Skienselva is a short river in Telemark, southern Norway, running from Lake Norsjø through the town of Skien to the sea at Porsgrunn. It is the lower part of the Skien watercourse, which drains much of Telemark, and was long used to float timber to the coast for export.

saphrax.s: Saphrax was a leader of the Greuthungi Goths who, with Alatheus, led part of the people across the Danube into Roman territory in 376 after the Hunnic invasion. Together with the Tervingi of Fritigern they fought the Romans in the Gothic War, and the sudden arrival of their…

surselva.s: The Surselva is the valley of the Vorderrhein in western Graubünden, Switzerland, stretching from the Oberalp Pass down to Ilanz and beyond. It is a heartland of the Romansh language and was the core of the Grey League, formed by the abbot of Disentis with local lords and…

sidi-saiyyed-mosque.s: The Sidi Saiyyed Mosque is a mosque in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, built in 1572–1573 in the last years of the Gujarat Sultanate by Sidi Saiyyed, a noble of Abyssinian origin. It is famous for its carved stone lattice windows, especially one showing intertwining trees with branches…

suakin.s: Suakin is a port town on the Red Sea coast of Sudan, built largely on a small coral island. A medieval trading port and a station for pilgrims bound for Mecca, it came under Ottoman rule in the 16th century as part of the province of Habesh and was transferred to Egypt in 1865.

spanish-golden-age.s: The Spanish Golden Age, or Siglo de Oro, was a period of flourishing in Spanish literature and art in the 16th and 17th centuries, under the Habsburg kings. It produced the novelist Miguel de Cervantes, the playwrights Lope de Vega and Calderón de la Barca, the poets Garcilaso…

serrania-de-ronda.s: The Serranía de Ronda is a range of limestone mountains in the west of Málaga province, Andalusia, Spain, around the town of Ronda. Its rugged terrain long favoured rebels and bandits: in the 9th century Umar ibn Hafsun held out at nearby Bobastro, and in 1570 it was a…

samsat.s: Samsat is a town in Adıyaman province in south-eastern Turkey, on the site of ancient Samosata on the upper Euphrates. It was the capital of the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Kummuh and later of the Hellenistic kingdom of Commagene, and the birthplace of the satirist Lucian.

shwebo.s: Shwebo is a town in the Sagaing Region of upper Myanmar, north-west of Mandalay. Formerly the village of Moksobo, it was the home of Alaungpaya, who rose there in 1752 against the Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom, founded the Konbaung dynasty and made it his first capital.

sami-people.s: The Sámi are the indigenous people of the far north of Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia's Kola Peninsula, a region they call Sápmi. Traditionally they lived by fishing, hunting, trapping and later reindeer herding, and they speak several related Uralic languages.

sulaymaniyah.s: Sulaymaniyah is a city in the Kurdistan Region of north-eastern Iraq, near the Iranian border. It was founded in 1784 by Ibrahim Pasha Baban as the capital of the Baban emirate and named after the Ottoman governor of Baghdad, Sulayman Pasha.

sad-al-dawla.s: Sa'd al-Dawla was the Hamdanid emir of Aleppo from 967 to 991, the son and successor of Sayf al-Dawla. Much of his reign was spent in struggles with rebellious commanders and between the Byzantine Empire, to which Aleppo paid tribute from 969, and the Fatimids of Egypt.

sad-i-ibn-zangi.s: Sa'd I ibn Zangi was the Salghurid atabeg of Fars in southern Iran from about 1198 to 1226. He strengthened the dynasty, built walls and mosques at Shiraz and fought the Khwarazmian Empire, which captured him and forced him to cede part of his lands.

shangdu.s: Shangdu, known in the West as Xanadu, was the summer capital of the Yuan dynasty, in present-day Inner Mongolia, China. Kublai Khan had it built from 1256 and held court there in summer, and Marco Polo described its palace and park.

shin-sawbu.s: Shin Sawbu was queen regnant of the Hanthawaddy Kingdom in lower Burma from 1454 to 1471, the only woman to rule a Burmese kingdom in her own right. A daughter of Razadarit, she had lived at the court of Ava before escaping home.

shihab-dynasty.s: The Shihab dynasty were an Arab family who ruled the emirate of Mount Lebanon under Ottoman suzerainty from 1697 to 1842, succeeding the Ma'n dynasty. Originally Sunni Muslims from Wadi al-Taym, some of them later became Maronite Christians.

solduz.s: Solduz is a valley and plain in West Azerbaijan province of north-western Iran, south of Lake Urmia, around the modern town of Naqadeh. It contains the mound of Hasanlu Tepe, whose fortified Iron Age citadel dominated the valley until its destruction around 800 BCE, and many…

sadducees.s: The Sadducees were a Jewish party of the Second Temple period, linked with the priestly aristocracy that controlled the Temple in Jerusalem from the 2nd century BCE. They accepted only the written Torah, rejected the oral tradition of the Pharisees and denied the resurrection…

simon-thassi.s: Simon Thassi was the second son of Mattathias and the last of the Maccabee brothers, who led Judaea from 142 BCE. He expelled the Seleucid garrison from the Akra in Jerusalem, and in 140 BCE an assembly confirmed him as high priest, commander and ethnarch, founding the…

simon-bar-giora.s: Simon bar Giora was a leader of the First Jewish–Roman War who commanded one of the rival factions in Jerusalem during the Roman siege of 70 CE. After the city fell he was captured, led in the triumph of Vespasian and Titus in Rome and executed.

simon-i-of-kartli.s: Simon I was King of Kartli in eastern Georgia from 1556 to 1569 and again from 1578 to 1600. He resisted both Safavid Iran, which held him captive for nearly a decade, and the Ottoman Empire, fighting to keep his kingdom independent between them.

suleja.s: Suleja is a town in Niger State, Nigeria, just north of the Federal Capital Territory. It was founded around 1828 as Abuja by the exiled Hausa rulers of Zazzau after the Fulani jihad and remained the seat of their emirate.

seven-wonders-of-the-ancient-world.n: Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
seven-wonders-of-the-ancient-world.s: The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World are a list of remarkable monuments drawn up by Greek writers of the Hellenistic period: the Great Pyramid of Giza, the Hanging Gardens of Babylon, the statue of Zeus at Olympia, the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, the Mausoleum at…

serpent-column.s: The Serpent Column is a bronze column of three intertwined snakes that once supported a golden tripod dedicated at Delphi by the Greek states that defeated Persia at Plataea in 479 BCE. Its coils bear the names of 31 allied states.

syriza.s: Syriza, the Coalition of the Radical Left, is a Greek left-wing party formed as an electoral alliance in 2004 and as a single party in 2012. Led by Alexis Tsipras, it won the elections of January 2015 on a promise to end austerity, but after a referendum rejected the…

spetses.s: Spetses is a small Greek island off the eastern coast of the Peloponnese, near the entrance to the Argolic Gulf. Like Hydra it built a merchant fleet in the 18th century, and its ships fought in the Greek War of Independence, when the island's Laskarina Bouboulina commanded…

saale.s: The Saale is a river of central Germany, about 413 km long, which rises in the Fichtelgebirge in Bavaria and flows north through Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt, past Jena and Halle, to join the Elbe. In the early Middle Ages it marked the boundary between Germans and Slavs, and…

sabellians.s: Sabellians is a name used by ancient and modern writers for the Oscan-speaking peoples of central and southern Italy related to the Sabines, such as the Samnites, Lucanians and Hirpini. Tradition held that many of them began as 'sacred spring' migrations of young men sent out…

sacco-river.s: The Sacco is a river of southern Lazio, Italy, flowing south-east through the valley between the Monti Ernici and the Monti Lepini to join the Liri. Its valley, the ancient homeland of the Hernici, carried the Via Latina and has long been a main route between Rome and Campania.

salome-daughter-of-herodias.s: Salome was a Herodian princess, daughter of Herodias and Herod Philip, named by Josephus. She is identified with the unnamed daughter of Herodias who, in the Gospels, danced before Herod Antipas and asked for the head of John the Baptist.

sakuradamon-incident.s: The Sakuradamon Incident was the assassination of Ii Naosuke, chief minister of the Tokugawa shogunate, on 24 March 1860 outside the Sakurada Gate of Edo Castle. The killers, mostly samurai from Mito, opposed his signing of trade treaties with Western powers without imperial…

sawayama-castle.s: Sawayama Castle was a Japanese mountain castle on Mount Sawa, in modern Hikone, Shiga Prefecture, commanding the road along the eastern side of Lake Biwa. It was the seat of Ishida Mitsunari until it fell to Tokugawa forces after the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600.

shiga-prefecture.s: Shiga Prefecture is a landlocked prefecture of the Kansai region of Japan, surrounding Lake Biwa, the country's largest lake, with its capital at Ōtsu. It corresponds to the old province of Ōmi, which lay on the main routes from Kyoto to eastern Japan and contained castle…

senhime.s: Senhime was a granddaughter of Tokugawa Ieyasu and the eldest daughter of the second shogun, Tokugawa Hidetada. Married as a child to Toyotomi Hideyori, she was rescued from Osaka Castle when it fell in 1615.

stesichorus.s: Stesichorus was a Greek lyric poet of the late 7th and 6th centuries BCE, associated with Himera in Sicily. He composed long narrative poems on myths such as the Trojan War, Heracles and Geryon, and the story of Helen, which influenced later epic and tragedy.

sabuktigin.s: Sabuktigin was a Turkic slave commander who ruled Ghazni from 977 to 997, nominally for the Samanids, and founded the Ghaznavid dynasty. He extended his power over Bust and the Kabul valley and repeatedly defeated the Hindu Shahi king Jayapala, pushing his frontier towards…

sous.s: The Sous is a region of south-western Morocco, the fertile valley of the Sous river between the High Atlas and the Anti-Atlas, with Agadir and Taroudant as its main towns. Long a land of Amazigh tribes and religious lodges, it was the base from which the Saadi dynasty rose in…

shingani.s: Shingani is one of the two historic quarters of old Mogadishu, on the coast beside Hamar Weyne. For centuries the city was divided between these two rival districts, each with its own merchant families and mosques.

shukkeien.s: Shukkeien is a Japanese landscape garden in Hiroshima, begun in 1620 for Asano Nagaakira, the first Asano lord of the Hiroshima domain, by his tea master Ueda Sōko. Its name means 'shrunken-scenery garden', as it recreates famous landscapes in miniature around a central pond.

silingi.s: The Silingi were a branch of the Vandals who probably lived in Silesia, which may take its name from them. They crossed the Rhine in 406 and entered Hispania in 409, receiving Baetica in 411, but were almost destroyed by the Visigoths, fighting for Rome, in 416–418.

sacra-infermeria.s: The Sacra Infermeria was the great hospital of the Knights Hospitaller in Valletta, Malta, begun in 1574 under Grand Master Jean de la Cassière. It was one of the largest and best-equipped hospitals in early modern Europe, with a long ward for hundreds of patients, who were…

somanathapura.s: Somanathapura is a village in Mysuru district, Karnataka, India, on the Kaveri river. It is known for the Keshava temple, built in 1268 by Somanatha, a commander of the Hoysala king Narasimha III.

sosevur.s: Sosevur, modern Angadi in Chikkamagaluru district, Karnataka, India, was the earliest seat of the Hoysala dynasty. Dynastic legend places there the story of the founder Sala, who killed a tiger at the command of a Jain teacher, a scene that became the royal emblem.

sima-daozi.s: Sima Daozi was a prince of the Eastern Jin dynasty of China, son of Emperor Jianwen and brother of Emperor Xiaowu. After Xiaowu's death in 396 he controlled the government in the name of the disabled Emperor An, together with his son Sima Yuanxian.

san-luis-potosi.s: San Luis Potosí is a state of north-central Mexico, with a capital of the same name founded in 1592 after the discovery of silver nearby. Its eastern part lies in the Huasteca, home to Huastec and Nahua communities.

state-protection-authority.s: The State Protection Authority, ÁVH, was the secret police of communist Hungary, known as the ÁVO until 1950. Under Mátyás Rákosi it carried out mass arrests, torture and the show trials of real and imagined opponents.

surrender-at-vilagos.s: The Surrender at Világos took place on 13 August 1849, when the Hungarian army under Artúr Görgei laid down its arms to the Russian forces that had intervened on the Austrian side. It effectively ended the Hungarian war of independence of 1848-1849.

sainte-marie-among-the-hurons.s: Sainte-Marie among the Hurons was a French Jesuit mission founded in 1639 near present-day Midland, Ontario, as the headquarters of the mission to the Wendat. It included a church, a hospital and farm buildings.

simcoe-county.s: Simcoe County is a county in central Ontario, Canada, lying between Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay. It covers most of the former Wendat homeland of Huronia, and archaeological sites of Wendat villages are numerous there.

sturlung-age.s: The Sturlung Age was a period of violent conflict in Iceland in the 13th century, named after the powerful Sturlung family. A few great chieftain families fought for supremacy, in battles such as Örlygsstaðir in 1238, while the Norwegian king Haakon IV encouraged their rivalry.

snettisham-hoard.s: The Snettisham Hoard is a series of Iron Age treasure deposits found at Snettisham in Norfolk, England, from 1948 onwards. It includes many gold and silver torcs, among them the Great Torc, buried in the 1st century BCE, together with coins and ingots.

sabya.s: Sabya is a town in the Jazan region of south-western Saudi Arabia, on the coastal plain of the Tihamah. The Sufi teacher Ahmad ibn Idris died there in 1837, and in the early 20th century it was the seat of his great-grandson Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi, ruler of the Idrisid…

saudi-yemeni-war.s: The Saudi–Yemeni War was fought in the spring of 1934 between Saudi Arabia and the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen over the border regions of Asir, Najran and Jizan. Saudi forces under Prince Faisal advanced along the Tihamah coast and took Hodeidah.

santa-cruz-de-mar-pequena.s: Santa Cruz de Mar Pequeña was a fortified trading post founded on the Atlantic coast of north-west Africa in 1478 by Diego García de Herrera, lord of the Canary Islands. It traded with local Berber tribes and was abandoned in the early 16th century.

sungbos-eredo.s: Sungbo's Eredo is a system of earthworks, a ditch and bank about 160 kilometres long, surrounding the area of Ijebu-Ode in south-western Nigeria. Radiocarbon dates suggest it was dug around the end of the first millennium CE, pointing to a large and organised society.

sauk.s: The Sauk, or Sac, are an Algonquian-speaking people of the western Great Lakes, closely allied with the Meskwaki. Pushed west from Michigan and Wisconsin, they settled along the upper Mississippi, where a disputed land cession of 1804 led to the Black Hawk War of 1832.

stari-grad.s: Stari Grad is a town on the Croatian island of Hvar. It was founded in 384 BCE as Pharos by Greek colonists from the island of Paros, who defeated the local Illyrians with help from Syracuse.

shkoder.s: Shkodër is a city in north-western Albania on the south-eastern shore of Lake Shkodër and one of the oldest towns in the Balkans. As Scodra it was the capital of the Illyrian king Gentius, captured by Rome in 168 BCE.

staraya-ladoga.s: Staraya Ladoga is a village on the Volkhov river near Lake Ladoga in north-western Russia, on the site of one of the earliest towns of Rus'. Founded around 753 as a trading settlement where Scandinavians, Finns and Slavs met, it lay on the river routes to the Dnieper and the…

shehu-alimi.s: Shehu Alimi was a Fulani Muslim cleric whose preaching drew followers in the Oyo Empire in the early 19th century. Around 1817 the rebel commander Afonja of Ilorin enlisted him and his Muslim fighters against the Alaafin of Oyo.

sunpu.s: Sunpu was the provincial capital of Suruga Province in Japan, on the site of the modern city of Shizuoka. Under the Imagawa clan it became a cultured castle town that attracted courtiers and poets from Kyoto.

suruga-province.s: Suruga Province was an old province of Japan in the central part of present-day Shizuoka Prefecture, on the Pacific coast below Mount Fuji. Governed by the Imagawa clan from the 14th century, it was conquered by Takeda Shingen in 1568 and later held by Tokugawa Ieyasu.

saint-nazarius.s: Nazarius was an early Christian martyr venerated in Milan, where Bishop Ambrose found his body and that of his companion Celsus in 395. In 765 Chrodegang of Metz brought relics believed to be his from Rome to the new monastery of Lorsch, which was dedicated to him.

st-blaise-abbey.s: St. Blaise Abbey was a Benedictine monastery at St. Blasien in the southern Black Forest, Germany, first recorded in the 9th century. It led a monastic reform movement in the 11th and 12th centuries and founded or reformed many houses in Swabia and Switzerland.

saint-verena.s: Verena is a saint venerated especially in Switzerland and south-western Germany. According to her legend she came from Egypt with the Theban Legion, lived as a hermit near Solothurn and later at Zurzach on the Rhine, where she cared for the poor and the sick.

st-gallen.s: St. Gallen is a city in north-eastern Switzerland, capital of the canton of St. Gallen, south of Lake Constance. It grew around the Abbey of Saint Gall, founded in the 8th century, and became a free imperial city whose linen trade made it wealthy and often set it against the…

saint-othmar.s: Othmar was an Alemannic priest who in 719 founded the Abbey of Saint Gall at the site of the hermit Gallus's cell and became its first abbot. He introduced the Benedictine rule and founded a hospital and a home for lepers.

salem-baden-wurttemberg.s: Salem is a municipality in the Lake Constance district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, a few kilometres north of the lake. It grew around Salem Abbey, a Cistercian house founded in the 1130s that became one of the richest imperial abbeys in Swabia.

salem-massachusetts.s: Salem is a coastal city in Essex County, Massachusetts, north-east of Boston. Settled in 1626 and taken over in 1628 by an advance party of the Massachusetts Bay Company under John Endecott, it was one of the first towns of New England.

salem-witch-trials.s: The Salem witch trials were a series of prosecutions for witchcraft in the Province of Massachusetts Bay in 1692 and 1693, centred on Salem Village and the town of Salem. Set off by the fits of young girls, accusations spread to more than 200 people.

salem-new-jersey.s: Salem is a city in south-western New Jersey near the Delaware River. It was founded in 1675 by the English Quaker John Fenwick, one of the proprietors of West Jersey, as one of the first English settlements in the Delaware valley.

schule-schloss-salem.s: Schule Schloss Salem is a boarding school in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, founded in 1920 by Prince Maximilian of Baden and the educator Kurt Hahn in the former imperial abbey of Salem. Its teaching aimed to build character and civic responsibility through community service,…

steinhausen-pilgrimage-church.s: The pilgrimage church at Steinhausen, near Bad Schussenried in upper Swabia, was built from 1728 to 1733 by Dominikus Zimmermann for the abbey of Schussenried, with frescoes by his brother Johann Baptist Zimmermann. Its oval plan and light-filled interior make it one of the…

saverne-affair.s: The Saverne Affair, or Zabern Affair, was a political crisis in the German Empire in 1913. In the Alsatian garrison town of Saverne a young Prussian lieutenant insulted the local population, and the army then arrested civilians without legal authority.

sacsayhuaman.s: Sacsayhuamán is an Inca complex on a hill overlooking Cusco in Peru, famous for its zigzag walls of huge, precisely fitted stone blocks. Built mainly in the 15th century, it served ceremonial and military purposes.

sagala.s: Sagala was an ancient city of the Punjab, generally identified with modern Sialkot in Pakistan. It was the capital of the Indo-Greek king Menander I in the 2nd century BCE and is described in the Milindapanha as a prosperous city.

suharto.s: Suharto was an Indonesian army general who took power after the failed coup of 1965, during mass killings of alleged communists, and was president from 1967 to 1998. His New Order regime brought rapid economic growth and stability but also the invasion of East Timor,…

sirkap.s: Sirkap is the second city of Taxila, in present-day Punjab, Pakistan, laid out on a grid plan in the 2nd century BCE by the Indo-Greeks and rebuilt under the Indo-Scythians and Indo-Parthians. Excavations by John Marshall uncovered streets, houses, stupas and the double-headed…

sinn-fein.s: Sinn Féin is an Irish republican political party founded by Arthur Griffith in 1905. After the Easter Rising it became the main nationalist party, winning most Irish seats in 1918 and setting up Dáil Éireann.

saulteaux.s: The Saulteaux are a branch of the Ojibwe people, named by the French after the rapids of Sault Ste. Marie.

six-nations-of-the-grand-river.n: Six Nations of the Grand River
six-nations-of-the-grand-river.s: Six Nations of the Grand River is the most populous First Nations reserve in Canada, near Brantford in southern Ontario, home to members of all six nations of the Iroquois Confederacy. It derives from land along the Grand River granted by the Haldimand Proclamation of 1784 to…

sefidrud.s: The Sefidrud, 'White River', is the second-longest river of Iran, formed by the meeting of the Qezel Owzan and the Shahrud at Manjil and flowing north through the Alborz to the Caspian Sea in Gilan. Its delta divided Gilan into Biyapas, west of the river, and Biyapish to the…

sir-seewoosagur-ramgoolam-botanical-gard.s: The Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Botanical Garden, long known as the Pamplemousses Garden, is a botanical garden in northern Mauritius and one of the oldest in the southern hemisphere. Begun in 1735 as the private garden of the governor Mahé de La Bourdonnais, it was developed…

salo.s: Salò is a town on the western shore of Lake Garda in Lombardy, northern Italy. In 1943–1945 it housed ministries and offices of Mussolini's German-backed Italian Social Republic, which is therefore often called the Republic of Salò.

suwayda.s: Suwayda is a city in southern Syria, capital of the Suwayda Governorate in the Jabal al-Druze, whose population is mainly Druze. It was the capital of the autonomous Jabal Druze State under the French Mandate and a centre of the Great Syrian Revolt led by Sultan al-Atrash in…

sri-lankan-tamils.s: Sri Lankan Tamils are the Tamil-speaking people native to northern and eastern Sri Lanka, with Jaffna as their cultural centre. Mostly Hindu, with a Christian minority, they formed the Jaffna kingdom in the Middle Ages.

shaykh-junayd.s: Shaykh Junayd was head of the Safavid Sufi order of Ardabil from 1447 to 1460. Driven from Ardabil by a rival, he turned the order into a militant movement, won followers among the Turkmen tribes of Anatolia and married a sister of the Aq Qoyunlu ruler Uzun Hasan.

scotts-hall-jamaica.s: Scott's Hall is a Maroon community in the parish of St Mary in Jamaica, one of the towns of the Windward Maroons established after the peace of 1739. Its people, like those of Moore Town, Charles Town and Accompong, still claim the land and self-government guaranteed by that…

second-maroon-war.s: The Second Maroon War of 1795 to 1796 was a conflict in Jamaica between the Maroons of Trelawny Town and the British colonial government under the Earl of Balcarres. After months of guerrilla fighting in the Cockpit Country, the Maroons surrendered on terms, but the colonial…

storsjon.s: Storsjön, the "great lake", is a large lake in Jämtland in central Sweden, among the largest in the country. Its shores and islands, including Frösön, formed the heartland of medieval Jämtland, and the town of Östersund stands on its eastern shore.

sverre-of-norway.s: Sverre Sigurdsson was King of Norway from 1184 to 1202, having led the Birkebeiner faction in the civil wars from 1177. Claiming to be a son of King Sigurd Munn, he defeated his rival Magnus Erlingsson and strengthened royal power against the church, which excommunicated him.

sidoarjo.s: Sidoarjo is a town and regency in East Java, Indonesia, on the Brantas delta just south of Surabaya. The fertile delta was the heartland of the 11th-century kingdom of Janggala.

sook-ching.s: Sook Ching, meaning "purge through cleansing", was the mass killing of ethnic Chinese by the Japanese military in Singapore and Malaya after the fall of Singapore in February 1942. Chinese men were screened at registration centres, and those suspected of anti-Japanese…

sangrur.s: Sangrur is a city in southern Punjab, India, and the headquarters of Sangrur district. In the 19th century it became the capital of the princely state of Jind, whose rulers built palaces, gardens and public buildings there.

sarup-singh-of-jind.s: Sarup Singh was Raja of Jind, a Sikh princely state in the Punjab, from 1837 until his death in 1864. During the Indian Rebellion of 1857 he sent troops to support the British at the siege of Delhi, and was rewarded with additional territory and honours.

siege-of-caizhou.s: The Siege of Caizhou in 1233 and 1234 was the final campaign against the Jurchen Jin dynasty in China. Mongol forces and a Southern Song army besieged Emperor Aizong in the city of Caizhou in Henan, which fell in February 1234.

seoul.s: Seoul is the capital of South Korea, on the Han river in the north-west of the peninsula. As Hanyang, later Hanseong, it was the capital of Joseon from 1394, with palaces such as Gyeongbokgung, and it remained the capital of the Korean Empire and, as Keijo, of Japanese-ruled…

sejong-the-great.s: Sejong the Great was the fourth king of Joseon Korea, ruling from 1418 to 1450. He supported the Hall of Worthies, a royal research institute, and under him Korea created the Hangul alphabet, rain gauges, water clocks and new works on agriculture and medicine.

santissima-trinita-di-saccargia.s: Santissima Trinità di Saccargia is a Romanesque church near Codrongianos in northern Sardinia, consecrated in 1116 and given by the judges of Logudoro to Camaldolese monks. Built in Pisan style of alternating black basalt and white limestone, it has a tall bell tower and a…

santa-catarina.s: Santa Catarina is a state of southern Brazil on the Atlantic coast, with its capital at Florianópolis on Santa Catarina Island. Settled by Portuguese and Azorean colonists and later by German and Italian immigrants, it saw fighting in the Ragamuffin War, when rebels briefly…

shah-nawaz-bhutto.s: Shah Nawaz Bhutto was a politician from Sindh who became diwan, or chief minister, of Junagadh State in 1947. He advised the Nawab Mahabat Khanji III to accede to Pakistan, a decision overturned when India took control of the state later that year.

syrym-datuly.s: Syrym Datuly was a Kazakh batyr of the Baiuly tribes of the Junior Zhuz who led a revolt from 1783 to 1797 against Russian colonial pressure and the khans who cooperated with it. His forces raided Russian forts along the Ural line and helped drive out Khan Nurali.

shahrud-river.s: The Shahrud is a river of northern Iran that flows through the Alborz mountains and joins the Qezel Owzan at Manjil to form the Sefidrud, which runs to the Caspian Sea. Its valley and that of its tributary the Alamut formed the district of Rudbar, centre of the Justanid kings…

sas-bahu-temple.s: The Sas-Bahu Temple is a pair of Hindu temples inside Gwalior Fort in Madhya Pradesh, India, dedicated to Vishnu and completed in 1093 by the Kachchhapaghata king Mahipala. The larger temple, though its tower has collapsed, is richly carved inside and out.

shahu-of-kolhapur.s: Shahu of Kolhapur, born Yeshwantrao Ghatge in the family of the chiefs of Kagal, was adopted into the Kolhapur royal house in 1884 and ruled the princely state from 1894 to 1922. A social reformer, he founded schools and hostels, supported the Satyashodhak movement and in 1902…

shahu-i.s: Shahu I was the fifth Chhatrapati of the Maratha Empire, a grandson of Shivaji. Held captive by the Mughals from 1689, he was released in 1707 and won the Maratha throne against his aunt Tarabai, ruling from Satara.

samuel-gottlieb-gmelin.s: Samuel Gottlieb Gmelin was a German physician and naturalist in Russian service. From 1768 he led an expedition of the St Petersburg Academy of Sciences through southern Russia, the Caspian coast and northern Persia, describing its plants, animals and peoples.

sikh-gurus.s: The Sikh gurus were the ten spiritual masters who founded and led Sikhism, from Guru Nanak, born in 1469, to Guru Gobind Singh, who died in 1708. They compiled the scripture, founded centres such as Amritsar and, under the later gurus, organised the community to resist Mughal…

sayyida-shirin.s: Sayyida Shirin was a Buyid queen who ruled at Rayy in northern Iran as regent for her son Majd al-Dawla from 997 until her death in 1028. A princess of the Bavandid dynasty of Tabaristan, she kept power by skilful diplomacy, and Mahmud of Ghazni is said to have held back from…

simhavishnu.s: Simhavishnu was a king of the Pallava dynasty of Kanchipuram in southern India in the late 6th century. He expelled the Kalabhras from the Kaveri delta, taking the Chola country, and with it the Pallavas became the leading power of the Tamil lands.

shankaragana.s: Shankaragana was a king of the Kalachuris of Mahishmati in the late 6th century, son of Krishnaraja and father of Buddharaja. Copper-plate grants show his authority reaching Ujjain in Malwa and parts of Gujarat and the northern Deccan.

shah-abdul-latif-bhittai.s: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was a Sufi poet of Sindh and the most celebrated poet of the Sindhi language. His collected verse, the Shah Jo Risalo, retells local folk romances as allegories of the soul's search for God.

sanjaya-of-mataram.s: Sanjaya was a king of Central Java in the early 8th century, regarded as the founder of the Medang Kingdom of Mataram. The Canggal inscription of 732 records him erecting a Shiva lingam, and later kings, such as those listed in the Mantyasih inscription of 907, traced their…

stockholm-bloodbath.s: The Stockholm Bloodbath was the mass execution of some eighty Swedish nobles, clergy and burghers in Stockholm in November 1520, ordered by Christian II of Denmark after his conquest of Sweden. Accused of heresy for opposing the archbishop, they were beheaded in the main square.

sture-family.s: The Sture family was a Swedish noble family whose members governed Sweden as regents during the late Kalmar Union. Sten Sture the Elder defeated the Danish king Christian I at Brunkeberg in 1471, and Svante Nilsson and Sten Sture the Younger continued to resist Danish kings…

shinran.s: Shinran was a Japanese Buddhist monk, a disciple of Hōnen and founder of the Jōdo Shinshū, or True Pure Land school. Exiled in 1207, he married and lived among ordinary people, teaching that salvation depended entirely on faith in the Buddha Amida.

salastambha.s: Salastambha was the founder of the Mlechchha dynasty of Kamarupa, which took power in Assam in the mid-7th century after the end of the Varman line of Bhaskaravarman. His dynasty ruled from Haruppeshvara, near modern Tezpur, until the late 9th century, when it was succeeded by…

shaktism.s: Shaktism is a major tradition of Hinduism that worships the goddess, Devi or Shakti, as the supreme power of the universe. Based on texts such as the Devi Mahatmya and the Tantras, it reveres goddesses such as Durga, Kali and Kamakhya.

sujanpur-tira.s: Sujanpur Tira is a town on the Beas river in the Hamirpur district of Himachal Pradesh, India. Raja Sansar Chand of Kangra made it his court in the late 18th century, building a palace and temples with wall paintings, and it became a centre of the Kangra school of miniature…

sulaimanu-of-kano.s: Sulaimanu was the first Fulani emir of Kano in northern Nigeria, ruling from 1807 to 1819. A scholar and a flagbearer of Usman dan Fodio, he was chosen to lead Kano after the jihadists overthrew its last Hausa king, Muhammad Alwali.

susharman.s: Susharman was the fourth and last king of the Kanva dynasty of Magadha in northern India, known from the Puranas. According to them he was killed around 28 BCE by a king of the Satavahana dynasty, usually identified as its founder Simuka, bringing the Kanva line to an end…

sakhalin-oblast.s: Sakhalin Oblast is a federal subject of Russia covering the island of Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands, with its capital at Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk. It was formed in 1947 after the Soviet Union took southern Sakhalin, Japanese Karafuto, and the Kurils at the end of the Second World War.

savitsky-museum.s: The Savitsky Museum, the State Museum of Arts of Karakalpakstan in Nukus, Uzbekistan, was founded in 1966 by the artist and collector Igor Savitsky. Far from Moscow, he gathered tens of thousands of works, including Russian and Central Asian avant-garde paintings banned under…

salween.s: The Salween is a major river of South-East Asia, rising on the Tibetan Plateau and flowing south through Yunnan, the Shan and Karenni hills of Myanmar, and along part of the Thai border to the Andaman Sea at Mawlamyine. Its deep, rapid course is largely unnavigable, and for…

simraungadh.s: Simraungadh is a town and archaeological site in Bara District of southern Nepal, close to the border with Bihar. It was the capital of the Karnat dynasty of Mithila from the late 11th century until Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq took it in 1324.

srinagar.s: Srinagar is the largest city of the Kashmir valley, on the Jhelum River and the shores of Dal Lake, and the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir in India. It was the capital of the Shah Mir and Chak sultans and later a centre of Mughal, Afghan, Sikh and Dogra rule.

srinagar-uttarakhand.s: Srinagar is a town on the Alaknanda River in Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand, India. It was the capital of the Panwar kings of Garhwal from the 16th century until the Gorkha conquest of 1804, after which the restored dynasty moved to Tehri.

seiyun.s: Seiyun is a town in the Wadi Hadramawt in eastern Yemen. It was the capital of the Kathiri sultans, whose large white mud-brick palace still stands in the town and now houses a museum.

sputnik-1.s: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial Earth satellite, launched by the Soviet Union from Baikonur on 4 October 1957. A polished sphere with four antennas, it transmitted radio signals for three weeks and burned up in the atmosphere in January 1958.

surkhay-khan-i.s: Surkhay Khan I was khan of Kazikumukh, the Lak state in the mountains of Dagestan, in the first half of the 18th century. Allied with Hajji Davud, he sacked Shamakhi in 1721 and afterwards ruled Shirvan for a time under Ottoman protection.

smaradahana.s: The Smaradahana ('Burning of the God of Love') is an Old Javanese kakawin poem written by Mpu Dharmaja at the court of Kediri in the early 12th century. It tells how Shiva burned Kama, the god of love, with his third eye, and how Kama and his wife were reborn in human form.

senufo.s: The Senufo are a people of West Africa living in northern Côte d'Ivoire, southern Mali and western Burkina Faso, speaking Gur languages. They are mainly farmers, organised in villages and lineages, with the poro society governing initiation.

sikasso.s: Sikasso is a city in southern Mali, near the borders with Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. In the late 19th century it was the capital of the kingdom of Kenedougou, defended by a massive earthen wall that withstood Samori Ture's siege of 1887–1888.

simonides-of-ceos.s: Simonides of Ceos was a Greek lyric poet from Ioulis on the island of Keos. He wrote victory odes, laments and epigrams for patrons across the Greek world, including the tyrants of Athens and Thessalian lords, and his epitaphs for the dead of Thermopylae and the Persian Wars…

sorghaghtani-beki.s: Sorghaghtani Beki was a Keraite princess, niece of Ong Khan, who married Tolui, youngest son of Genghis Khan. After Tolui's death she managed his appanage in northern China and raised her four sons, Möngke, Kublai, Hülegü and Ariq Böke.

samatata.s: Samatata was an ancient region of south-eastern Bengal, centred on the area around modern Comilla in Bangladesh. It is named as a frontier kingdom in Samudragupta's Allahabad pillar inscription of the 4th century CE, and the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang visited it in the 7th century.

sarts.s: Sart was a name used in Central Asia for settled, town-dwelling and farming peoples, as distinct from nomads, especially in the oases of Khwarazm, Ferghana and Tashkent. Originally meaning 'merchant', it came to cover Turkic- and Persian-speaking settled Muslims.

salmas.s: Salmas is a city in West Azerbaijan province in north-western Iran, on a plain north-west of Lake Urmia near the Turkish border. In the 18th century it was ruled together with Khoy by the Donboli khans.

shaki-azerbaijan.s: Sheki is a city in northern Azerbaijan on the southern slopes of the Greater Caucasus, long a stop on regional trade routes and a centre of silk production. From the 1740s it was the capital of the Sheki Khanate, whose Palace of the Shaki Khans, decorated with stained glass…

stroganov-family.s: The Stroganovs were a family of Russian merchants and industrialists who grew rich from salt, furs and trade in the Perm region in the 16th century. Ivan IV granted them vast lands on the Kama, and they hired the Cossack leader Yermak, whose expedition of 1581–82 began the…

seraikela-kharsawan-district.s: Seraikela Kharsawan is a district of Jharkhand, India, created in 2001 from West Singhbhum district, with its headquarters at Seraikela. It is named after the former princely states of Seraikela and Kharsawan, which merged with Orissa in 1948 and were transferred to Bihar…

sinja.s: Sinja is a valley in Jumla district in the Karnali region of western Nepal that served as the capital of the Khasa Malla kingdom from the 12th to the 14th century. Remains of temples, stone pillars and inscriptions survive there.

sisowath-sirik-matak.s: Sisowath Sirik Matak was a Cambodian prince and politician of the Sisowath branch of the royal family and a cousin of Norodom Sihanouk. As deputy prime minister he joined Lon Nol in deposing Sihanouk in March 1970 and became a leading figure of the Khmer Republic.

sangye-gyatso.s: Sangye Gyatso was regent, or desi, of Tibet from 1679 under the Fifth Dalai Lama. He concealed the Dalai Lama's death in 1682 for some fifteen years while completing the Potala Palace, and wrote major works on medicine, astronomy and history.

saint-sophia-cathedral-kyiv.s: Saint Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv is an Orthodox cathedral founded by Yaroslav the Wise in the first half of the 11th century, built on Byzantine models and named after the Hagia Sophia of Constantinople. It was the metropolitan church of Kievan Rus', and its interior keeps…

saint-sophia-cathedral-polotsk.s: Saint Sophia Cathedral in Polotsk, Belarus, was built in the mid-11th century, probably under Prince Vseslav of Polotsk, as the principality's chief church, matching the Sophia cathedrals of Kyiv and Novgorod. Damaged and rebuilt several times, it was reconstructed in Baroque…

sfax.s: Sfax is a port city on the Gulf of Gabès in eastern Tunisia and the country's second-largest city. It grew in the Aghlabid period, when its walls and Great Mosque were built in the 9th century.

salamis-cyprus.s: Salamis was an ancient city on the east coast of Cyprus, north of modern Famagusta, founded in the 11th century BCE as successor to Enkomi. Its kings were often the strongest on the island, notably Evagoras I in the 4th century BCE.

salamis-island.s: Salamis is the largest Greek island in the Saronic Gulf, lying close to the coast of Attica west of Piraeus. Athens and Megara fought over it until Athens took it in the 6th century BCE, traditionally under Solon.

suppiluliuma-ii.s: Suppiluliuma II was the last known king of the Hittite Empire, reigning from about 1207 BCE. His inscriptions record naval battles against ships of Alashiya, the kingdom of Cyprus, and fighting on the island itself.

shaushgamuwa.s: Shaushgamuwa was a king of Amurru in the late 13th century BCE and a vassal and brother-in-law of the Hittite king Tudhaliya IV. Their surviving treaty is notable for ordering Amurru to treat Assyria as an enemy and to stop Assyrian merchants and Ahhiyawan ships from trading…

saddell-abbey.s: Saddell Abbey is a ruined Cistercian monastery on the east coast of Kintyre in Argyll, Scotland. It is traditionally said to have been founded by Somerled, King of the Isles, or by his son Ragnall in the later 12th century.

shishunaga.s: Shishunaga was a king of Magadha in eastern India and founder of the Shishunaga dynasty, which replaced the line of Bimbisara around the late 5th or early 4th century BCE. Buddhist sources say he was a minister raised to the throne by the people.

shishunaga-dynasty.s: The Shishunaga dynasty ruled the kingdom of Magadha in eastern India from around the late 5th century BCE until about 345 BCE. Founded by Shishunaga, who conquered Avanti, it kept its court at Rajagriha, Vaishali and Pataliputra.

sirwah.s: Sirwah is an archaeological site in the Marib governorate of Yemen, west of Marib, that was a major religious and political centre of the ancient kingdom of Saba. Its temple of the god Almaqah held the great inscription of the Sabaean ruler Karib'il Watar, recording his…

sena-mozambique.s: Sena is a town on the south bank of the Zambezi in central Mozambique. Already a trading post of Swahili merchants, it was occupied by the Portuguese in the 1530s and became, with Tete upriver, one of their main bases in the interior, trading with the Mutapa state and the…

sena-dynasty.s: The Sena dynasty ruled Bengal from the late 11th century to the early 13th century, after taking over from the Pala Empire. Its kings, notably Vijaya Sena and Ballala Sena, patronised Brahmanical Hinduism and Sanskrit literature, and the poet Jayadeva is associated with the…

sil-naedo-slaine.s: Síl nÁedo Sláine was a branch of the southern Uí Néill dynasty of early medieval Ireland, descended from Áed Sláine, a 7th-century king of Tara. Its kings ruled Brega, the plain north of the Liffey in modern Meath and Dublin, and several held the kingship of Tara in the 7th…

slane.s: Slane is a village above the River Boyne in County Meath, Ireland. On the Hill of Slane St Patrick is said to have lit a Paschal fire in defiance of the king of Tara, and a monastery founded there became an important church of the kingdom of Brega until it suffered Norse raids.

salomon-of-brittany.s: Salomon was king of Brittany from 857 to 874. A nephew of Nominoe, he murdered his cousin Erispoe and seized power, then fought and negotiated with Charles the Bald, who granted him the Cotentin and Avranchin in 867.

singaraja.s: Singaraja is a port town on the north coast of Bali, Indonesia, and the capital of Buleleng Regency. It was founded as the royal seat of the Kingdom of Buleleng in the 17th century by Gusti Panji Sakti.

sisibe.s: The Sisibe were the ruling lineage of Bundu, the Muslim state between the Senegal and Falémé rivers, descended from its founder Malik Sy, who settled there around 1690. His successors took the title almamy, and rivalry between branches of the lineage made successions often…

samlaut-uprising.s: The Samlaut uprising was a peasant revolt that broke out in 1967 around Samlaut in Battambang province, Cambodia, provoked by forced government rice purchases and land grievances. The army under Lon Nol suppressed it harshly.

sangkum-reastr-niyum.s: The Sangkum Reastr Niyum, the People's Socialist Community, was the political movement founded by Norodom Sihanouk in 1955 after he abdicated the throne to enter politics. It won every seat in the National Assembly in the elections from 1955 to 1966 and governed Cambodia under…

stotzas.s: Stotzas was a Byzantine soldier who led the great mutiny of the army in Africa in 536, soon after the reconquest of the Vandal kingdom. The mutineers, angered by arrears of pay and disputes over land and religion, nearly took Carthage before Belisarius returned and defeated them.

saint-padarn.s: Saint Padarn, in Latin Paternus, was a 6th-century Welsh saint, traditionally a bishop and the founder of the monastery of Llanbadarn Fawr near Aberystwyth. Llanbadarn became one of the leading churches of medieval Wales and the seat of an early bishopric.

soysisamouth.s: Soysisamouth was the first king of Champasak in southern Laos. A grandson of King Sourigna Vongsa of Lan Xang, he was installed at Champasak in 1713 with the support of the influential monk Phra Khru Phonsamek, separating the south from the kingdom of Vientiane.

syennesis.s: Syennesis was the name, or perhaps the title, of the native kings of Cilicia in southern Anatolia during the period of Achaemenid rule. Herodotus mentions a Syennesis who helped arrange the peace between Lydia and Media in 585 BCE, and Xenophon describes another who supported…

sigibert-the-lame.s: Sigibert the Lame was king of the Franks of Cologne in the late 5th and early 6th centuries, lamed by a wound received fighting the Alemanni at Zülpich. An ally of Clovis I, he sent his son Chloderic to fight the Visigoths at Vouillé in 507.

susa-piedmont.s: Susa is a town in the Susa valley of Piedmont, north-western Italy, at the foot of the routes over the Montgenèvre and Mont Cenis passes. As Segusio it was the seat of the Alpine kingdom of Donnus and Cottius and later of the small Roman province of the Cottian Alps.

subic-family.s: The Šubić of Bribir were a Croatian noble family from Bribir in northern Dalmatia, one of the twelve noble tribes of Croatia. They rose to great power in the late 13th century under Paul I Šubić, ban of Croatia and lord of Bosnia, and dominated Croatia and Dalmatia until the…

sapa-inca.s: Sapa Inca, the 'unique Inca', was the title of the ruler of the Inca state. Believed to descend from the sun god Inti, the Sapa Inca was an absolute ruler of sacred status, governing the four quarters of the empire from Cusco.

sinchi-roca.s: Sinchi Roca was, in Inca tradition, the second ruler of Cusco and the son of the founder Manco Capac, probably in the 13th century. Spanish chroniclers credit him with consolidating the early Inca settlement in the Cusco valley, but little is known of his reign, and his…

sarmizegetusa-regia.s: Sarmizegetusa Regia was the capital of the Dacian kingdom, built on mountain terraces at about 1,200 metres in the Orăștie Mountains of Romania. It had a fortress, a sacred zone of circular and rectangular sanctuaries, and workshops.

sitobu.s: Sitobu is remembered in Dagomba tradition as a son of Na Gbewaa, founder of the Mamprugu kingdom, and as the ancestor of the royal house of Dagbon in present-day northern Ghana. After a dispute among Na Gbewaa's sons over the succession he moved west with his followers.

saddharma-ratnavaliya.s: The Saddharma Ratnavaliya is a classic of Sinhala prose written in the 13th century by the monk Dharmasena Thera. Based on the Pali commentary on the Dhammapada, it retells Buddhist stories in lively, everyday Sinhala for ordinary readers, and it is valued as a model of the…

sinhala-language.s: Sinhala is the Indo-Aryan language of the Sinhalese people and one of the official languages of Sri Lanka, written in its own script. Descended from the speech of settlers from northern India in the 1st millennium BCE, it developed apart from related languages and absorbed…

strata-florida-abbey.s: Strata Florida Abbey is a ruined Cistercian abbey near Pontrhydfendigaid in Ceredigion, Wales, founded in 1164 and soon refounded on its present site under the patronage of Rhys ap Gruffydd. It became a centre of Welsh learning and politics, where chronicles of the Welsh…

saint-david.s: Saint David, Dewi Sant in Welsh, was a 6th-century bishop and monastic founder in south-west Wales and is the patron saint of Wales. His monastery at Mynyw, later St Davids, became the leading church of Wales and a major place of pilgrimage.

sherburn-in-elmet.s: Sherburn-in-Elmet is a village in North Yorkshire, England, between Leeds and Selby. Its name preserves that of the early British kingdom of Elmet, and in the Middle Ages it was an important estate and residence of the archbishops of York.

saeberht-of-essex.s: Sæberht was king of the East Saxons from about 604 until about 616 and the first Christian king of Essex. A nephew of King Æthelberht of Kent, he accepted baptism and allowed Mellitus to establish a bishopric in London, but his sons returned to paganism after his death.

strathearn.s: Strathearn is the valley of the River Earn in Perth and Kinross, Scotland, running from Loch Earn to the Firth of Tay. It held the Pictish royal centre of Forteviot and was long thought to be the heartland of Fortriu.

shota-rustaveli.s: Shota Rustaveli was a Georgian poet of the late 12th and early 13th centuries, author of the epic The Knight in the Panther's Skin. He is thought to have served at the court of Queen Tamar, possibly as treasurer, and tradition says he ended his life at the Georgian Monastery…

salaga.s: Salaga is a town in the Savannah Region of northern Ghana, in the kingdom of Gonja. From the 18th century it was a great market for kola nuts and slaves, linking the Ashanti Empire with Hausa traders from the north, and it was the leading slave market of the Volta region until…

statute-of-rhuddlan.s: The Statute of Rhuddlan, issued by Edward I at Rhuddlan Castle in March 1284, set out the government of the lands of Gwynedd and the Principality of Wales after the conquest of 1282–1283. It created shires such as Anglesey, Caernarfon, Merioneth and Flint, introduced English…

sumhuram.s: Sumhuram, at Khor Rori on the Dhofar coast of southern Oman, was a fortified port founded by the Kingdom of Hadramawt in the last centuries BCE to control the frankincense trade. Its inscriptions name it as a royal foundation, and finds of Indian and Mediterranean pottery show…

sayin.s: Sayin was the chief god of the ancient Kingdom of Hadramawt in southern Arabia, usually understood as a moon god. His main temple stood at Shabwa, the capital, where, according to Pliny the Elder, incense brought in from the producing districts was taxed with a tithe for the god.

shabwa.s: Shabwa was the capital of the ancient Kingdom of Hadramawt, on the edge of the desert in what is now southern Yemen. Caravans of frankincense had to pass through its walled town, where priests took a tithe for the god Sayin, according to Pliny the Elder.

sans-souci-palace.s: Sans-Souci was the royal palace of Henri I, king of Haiti, built at Milot between 1810 and 1813. It was the seat of his court, with gardens, a chapel and government buildings, and Christophe shot himself there in October 1820.

saint-nino.s: Saint Nino was a woman, traditionally from Cappadocia, who brought Christianity to the Kingdom of Iberia in eastern Georgia in the early 4th century. According to tradition her healing of Queen Nana and her prayers led King Mirian III to adopt Christianity.

simele-massacre.s: The Simele massacre was the killing of Assyrian villagers by the Iraqi army in northern Iraq in August 1933, centred on the town of Simele near Dohuk. It followed armed clashes with Assyrians seeking autonomy under their patriarch, and estimates of the dead range from several…

society-of-united-irishmen.s: The Society of United Irishmen was founded in Belfast in 1791 by Theobald Wolfe Tone and others, at first to seek parliamentary reform and Catholic emancipation. Inspired by the French Revolution and suppressed by the government, it became a secret revolutionary movement…

shalmaneser-v.s: Shalmaneser V was king of Assyria from 727 to 722 BCE, son and successor of Tiglath-Pileser III. When King Hoshea of Israel stopped paying tribute, he besieged Samaria, which fell around 722 BCE, ending the northern kingdom.

statuto-albertino.s: The Statuto Albertino was the constitution granted by King Charles Albert of Sardinia in March 1848. It created a parliament with an elected chamber and an appointed senate while leaving the king wide powers.

siloam-tunnel.s: The Siloam tunnel, also called Hezekiah's tunnel, is an ancient water channel about 533 metres long cut through the rock beneath the City of David in Jerusalem. It carries water from the Gihon spring to the Pool of Siloam and is usually dated to King Hezekiah's preparations…

san-francisco-de-campeche.s: San Francisco de Campeche is a port city on the Gulf of Mexico, capital of the Mexican state of Campeche. Founded by the Spanish in 1540 on the site of a Maya town, it became the main port of the Province of Yucatán and was repeatedly raided by pirates, which led to the…

senasammata-vikramabahu.s: Senasammata Vikramabahu was the first king of Kandy, ruling from about 1469 to 1511. Of the royal line of Gampola, he made the central highlands a separate kingdom, at first under the overlordship of the Kingdom of Kotte, and founded the city of Senkadagala, later known as Kandy.

sanatruq-i.s: Sanatruq I was ruler of Hatra in northern Mesopotamia in the mid-2nd century CE and the first to take the title 'king of the Arabs'. Under his dynasty the city, a Parthian vassal on the caravan routes, built its great temples and walls and withstood Roman sieges.

sarvastivada.s: Sarvastivada was one of the early schools of Buddhism, named after its doctrine that the dharmas, the elements of existence, exist in past, present and future. Strong in Kashmir, Gandhara and Central Asia from about the 2nd century BCE, it produced a large Abhidharma…

sarnath.s: Sarnath is a site near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, India, where the Buddha gave his first sermon in the deer park of Isipatana. It became a major monastic centre: Ashoka raised a pillar there whose lion capital is now India's national emblem, and the Dhamek Stupa dates largely…

surame.s: Surame is the site of the ruined first capital of the Kebbi kingdom, in Sokoto State, north-western Nigeria. It was built by Muhammadu Kanta in the early 16th century and enclosed by massive earthen and stone walls, and it remained the royal seat until the kings moved to…

siyavash.s: Siyavash is a legendary prince of Iranian tradition, son of King Kay Kavus, whose story is told in Ferdowsi's Shahnameh. Falsely accused by his stepmother Sudabeh, he proved his innocence by passing through fire, then fled to Turan, where he was unjustly killed by Afrasiab, a…

saketa.s: Saketa was an ancient city in northern India, a major centre of the kingdom of Kosala in the time of the Buddha, usually identified with Ayodhya or a site close to it on the Sarayu River. It lay on the trade route linking the Ganges valley with the north-west and was later…

sarayu-river.s: The Sarayu is a river of northern India, the name given in Hindu tradition to the stretch of the Ghaghara that flows past Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh. It is mentioned in the Rigveda and in the Ramayana, which places Rama's city on its banks, and pilgrims bathe in it at Ayodhya.

shravasti.s: Shravasti, in Pali Savatthi, was the capital of the kingdom of Kosala in northern India and one of the largest cities of the Buddha's time. The Buddha spent many rainy seasons at its Jetavana monastery, and Jain tradition makes it the birthplace of the tirthankara Sambhavanatha.

sanctuary-of-apollo-hylates.s: The Sanctuary of Apollo Hylates is an ancient religious site west of Kourion in south-western Cyprus, dedicated to Apollo as god of the woodland. Worship there began by the 8th century BCE and continued until late antiquity, and the surviving remains, including a partly…

spiti.s: Spiti is a high desert valley of the Spiti River in Himachal Pradesh, India, on the border with Tibet. Its people follow Tibetan Buddhism, and monasteries such as Tabo, founded in 996, and Key are among the oldest and best known in the Himalaya.

stok-palace.s: Stok Palace is a royal palace in the village of Stok, south of Leh in Ladakh, India, on the far side of the Indus. Built in the early 19th century, it became the residence of the Namgyal royal family after the Dogra conquest of Ladakh and remains their home.

shiva-simha-malla.s: Shiva Simha Malla was king of Kantipur (Kathmandu) in Nepal in the late 16th and early 17th centuries. Around 1597 he brought the city of Lalitpur (Patan), long dominated by its own nobles, under his rule and placed it under his son Hariharasimha, whose descendants later ruled…

southern-african-development-community.s: The Southern African Development Community (SADC) is a regional organisation of 16 states in southern Africa, founded in 1992 as successor to the Southern African Development Coordination Conference of 1980. With its secretariat in Gaborone, Botswana, it promotes economic…

scattery-island.s: Scattery Island is a small island in the Shannon estuary off Kilrush, County Clare, Ireland. St Senan founded a monastery there in the 6th century, and its round tower and churches survive.

samogitia.s: Samogitia is a historical region of western Lithuania, between the lower Neman and the Baltic coast. Its people resisted the Teutonic and Livonian orders for more than a century, and the land, which separated the orders' Prussian and Livonian territories, was repeatedly ceded…

samogitians.s: The Samogitians are a Baltic people of western Lithuania, living in the region of Samogitia. In the 13th century they defeated the Livonian Order at Saule in 1236 and at Durbe in 1260, and they long resisted conversion and conquest by the military orders.

silvio-pellico.s: Silvio Pellico was an Italian writer and patriot from Saluzzo in Piedmont. Arrested in Milan in 1820 for his links with the Carbonari, he spent ten years in Austrian prisons, mostly in the Spielberg fortress at Brno.

sanahin-monastery.s: Sanahin Monastery is a medieval Armenian monastery in the Lori region of northern Armenia, founded around 966 under King Ashot III and his queen Khosrovanuysh. It became a major centre of learning, with schools of illumination and calligraphy, and the burial place of the…

samshvilde.s: Samshvilde is a ruined fortified town in the Kvemo Kartli region of south-eastern Georgia, above the gorge of the Khrami river. It served as a seat of the Kiurikian kings of Lori in the late 10th and 11th centuries and later as a Georgian royal fortress.

savaii.s: Savaiʻi is the largest island of the Samoan archipelago and of the independent state of Samoa, a shield volcano whose last eruptions, from Mount Matavanu in 1905–1911, buried villages in lava. Its high chiefly titles were among the leading titles of Samoa.

shashe-river.s: The Shashe is a river of southern Africa that rises in north-eastern Botswana and forms part of the border between Botswana and Zimbabwe before joining the Limpopo. The confluence, where Botswana, Zimbabwe and South Africa meet, was the heart of the Mapungubwe kingdom in the…

sasak-people.s: The Sasak are the indigenous people of the island of Lombok in Indonesia, speaking an Austronesian language related to Balinese. Most are Muslim, and some, the Wetu Telu, combine Islam with older customs.

sandzak.s: Sandžak is a historical region on the border of Serbia and Montenegro, named after the Ottoman Sanjak of Novi Pazar. Its main towns include Novi Pazar, Pljevlja and Bijelo Polje, and much of its population is Bosniak Muslim.
