sil-muiredaig.s: The Síl Muiredaig were the ruling kindred of Connacht from the 8th century, descended from Muiredach Muillethan, a king of Connacht who died in 702. They included the Ua Conchobair, or O'Connor, kings, among them the high kings Toirdelbach and Ruaidrí Ua Conchobair, as well as…

srirangapatna.s: Srirangapatna, historically Seringapatam, is a town on an island in the Kaveri river near Mysore in southern India. It was the capital of the Wodeyar kings of Mysore from 1610 and then of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, who fortified it.

styria.s: Styria (Steiermark) is a mountainous region of south-eastern Austria, with its capital at Graz. It takes its name from the castle of Steyr, seat of the Otakar margraves who ruled it from 1056.

storting.s: The Storting is the parliament of Norway, established by the Eidsvoll Constitution of 17 May 1814. In November 1814 it accepted the union with Sweden and elected Charles XIII of Sweden as King of Norway while keeping the constitution.

saint-cloud.s: Saint-Cloud is a town on the Seine west of Paris, named after the Merovingian prince Clodoald, Saint Cloud, who founded a monastery there in the 6th century. Its château, built by the Orléans branch of the French royal family, was a residence of Napoleon, who seized power at…

seir-kieran.s: Seir Kieran, in Irish Saighir, is a site in County Offaly, Ireland, where Saint Ciarán the Elder founded one of Ireland's earliest monasteries in the 5th or 6th century. It was the chief church of Osraige and a burial place of its kings, until Aghaboe and later Kilkenny…

stip.s: Štip is a city in the eastern part of North Macedonia, on the Bregalnica River. In antiquity, as Astibos, it was one of the centres of the kingdom of Paeonia, and it later lay on the Roman road through the region.

struma.s: The Struma, called the Strymon in antiquity, is a river that rises near Sofia in Bulgaria and flows south about 415 km through Greece to the Aegean Sea near Amphipolis. Its valley was home to Paeonian and Thracian peoples, and its lower course was rich in timber and close to…

saint-germain-des-pres.s: Saint-Germain-des-Prés is a former Benedictine abbey in Paris, founded by King Childebert I in the 550s to house relics of Saint Vincent brought from Spain, and later named after Bishop Germanus of Paris, who was buried there. It was a burial place of Merovingian kings and a…

shrewsbury.s: Shrewsbury is the county town of Shropshire, England, on a loop of the River Severn near the Welsh border. Later Welsh tradition identified it with Pengwern, but the town is first recorded in the early 10th century as an English burh.

sakarya-river.s: The Sakarya, the ancient Sangarius, is the third-longest river of Turkey, flowing about 824 km from central Anatolia in a great arc to the Black Sea. The Phrygian capital Gordion stood on its banks.

sulla.s: Lucius Cornelius Sulla was a Roman general and statesman. After serving in the Jugurthine War and the Social War, he fought the First Mithridatic War against Mithridates VI, sacking Athens in 86 BCE.

selyf-ap-cynan.s: Selyf ap Cynan was a king of Powys in the early 7th century, known in Welsh tradition as Selyf Sarffgadau, 'the serpent of battles'. He was killed fighting Æthelfrith of Northumbria at the Battle of Chester around 615, where, according to Bede, the English also slaughtered…

southern-dobruja.s: Southern Dobruja is the southern part of the Dobruja region between the lower Danube and the Black Sea, today in north-eastern Bulgaria. Part of Bulgaria from 1878, it was taken by Romania after the Second Balkan War in 1913 and returned to Bulgaria by the Treaty of Craiova in…

sopocani-monastery.s: Sopoćani is a Serbian Orthodox monastery near Novi Pazar in south-western Serbia, founded by King Stefan Uroš I in the 1260s as his burial church. Its frescoes, painted around 1265, are among the finest works of 13th-century Byzantine-style painting.

stefan-milutin.s: Stefan Milutin was King of Serbia from 1282 to 1321, after his brother Stefan Dragutin gave up the throne. He conquered much of northern Macedonia from the Byzantine Empire, including Skopje, and later made peace by marrying the Byzantine princess Simonis.

stefan-decanski.s: Stefan Uroš III Dečanski was King of Serbia from 1321 to 1331, son of Stefan Milutin. He won a decisive victory over the Bulgarians at the Battle of Velbazhd in 1330, in which Tsar Michael Shishman was killed.

stefan-uros-i.s: Stefan Uroš I was King of Serbia from 1243 to 1276. He built up the kingdom's economy by inviting Saxon miners, who opened the silver mine at Brskovo, and by fostering trade with Ragusa.

stefan-uros-v.s: Stefan Uroš V was the second and last emperor of the Serbian Empire, ruling from 1355 to 1371 after his father Stefan Dušan. During his reign the great nobles became practically independent, and Vukašin Mrnjavčević was crowned king and co-ruler in 1365.

syrmia.s: Syrmia is a fertile region between the Danube and Sava rivers, today divided between Serbia and Croatia. Its Roman city of Sirmium was a major imperial centre, and in the Middle Ages it formed a county of the Kingdom of Hungary.

skouriotissa.s: Skouriotissa is a copper mine in north-western Cyprus, near the village of Katydata, and one of the oldest mining sites in the world still exploited. Its huge ancient slag heaps show copper working from the Bronze Age through Roman times, when it supplied the nearby city of…

solon.s: Solon was an Athenian statesman, lawgiver and poet. As archon in 594 BCE he cancelled the debts that had reduced poor Athenians to bondage, banned enslavement for debt and divided citizens into property classes for political office.

saint-kentigern.s: Saint Kentigern, also called Mungo, was a 6th-century British bishop in the kingdom of Strathclyde and is the patron saint of Glasgow. His 12th-century Life by Jocelin of Furness tells of his miracles and his dealings with King Rhydderch Hael, though much of it is legend.

selsey.s: Selsey is a seaside town on the Selsey peninsula in West Sussex, England. Wilfrid founded a monastery there in the 680s on land given by King Æthelwealh, and it became the seat of the bishops of the South Saxons until the see moved to Chichester in 1075.

stockholm.s: Stockholm is the capital and largest city of Sweden, built on islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea. First recorded in 1252 and associated with Birger Jarl, it grew as a trading port with strong German and Hanseatic links and became the seat of royal government.

siunia-dynasty.s: The Siunia were an ancient Armenian princely family that ruled the province of Syunik from antiquity into the Middle Ages. They were among the leading noble houses of Armenia under the Arsacid kings and later under Persian and Arab rule, and in the late 10th century a branch…

sapaudia.s: Sapaudia was a late Roman name for a region around Geneva and Lake Geneva, in present-day Switzerland and France. In 443 the Roman general Aetius resettled the surviving Burgundians there, and from this base they built a kingdom in the Rhône valley.

sirmium.s: Sirmium was a Roman city on the Sava river in Pannonia, today Sremska Mitrovica in Serbia. In the late 3rd and 4th centuries it was one of the imperial residences of the Tetrarchy and the birthplace of several emperors, among them Probus.

shavsheti.s: Shavsheti is a historic region of south-western Georgia, today the Şavşat district of Artvin Province in north-eastern Turkey. In the 9th and 10th centuries it was one of the lands of Tao-Klarjeti ruled by branches of the Bagratid dynasty, and it remained part of Georgia until…

somerled.s: Somerled was a Norse-Gaelic warlord of Argyll who married a daughter of Olaf I, king of Mann and the Isles. In 1156 he defeated his brother-in-law Godred in a sea battle and took the southern Hebrides, and by 1158 he held the whole kingdom for a time.

spoleto.s: Spoleto is a hill town in Umbria, central Italy, the Roman Spoletium. Taken by the Lombards around 570, it became the seat of a powerful duchy that cut the route between Rome and Ravenna, and Duke Guy of Spoleto was crowned emperor in 891.

sutri.s: Sutri is a town in Lazio, central Italy, on the Via Cassia north of Rome, with an Etruscan past and a rock-cut amphitheatre. In 728 the Lombard king Liutprand gave it to Pope Gregory II, the Donation of Sutri, regarded as the first territorial grant to the papacy.

svear.s: The Svear were a North Germanic people of the Lake Mälaren region and Uppland in eastern Sweden, the Suiones described by Tacitus. Their kings, centred at Uppsala, extended their rule over the Geats around 1000, and Sweden takes its name from them.

salote-tupou-iii.s: Sālote Tupou III was queen of Tonga from 1918 to 1965. She strengthened the monarchy while Tonga was a British protected state, promoted education and health, and settled divisions among the Methodist churches.

shirley-baker.s: Shirley Baker was an English-born Wesleyan missionary who became adviser to George Tupou I of Tonga. He helped draft the constitution of 1875 and served as premier from 1880.

shi-lang.s: Shi Lang was a Chinese admiral who served under Zheng Zhilong and Koxinga before finally defecting to the Qing in 1651. In 1683 he destroyed the Zheng fleet at the Battle of Penghu, leading to the surrender of the Kingdom of Tungning.

strandzha.s: Strandzha is a range of low, forested mountains in south-eastern Bulgaria and the European part of Turkey, near the Black Sea, rising to just over 1,000 metres. In antiquity it lay in Thrace, and in 1903 it was the scene of the Preobrazhenie Uprising against Ottoman rule,…

sion-switzerland.s: Sion is the capital of the Swiss canton of Valais, in the upper Rhône valley. It has been the seat of a bishop since the late 6th century, and from 999 its bishops also held the temporal lordship of the Valais as counts.

swabia.s: Swabia is a historic region of south-western Germany, taking its name from the Suebi and corresponding roughly to the land settled by the Alemanni between the upper Rhine, Lake Constance and the Lech. From the 10th century it formed the Duchy of Swabia, held by the…

south-caucasus.s: The South Caucasus, also called Transcaucasia, is the region south of the main ridge of the Greater Caucasus, between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea. Today it comprises Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan.

society-of-mary-marists.s: The Society of Mary, whose members are known as Marists, is a Catholic religious congregation founded in Lyon by Jean-Claude Colin and approved by Pope Gregory XVI in 1836. The same year it was entrusted with missions in the western Pacific.

sido.s: Sido was a Suebian king of the 1st century CE who, with his brother Vangio, overthrew their uncle Vannius in 50 CE and shared his kingdom north of the Danube. The brothers remained loyal clients of Rome.

senekerim-hovhannes-artsruni.s: Senekerim-Hovhannes Artsruni was the last king of Vaspurakan, the Armenian kingdom around Lake Van, ruling from 1003. Under pressure from Turkic raids, he ceded his kingdom to the Byzantine emperor Basil II in 1021 in exchange for estates around Sebasteia, the present-day…

svapnavasavadatta.s: Svapnavasavadatta, The Dream of Vasavadatta, is a Sanskrit play in six acts attributed to Bhasa. It tells how King Udayana of Vatsa, believing his queen Vasavadatta has died in a fire, is persuaded to marry a princess of Magadha for political reasons, while Vasavadatta lives…

sancho-ii-of-pamplona.s: Sancho II Garcés, called Abarca, was king of Pamplona from 970 to 994, son of García Sánchez I. Following his father's will, he gave the Rioja lands around Viguera to his brother Ramiro with the title of king.

sherborne.s: Sherborne is a market town in Dorset, south-west England. In 705 it became the seat of a West Saxon bishopric under the scholar Aldhelm, and its abbey church was the burial place of King Alfred's elder brothers Æthelbald and Æthelberht.

stjepan-radic.s: Stjepan Radić was a Croatian politician who founded the Croatian Peasant Party with his brother Antun in 1904 and led the Croat opposition to Serbian centralism in the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. Imprisoned in 1925, he then briefly joined the government.

sawant-singh.s: Sawant Singh was the ruler of Kishangarh in Rajasthan from 1748 and a poet who wrote devotional verse to Krishna under the name Nagari Das. Under his patronage the court painter Nihal Chand created the Kishangarh style of painting, famous for its idealised lovers.

sunassura.s: Sunassura was a king of Kizzuwatna in south-eastern Anatolia around 1400 BCE. A treaty with the Hittite king Tudhaliya I records that he left the side of the Mitanni Empire and accepted Hittite overlordship, with detailed terms on the borders and duties of the two kingdoms.

sostratus-of-cnidus.s: Sostratus of Cnidus was a Greek architect and courtier of the early 3rd century BCE, credited with building the Pharos, the great lighthouse of Alexandria, under the first Ptolemaic kings. The lighthouse, counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, bore a dedication…

sankosh-river.s: The Sankosh is a river that rises in northern Bhutan, where it is called the Puna Tsang Chu, and flows south through the Bhutanese town of Punakha into India, where it joins the Brahmaputra. In its lower course it forms part of the boundary between the states of Assam and West…

srimanta-sankardev.s: Sankardev was an Assamese saint, scholar, playwright and social reformer. He founded the Ekasarana Dharma, a Vaishnava devotional movement centred on Krishna that rejected caste barriers and idol worship, and established monasteries called sattras.

shimosa-province.s: Shimōsa was an old province of Japan, covering the north of present-day Chiba Prefecture and part of Ibaraki Prefecture, east of Edo. From 1455 the town of Koga in Shimōsa was the base of the Koga kubo, the eastern branch of the Ashikaga.

st-angelo-fort.s: St Angelo Fort is a coastal fort at Kannur, on the Malabar coast of Kerala, India, built by the first Portuguese viceroy, Francisco de Almeida, in 1505 with the permission of the Kolathiri ruler. The Dutch captured it in 1663 and rebuilt it, then sold it to the Arakkal ruler…

satyashodhak-samaj.s: The Satyashodhak Samaj, the Truth-seekers' Society, was a social reform movement founded in Pune in 1873 by Jyotirao Phule. It campaigned against caste discrimination and the religious and social dominance of Brahmins, and for the education of lower castes and women.

sekeletu.s: Sekeletu was king of the Kololo on the upper Zambezi from 1851, succeeding his father Sebetwane. He supported David Livingstone, providing porters for his journeys across Africa to Luanda and down the Zambezi to the Indian Ocean in 1853–1856.

sunjong-of-korea.s: Sunjong of Korea was the second and last emperor of the Korean Empire, reigning from 1907 to 1910 under the era name Yunghui. He came to the throne when Japan forced his father Gojong to abdicate after the Hague envoy affair, and his reign saw the disbanding of the Korean army…

saito-makoto.s: Saitō Makoto was a Japanese admiral and statesman who served as Governor-General of Korea from 1919 to 1927 and again from 1929 to 1931. Appointed after the March First Movement, he replaced open military rule with a policy of cultural rule that allowed limited Korean…

sven-hedin.s: Sven Hedin was a Swedish geographer and explorer who made several expeditions through Central Asia and Tibet between the 1890s and the 1930s. In 1900 he found the ruins of the ancient city of Loulan near Lop Nur, and he mapped large parts of the Taklamakan Desert and the…

shyaam-a-mbul-a-ngoong.s: Shyaam a Mbul a Ngoong is the founder of the Kuba kingdom in central Africa according to Bushong oral tradition, which places his reign around 1625. Tradition says he came from the west, unified the chiefdoms between the Kasai and Sankuru rivers and introduced new institutions…

sankuru-river.s: The Sankuru is a river of the central Democratic Republic of the Congo and the main tributary of the Kasai, which it joins after a course of about 1,200 kilometres. Together with the Kasai it bounded the heartland of the Kuba kingdom, and it gives its name to Sankuru province.

stavropol.s: Stavropol is a city in the North Caucasus of southern Russia and the capital of Stavropol Krai. It was founded in 1777 as a fortress on the Azov–Mozdok defensive line and became the centre of a governorate in the 19th century, a base for Russian expansion into the Caucasus.

samosata.s: Samosata was an ancient city on the right bank of the upper Euphrates, at modern Samsat in south-eastern Turkey. It was the centre of the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Kummuh and later the capital of the Hellenistic kingdom of Commagene, until Rome annexed the region in 72 CE.

shaivism.s: Shaivism is the Hindu tradition that worships Shiva as the supreme deity. Rooted in Vedic and later Puranic religion, it developed temple cults, ascetic orders and philosophical schools such as Kashmir Shaivism and Shaiva Siddhanta.

shiva.s: Shiva is one of the principal gods of Hinduism, worshipped as the destroyer and transformer within the triad with Brahma and Vishnu, and as the supreme being by Shaivas. He is depicted as an ascetic with a trident, the crescent moon and a third eye, as the cosmic dancer…

solsones.s: Solsonès is a comarca, or county, in the pre-Pyrenean interior of Catalonia, Spain, with its capital at Solsona, a cathedral city and seat of a bishopric. Largely rural and wooded, it is one of the most thinly populated comarques, living from farming, forestry and tourism.

shephelah.s: The Shephelah is the region of low, rolling hills between the coastal plain and the Judaean mountains in southern Israel; its name means lowland in Hebrew. Fertile and crossed by valleys leading inland, it was a contested borderland between the kingdom of Judah and the…

sikhs.s: The Sikhs are followers of Sikhism, a monotheistic religion founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab in the early 16th century and shaped by nine succeeding Gurus. Persecuted under later Mughal emperors, they were organised as the Khalsa from 1699 and in the 18th century formed…

samur-river.s: The Samur is a river of the eastern Caucasus, about 213 kilometres long, rising in southern Dagestan and flowing to the Caspian Sea. Its lower course forms part of the border between Russia and Azerbaijan.

subathu.s: Subathu is a hill cantonment in Solan district, Himachal Pradesh, India, near the former princely state of Kuthar. The British kept it after the Anglo-Nepalese War of 1814–16 and made it one of their first hill garrisons, recruiting Gorkha soldiers there.

samaveda.s: The Samaveda is one of the four Vedas, the sacred texts of Hinduism, consisting of verses drawn mostly from the Rigveda and set to melodies for chanting at soma sacrifices. Compiled in the later Vedic period, probably in the Kuru realm of northern India, it was the special…

south-manchuria-railway.s: The South Manchuria Railway Company was a Japanese semi-official company founded in 1906 to run the railway from Dairen and Port Arthur to Changchun, which Japan had taken from Russia in the Russo-Japanese War. Based at Dairen, it also ran coal mines such as Fushun, ports,…

sahure.s: Sahure was the second king of the 5th Dynasty of ancient Egypt. He built his pyramid at Abusir, whose causeway and temple reliefs show seagoing ships returning from an expedition, and the Palermo Stone records the first known Egyptian expedition to Punt in his reign, which…

shamash-resha-usur.s: Shamash-resha-usur was a governor of Suhu and Mari on the middle Euphrates in the first half of the 8th century BCE, nominally subject to Babylon. His Akkadian inscriptions describe canal building and fighting off raiders, and one stela records that he brought honeybees from…

shah-rukn-e-alam.s: Shah Rukn-e-Alam was a Sufi saint of the Suhrawardi order in Multan, grandson of Bahauddin Zakariya. His tomb, a great octagonal brick mausoleum with a dome, built in the early 14th century in the time of the Tughluq dynasty, is one of the finest monuments of the region and…

setthathirath.s: Setthathirath was king of Lan Xang from 1548 to 1571 and briefly also king of Lan Na from 1546. In 1560 he moved the Lao capital from Luang Prabang to Vientiane, where he built Pha That Luang and the Haw Phra Kaew for the Emerald Buddha, which he had brought from Chiang Mai.

souphanouvong.s: Souphanouvong was a Lao prince and communist leader, known as the Red Prince, half-brother of Souvanna Phouma. Trained as an engineer in France, he joined the Lao Issara in 1945 and then founded the Pathet Lao with Viet Minh backing, leading it through decades of civil war.

sonmiani.s: Sonmiani is a small coastal town in the Lasbela District of Balochistan, Pakistan, on a lagoon of the Arabian Sea north-west of Karachi. It was the main port of the state of Las Bela, trading with Sindh and the Gulf.

siege-of-kawagoe-castle.s: The Siege of Kawagoe Castle was a battle of Japan's Sengoku period in which the Later Hojo clan defended Kawagoe Castle in Musashi province against a large coalition of the Uesugi clans and the Ashikaga of Koga. In 1546 Hojo Ujiyasu relieved the castle with a surprise night…

siege-of-odawara-1590.s: The Siege of Odawara of 1590 was Toyotomi Hideyoshi's campaign against the Later Hojo clan, whose refusal to submit was the last obstacle to his unification of Japan. Hideyoshi surrounded Odawara Castle with a huge army and fleet and built a castle of his own nearby.

shenyang.s: Shenyang, known in Manchu as Mukden, is the capital of Liaoning province in north-eastern China. Nurhaci made it the capital of the Later Jin in 1625, and it remained the Manchu capital until the move to Beijing in 1644; its Mukden Palace survives.

srirangam.s: Srirangam is a river island and temple town between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers at Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu, India. It is the site of the Ranganathaswamy Temple, dedicated to Vishnu, one of the largest functioning Hindu temples in the world and the foremost shrine of…

spurius-cassius-vecellinus.s: Spurius Cassius Vecellinus was a Roman statesman of the early Republic, three times consul. In 493 BCE he concluded the treaty with the Latin League known as the Foedus Cassianum, which made Rome and the Latins equal allies for mutual defence.

suryavarman-i.s: Suryavarman I was king of the Khmer Empire from about 1006 to 1050. He won the throne after years of civil war and extended Khmer power westwards over the Chao Phraya basin, including Lopburi.

schanfigg.s: The Schanfigg is a valley in the Swiss canton of Graubünden, running from Chur up the Plessur river to the resort of Arosa. Settled by Romansh speakers and later also by German-speaking Walser colonists, it formed one of the court districts of the League of the Ten…

sabratha.s: Sabratha was an ancient city on the coast of western Libya, founded as a Phoenician trading post and later one of the three Emporia that gave Tripolitania its name. It prospered under Rome from the export of goods brought by Saharan caravans, and its theatre of the late 2nd…

seon-of-balhae.s: Seon was the tenth king of Balhae, ruling from 818 to 830. He subdued neighbouring Mohe tribes and expanded the kingdom to its greatest extent in Manchuria and northern Korea, and its organisation into five capitals and fifteen prefectures is associated with his reign.

shuofang-commandery.s: Shuofang was a Chinese commandery in the Ordos region on the great northern bend of the Yellow River, first established by Emperor Wu of Han in 127 BCE after campaigns against the Xiongnu. A frontier district between farmland and steppe, it was abandoned and restored several…

samuel-doe.s: Samuel Doe was a Liberian army master sergeant of Krahn origin who seized power in a coup in April 1980, killing President William Tolbert and ending more than a century of Americo-Liberian rule. He ruled as head of state and from 1986 as president, amid rigged elections and…

sais.s: Sais was an ancient Egyptian city in the western Nile Delta, centre of the cult of the goddess Neith. Libyan chiefs ruled from it in the 8th century BCE, and it was the seat of the Twenty-fourth Dynasty and the capital of the Twenty-sixth, or Saite, Dynasty, which ruled Egypt…

skradin.s: Skradin is a small town in Dalmatia, Croatia, on the Krka river near Šibenik. As Scardona it was a Liburnian settlement and, under Rome, the seat of the conventus, or judicial assembly, of the Liburnians.

statielli.s: The Statielli were a Ligurian people of southern Piedmont, around Aquae Statiellae, modern Acqui Terme. In 173 BCE the consul Marcus Popillius Laenas attacked them although they had not taken up arms and sold the survivors into slavery; the Senate condemned his conduct and…

swami-vivekananda.s: Swami Vivekananda was an Indian Hindu monk, a disciple of Ramakrishna, who did much to introduce Vedanta and yoga to the West. Before his celebrated address to the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893 he travelled across India as a wandering monk, hosted by…

seine.s: The Seine is a river of northern France, about 777 km long, which rises on the Langres plateau in Burgundy and flows through Troyes, Paris and Rouen to the English Channel at Le Havre. Its basin was home to Gallic peoples such as the Parisii and Senones, and as the artery of…

sacro-catino.s: The Sacro Catino is a green hexagonal dish kept in the treasury of San Lorenzo Cathedral in Genoa. Genoese crusaders brought it back from the capture of Caesarea in 1101, believing it to be carved from a single emerald, and it was later identified with the Holy Grail.

saint-helena.s: Saint Helena is a remote volcanic island in the South Atlantic, a British overseas territory. Discovered by the Portuguese in 1502, it was run by the English East India Company from 1659 as a supply station for ships.

swansea.s: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales at the mouth of the River Tawe. It grew around a castle built around 1106 by Henry de Beaumont, Earl of Warwick, as the centre of the lordship of Gower, whose lords gave it its first charter.

statutes-of-kilkenny.s: The Statutes of Kilkenny were laws passed by a parliament at Kilkenny in 1366 under Lionel of Antwerp, Duke of Clarence. Aimed at the English settlers of the Lordship of Ireland, they forbade marriage with the Irish, the use of the Irish language and Brehon law, and other…

samothrace.s: Samothrace is a Greek island in the northern Aegean Sea, dominated by the peak of Mount Fengari. In antiquity it was famed for the Sanctuary of the Great Gods and its mystery cult, where the statue known as the Winged Victory of Samothrace was found.

schenk-von-limpurg.s: The Schenks of Limpurg were a Swabian noble family who held the hereditary office of imperial cupbearer (Schenk) and from the 13th century ruled the Lordship of Limpurg near Schwäbisch Hall. Their lands lay along the Kocher valley, with residences at Gaildorf and Obersontheim.

st-rumbolds-cathedral.s: St. Rumbold's Cathedral is the Gothic cathedral of Mechelen in Belgium, seat of the Archbishop of Mechelen-Brussels. Built mainly between the 13th and 15th centuries and dedicated to the early medieval missionary Saint Rumbold, it is known for its massive west tower, nearly…

sancho-iv-of-castile.s: Sancho IV, called the Brave, was King of Castile and León from 1284 to 1295. The second son of Alfonso X, he rebelled against his father to secure the succession over the heirs of his elder brother.

sancho-iv-of-navarre.s: Sancho IV, known as Sancho of Peñalén, was King of Pamplona (Navarre) from 1054 to 1076. Son of García Sánchez III, he succeeded after his father's death at the Battle of Atapuerca.

shobak-castle.s: Shobak Castle is a crusader fortress in southern Jordan, built in 1115 by King Baldwin I of Jerusalem on a hill at Shobak and named Montréal, the 'royal mountain'. It was the first stronghold of the lordship of Oultrejordain, guarding the routes between Damascus, Egypt and the…

stephanie-of-milly.s: Stephanie of Milly was heiress of the lordship of Oultrejordain in the Kingdom of Jerusalem, daughter of Philip of Milly. Her marriages carried the lordship to Humphrey III of Toron, then to Miles of Plancy and finally, in 1176, to Raynald of Châtillon.

sidon-sea-castle.s: The Sidon Sea Castle is a crusader fortress built in 1228 on a small island off the harbour of Sidon in Lebanon, linked to the shore by a causeway. Erected during the crusade of Frederick II, it was held by the lords of Sidon and later by the Templars, and was dismantled by…

sigurd-the-crusader.s: Sigurd I, known as Sigurd the Crusader (Jorsalfar), was King of Norway from 1103 to 1130. Between 1107 and 1111 he led the Norwegian Crusade, sailing with a large fleet by way of England, Portugal and Sicily to the Holy Land, where he helped King Baldwin I of Jerusalem capture…

sigurd-eysteinsson.s: Sigurd Eysteinsson, called the Mighty, was according to the Orkneyinga saga the first Earl of Orkney, in the late 9th century. Brother of Rognvald Eysteinsson, Earl of Møre, he received the islands from him after Harald Fairhair granted them to Rognvald.

scaliger-tombs.s: The Scaliger Tombs, or Arche Scaligere, are a group of Gothic funerary monuments in Verona, beside the church of Santa Maria Antica, built for the della Scala lords of the city in the 14th century. The tombs of Cangrande I, Mastino II and Cansignorio, crowned with equestrian…

saint-jean-pied-de-port.s: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port is a small town in the French Basque Country, at the foot of the road over the Pyrenees to Roncesvalles. It was the chief town of Lower Navarre, the part of the Kingdom of Navarre north of the mountains, and is a major stop on the French Way of the…

saint-palais-pyrenees-atlantiques.s: Saint-Palais is a small town in the French Basque Country, in Lower Navarre. After Castile conquered southern Navarre in 1512, the Albret kings of Navarre made it the seat of their government and courts for the lands north of the Pyrenees, and it had a royal mint.

serra-di-vaglio.s: Serra di Vaglio is an archaeological site on a hilltop near Vaglio Basilicata, north-east of Potenza in southern Italy. Inhabited from the early Iron Age, it was a major indigenous centre in the 6th century BCE and later a fortified Lucanian town with stone walls of the 4th…

sar-e-pol-e-zahab.s: Sar-e Pol-e Zahab is a town in Kermanshah province in western Iran, on the ancient route from Mesopotamia through the Zagros mountains to the Iranian plateau. Rock reliefs in the gorge nearby include the victory relief of the Lullubi king Anubanini from the late third…

svarozic.s: Svarožič was a West Slavic god whose temple at Rethra, among the Lutici, is described by Thietmar of Merseburg around 1015 under the name Zuarasici. His name means 'son of Svarog', and he is often linked with fire or the sun.

stirling.s: Stirling is a city in central Scotland on the River Forth, at what was long the lowest crossing of the river before its estuary. Its strategic position made Stirling Castle a royal stronghold, and two decisive battles of the Wars of Scottish Independence were fought nearby, at…

spartacus.s: Spartacus was a Thracian gladiator who led the largest slave revolt against the Roman Republic, the Third Servile War of 73–71 BCE. Escaping from a gladiator school at Capua with about seventy companions, he gathered an army of tens of thousands and defeated several Roman…

sultan-kudarat.s: Sultan Kudarat was ruler of the Sultanate of Maguindanao on Mindanao from about 1619 to 1671. He united much of Mindanao, resisted Spanish expansion and survived the expedition of Governor Sebastián Hurtado de Corcuera, who took his fortress at Lamitan in 1637.

sebastian-hurtado-de-corcuera.s: Sebastián Hurtado de Corcuera was a Spanish soldier and governor-general of the Philippines from 1635 to 1644. He led campaigns against the Muslim sultanates of the south, capturing Sultan Kudarat's stronghold at Lamitan in 1637 and Jolo in 1638.

soqotri-language.s: Soqotri is a Modern South Arabian language spoken on Socotra and its neighbouring islands, part of Yemen. Like Mehri, it is a Semitic language distinct from Arabic that preserves features of the pre-Islamic languages of southern Arabia.

socotra.s: Socotra is an island in the Indian Ocean, off the Horn of Africa, belonging to Yemen. Its long isolation produced a unique flora, including the dragon's blood tree, and the archipelago became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2008.

sher-muhammad-khan-of-malerkotla.s: Sher Muhammad Khan was nawab of Malerkotla in the Punjab in the early 18th century, serving under the Mughal governor of Sirhind. In 1705 he protested against the execution of Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh, the young sons of Guru Gobind Singh, who were walled up alive at Sirhind.

sulayman-abu-layla-pasha.s: Sulayman Abu Layla Pasha was the first Mamluk governor of Baghdad, ruling from 1749 to 1762. A Georgian mamluk and son-in-law of the governor Ahmad Pasha, he was nicknamed Abu Layla ('father of the night') for his night raids against rebellious tribes.

siege-of-orleans.s: The Siege of Orléans was the English siege of the city of Orléans on the Loire from October 1428 to May 1429, during the Hundred Years' War. Its fall would have opened the south of France to the English and their Burgundian allies, but at the end of April 1429 Joan of Arc…

space-race.s: The Space Race was the competition between the United States and the Soviet Union, from the late 1950s to the mid-1970s, to achieve the first feats of spaceflight. The Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, in 1957 and the first person in space, Yuri…

sojourner-truth.s: Sojourner Truth was an American abolitionist and campaigner for women's rights, born into slavery in New York as Isabella Baumfree. She escaped with her infant daughter in 1826, a year before New York ended slavery, and later won a court case to recover her son, sold illegally…

susan-b-anthony.s: Susan B. Anthony was an American campaigner for women's rights and the abolition of slavery, and the leading organiser of the movement for women's suffrage. With Elizabeth Cady Stanton she founded the National Woman Suffrage Association in 1869.

second-intifada.s: The Second Intifada was the far bloodier Palestinian uprising that erupted in September 2000 after the collapse of final-status peace talks. Suicide bombings in Israeli cities and large Israeli military operations in Palestinian towns killed around a thousand Israelis and…

six-day-war.s: The Six-Day War was the war of 5-10 June 1967 in which Israel, striking first after weeks of crisis, defeated Egypt, Jordan and Syria and captured the Sinai Peninsula, Gaza, the West Bank with East Jerusalem, and the Golan Heights. Fought in less than a week, it tripled the…

saqqez.s: Saqqez is a city in Kurdistan province in western Iran, in the Zagros Mountains. The area is rich in Iron Age remains: the nearby site of Ziwiye produced a famous hoard of gold, silver and ivory objects of the 7th century BCE, and some scholars place the Mannaean capital…

santa-elena-province.s: Santa Elena is a province on the Pacific coast of Ecuador, covering the Santa Elena peninsula, the westernmost part of the country's coast. It was separated from Guayas province in 2007.

skardu.s: Skardu is the main town of Baltistan in Gilgit-Baltistan, northern Pakistan, in a broad valley of the Indus near its confluence with the Shigar river. It was the seat of the Maqpon rajas, whose Kharpocho fort overlooks the town.

steyr.s: Steyr is a town in Upper Austria at the confluence of the Enns and the Steyr rivers. Its castle was the seat of the Otakar counts, who gave their name to Styria.

scipio-africanus.s: Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who defeated Carthage in the Second Punic War. He captured Carthago Nova in 209 BCE, won at Ilipa in 206 BCE, driving the Carthaginians from Iberia, and in 204 BCE invaded Africa with Masinissa as ally.

siga.s: Siga was an ancient city near the mouth of the Tafna river in north-western Algeria, the capital of the Masaesylian king Syphax in the late 3rd century BCE. A Punic trading post, it later became a Roman town.

sophonisba.s: Sophonisba was a Carthaginian noblewoman, daughter of the general Hasdrubal Gisco, who was married to King Syphax of the Masaesyli to bind him to Carthage in the Second Punic War. After Syphax's capture in 203 BCE she married his rival Masinissa, but when Scipio demanded her…

syphax.s: Syphax was king of the Masaesyli of western Numidia in the late 3rd century BCE, ruling from Siga and later Cirta. Courted by both Rome and Carthage in the Second Punic War, he sided with Carthage after marrying Sophonisba.

songea.s: Songea is a town in southern Tanzania and the capital of Ruvuma Region. It takes its name from Songea Mbano, a Ngoni chief, and the surrounding highlands were settled in the nineteenth century by Ngoni groups who had migrated from southern Africa.

segobrigii.s: The Segobrigii were a Ligurian or Celto-Ligurian people living around the site of Marseille when Greek settlers from Phocaea arrived around 600 BCE. In the foundation legend of Massalia their king Nannus gave his daughter Gyptis in marriage to the Greek leader Protis and…

shimane-prefecture.s: Shimane Prefecture is a prefecture in the Chūgoku region of western Japan, on the Sea of Japan, with its capital at Matsue. It covers the old provinces of Izumo, Iwami and Oki, and includes the ancient shrine of Izumo Taisha and the Iwami Ginzan silver mine.

sala-hoysala-founder.s: Sala is the legendary founder of the Hoysala dynasty of southern India. According to the dynasty's tradition, a Jain teacher at Sosevur cried out to him to strike a tiger that threatened them, with the words hoy Sala, strike, Sala, and his victory gave the line its name.

santal-people.s: The Santal are one of the largest Adivasi peoples of South Asia, living mainly in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar in India, with communities in Bangladesh and Nepal. They speak Santali, a Munda language with its own Ol Chiki script.

sriram-chandra-bhanj-deo.s: Sriram Chandra Bhanj Deo was Maharaja of Mayurbhanj, a princely state in Odisha, from 1882 to 1912. A modernising ruler, he built schools, hospitals and a light railway, encouraged the study of local archaeology and leased the Gorumahisani iron-ore deposits to the Tata…

seille-moselle.s: The Seille is a river in Lorraine, north-eastern France, about 140 kilometres long, which joins the Moselle at Metz. Its upper valley held important salt springs at Vic and Marsal, a source of wealth for the bishops of Metz.

shusha.s: Shusha is a town on a mountain plateau in Karabakh, in Azerbaijan. Founded in the 1750s by Panah Ali Khan as the fortress and capital of the Karabakh Khanate, it became a centre of both Armenian and Azerbaijani culture under Russian rule.

suiyuan.s: Suiyuan was a province of the Republic of China in what is now central Inner Mongolia, with its capital at Guisui, modern Hohhot. Formed in 1928, it was largely occupied by Japan from 1937 and incorporated into Mengjiang.

sebinkarahisar.s: Şebinkarahisar is a town in Giresun province, north-eastern Turkey, below a fortress on a high rock. Known in Byzantine times as Koloneia, it was taken by the Mengujekids after 1071 and later passed to the Seljuks and the Ottomans.

selenga-river.s: The Selenga is a river of Mongolia and Russia, about 1,000 kilometres long, which rises in the mountains of northern Mongolia and flows north into Lake Baikal, providing about half of the lake's inflow. Its basin held important pastures and settlements of steppe peoples,…

sebastian-lerdo-de-tejada.s: Sebastián Lerdo de Tejada was a Mexican liberal lawyer and statesman who served as president from 1872 to 1876. A close minister of Benito Juárez during the war against the French intervention, he succeeded him on his death and wrote the Reform laws into the constitution in 1873.

semna.s: Semna was a group of Egyptian fortresses at the southern end of the Second Cataract of the Nile in Nubia, in present-day Sudan. Senusret III of the Twelfth Dynasty fixed the frontier there in the 19th century BCE with boundary stelae forbidding Nubians to pass north except to…

statuta-valachorum.s: The Statuta Valachorum, or Vlach Statute, was a charter issued by Emperor Ferdinand II in 1630 for the Orthodox Vlach and Serb settlers of the Croatian and Slavonian Military Frontier. It confirmed their privileges, including freedom from serfdom, their own elected judges and…

sinoe-county.s: Sinoe County is a county on the coast of south-eastern Liberia, with its capital at Greenville. It grew from Mississippi-in-Africa, a colony of freed African Americans founded at the mouth of the Sinoe river in 1835, which joined Liberia in 1842.

shikoku.s: Shikoku is the smallest of the four main islands of Japan, lying south of Honshu across the Inland Sea. It was historically divided into the four provinces of Awa, Sanuki, Iyo and Tosa, and is known for the pilgrimage route of eighty-eight Buddhist temples associated with Kukai.

salinar.s: Salinar was a culture of the north coast of Peru, flourishing from about 400 to 200 BCE in the Chicama and Moche valleys. It is known for fortified hilltop settlements, cemeteries and distinctive oxidised pottery, often with stirrup spouts and modelled figures, as well as…

st-panteleimon-monastery.s: St. Panteleimon Monastery, known as the Rossikon, is the Russian monastery of Mount Athos in northern Greece. Russian monks are recorded on Athos from the 11th century, and the present monastery on the coast was built mainly in the 19th century, when Russian support made it…

si-kefa.s: Si Kefa, in Shan tradition Hso Hkan Hpa, was a ruler of the Shan state of Mong Mao in the 14th century, on the upper Shweli river in today's Yunnan and Myanmar. He expanded Mong Mao into a powerful kingdom in the 1340s and 1350s, resisting Yuan armies sent from Yunnan and…

state-great-khural.s: The State Great Khural is the unicameral parliament of Mongolia, established under the democratic constitution of 1992. It has 126 members since 2024 and elects the prime minister and government, while the president is chosen by direct election.

san-jose-mogote.s: San José Mogote is an archaeological site in the Etla arm of the Valley of Oaxaca, Mexico, the largest and most important village of the valley between about 1500 and 500 BCE. It has some of the earliest public buildings and carved monuments in Mesoamerica, including a stone…

saint-patricks-day.s: Saint Patrick's Day, 17 March, is the feast of Saint Patrick, the patron saint of Ireland, celebrated by Irish communities around the world. On Montserrat, settled in the 17th century largely by Irish Catholics, it is a public holiday, and it also commemorates a planned…

soufriere-hills.s: The Soufrière Hills is an active volcano in the south of the Caribbean island of Montserrat. Dormant for centuries, it erupted in July 1995 and has remained intermittently active, with dome collapses and pyroclastic flows that killed 19 people in 1997 and buried the capital,…

sulu-archipelago.s: The Sulu Archipelago is a chain of islands in the south-western Philippines, stretching between Mindanao and Borneo and including Jolo, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi. From the 15th century it was the heart of the Sultanate of Sulu, a Muslim maritime state that traded and raided across…

shitthaung-temple.s: The Shitthaung Temple is a Buddhist temple at Mrauk U in Rakhine State, Myanmar, built by King Min Bin in 1535. Its name means 'shrine of the 80,000 images', and its fortress-like stone structure contains galleries lined with carved reliefs and Buddha images.

surendranagar-district.s: Surendranagar district is a district of Gujarat in western India, on the northern edge of the Kathiawar peninsula next to the Little Rann of Kutch. It was formed from many former princely states, among them Wadhwan, Limbdi and Dhrangadhra, which joined the United State of…

suq-al-shuyukh.s: Suq al-Shuyukh is a town on the Euphrates in Dhi Qar Governorate of southern Iraq, on the edge of the marshes. Its name means 'market of the sheikhs': it grew in the 18th century as the market town and base of the Sa'dun chiefs of the Muntafiq confederation, trading in dates,…

saw-hnit.s: Saw Hnit was the last king of the Pagan dynasty in Burma, placed on the throne in 1299 by the Myinsaing brothers after they executed his father Kyawswa. He ruled only the town of Pagan as a governor under the new rulers of central Burma until his death in 1325.

shillong.s: Shillong is a hill city in north-eastern India and the capital of Meghalaya. Founded as a British station in the 1860s on the lands of the Khasi state of Mylliem, it became the capital of Assam in 1874 and remained so until Meghalaya was formed in 1972.

syiem.s: Syiem is the title of the chief of a traditional Khasi state, or hima, in the hills of present-day Meghalaya, India. The Syiem was chosen from a royal clan by the heads of the leading clans, with succession passing through the female line, usually to a sister's son.

shivanasamudra.s: Shivanasamudra is an island town on the Kaveri River in Karnataka, India, beside waterfalls where the river drops from the Deccan plateau. In 1902 the state of Mysore opened a hydroelectric station there, one of the first in Asia, to supply the Kolar Gold Fields, and from 1905…

sappho.s: Sappho was a Greek lyric poet of Lesbos, active in Mytilene around 600 BCE. Her poems, mostly songs about love and longing addressed to women and composed for a circle of young women, were collected in nine books in antiquity but survive mainly in fragments.

sigeion.s: Sigeion was an ancient Greek town on a headland at the mouth of the Hellespont in the Troad, in north-western Anatolia. Its position on the route to the Black Sea made it a prize fought over by Mytilene and Athens around 600 BCE, until Periander of Corinth awarded it to Athens.

shina-language.s: Shina is a Dardic Indo-Aryan language spoken in Gilgit-Baltistan in northern Pakistan and in neighbouring parts of Kashmir and Kohistan. It is the main language of Gilgit and of several valleys, including parts of Nagar, and has many dialects.

sligo-bay.s: Sligo Bay is an inlet of the Atlantic Ocean on the north-west coast of Ireland, at the mouth of the Garavogue River below the town of Sligo. Its shores are dominated by the mountains of Knocknarea and Benbulben.

satna-district.s: Satna district is a district of Madhya Pradesh in central India, in the Baghelkhand region, with its headquarters at Satna. Formed after independence, it includes the lands of several former princely states, such as Nagod, Maihar, Kothi and Sohawal.

sulayhid-dynasty.s: The Sulayhid dynasty was an Isma'ili Shia dynasty that ruled much of Yemen from about 1047 to 1138 as allies of the Fatimid caliphs of Cairo. Founded by Ali ibn Muhammad al-Sulayhi in the highlands, it ruled from Sana'a and later Dhu Jibla.

shikanoshima.s: Shikanoshima is a small island at the mouth of Hakata Bay in Fukuoka, Japan, joined to the mainland by a sandbar. In 1784 a farmer found there a gold seal inscribed 'King of Na of Wa of Han', generally identified with the seal the Chinese emperor Guangwu granted to envoys from…

sugu-okamoto.s: Sugu-Okamoto is an archaeological site in Kasuga, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, regarded as the centre of the Yayoi-period state of Na. Excavations since 1899 have found jar burials with Chinese bronze mirrors, bronze weapons and glass ornaments, above all in a rich grave of the…

santa-ana-manila.s: Santa Ana is a district of the City of Manila in the Philippines, on the Pasig River. It occupies the site of the pre-colonial polity of Namayan, and excavations around its church have uncovered burials with Chinese trade ceramics.

shimajiri-ozato-castle.s: Shimajiri Ōzato Castle is a ruined gusuku, or stone castle, in Nanjō in the south of Okinawa Island, Japan. It is traditionally regarded as the seat of the kings of Nanzan, the southern of the three kingdoms that divided Okinawa in the 14th century, before Shō Hashi conquered…

siraj-ud-daulah.s: Siraj ud-Daulah was the last independent Nawab of Bengal, succeeding his grandfather Alivardi Khan in 1756. In June that year he captured Calcutta from the East India Company, and the deaths of British prisoners in the 'Black Hole' were used to justify reprisals.

sierra-del-nayar.s: The Sierra del Nayar is a rugged part of the Sierra Madre Occidental in the Mexican state of Nayarit and neighbouring areas. Home of the Cora and Huichol peoples, its deep canyons and high mesas made it a refuge from Spanish rule, and the Cora stronghold at the Mesa del Nayar…

sobhuza-i.s: Sobhuza I, also known as Somhlolo, was king of the Swazi from about 1815 to 1836. Driven north from the Pongola river by the Ndwandwe under Zwide, he settled his people in the heart of present-day Eswatini, absorbed local clans and avoided war with the Zulu through diplomacy…

soshangane.s: Soshangane was a Ndwandwe commander who fled north after Shaka's victory over Zwide around 1819 and founded the Gaza Empire in southern Mozambique. Conquering Tsonga and Ndau communities and raiding Portuguese settlements, he built a kingdom stretching from the Limpopo towards…

seri-menanti.s: Seri Menanti is a royal town near Kuala Pilah in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia, the seat of the state's ruler, the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, since the installation of Raja Melewar in the late 18th century. Its old wooden palace, completed in 1908 without the use of nails, is now a…

sayri-tupac.s: Sayri Túpac was ruler of the Neo-Inca State at Vilcabamba from 1545, after the death of his father Manco Inca. In 1558 he accepted Spanish terms, left Vilcabamba and received estates in the Yucay valley in exchange for giving up his claims.

sambre.s: The Sambre is a river of northern France and southern Belgium, flowing about 190 km north-east to join the Meuse at Namur. It is usually identified with the Sabis of Caesar's account, where the Nervii were defeated in 57 BCE.

scheldt.s: The Scheldt is a river of western Europe, flowing about 350 km from northern France through Belgium to the North Sea in the Netherlands. Its estuary gives access to the port of Antwerp, and for centuries its valley was a frontier and trade route between Gaul, Flanders and the…

southold-new-york.s: Southold is a town on the North Fork of Long Island in Suffolk County, New York, United States. Founded in 1640 by Puritans from New Haven led by the minister John Youngs, it belonged to the New Haven Colony and passed to New York after the English conquest of New Netherland…

sinking-of-the-rainbow-warrior.s: The sinking of the Rainbow Warrior was a bombing by agents of the French foreign intelligence service, the DGSE, in Auckland harbour on 10 July 1985. The Greenpeace ship was preparing to protest against French nuclear tests at Moruroa, and the photographer Fernando Pereira was…

syrian-coastal-mountain-range.s: The Syrian Coastal Mountain Range runs north to south parallel to the Mediterranean coast of Syria, between the coastal plain and the Orontes valley, rising to about 1,500 m. Known in the Middle Ages as the Jabal Bahra and later as the Jabal al-Nusayriyah or Jabal Ansariyah,…

salamiyah.s: Salamiyah is a town in central Syria, south-east of Hama on the edge of the steppe. In the 9th century it was the secret headquarters of the Ismaili leadership, from where Abdallah al-Mahdi Billah left for North Africa around 902–903 to found the Fatimid Caliphate.

saraychik.s: Saraychik was a medieval town on the Ural River in western Kazakhstan, upstream from modern Atyrau. It was a trading station of the Golden Horde on the route from the Volga to Khwarazm, was sacked by Timur in 1395, and later became the seat of the Nogai Horde, whose rulers…

stormont.s: Stormont is an estate in east Belfast containing Parliament Buildings, a neoclassical building opened in 1932 at the end of a long processional avenue. It was the seat of the Parliament of Northern Ireland until that parliament was suspended in 1972, and it has housed the…

salzwedel.s: Salzwedel is a town in the Altmark region of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, on the Jeetze river. A fortified settlement on a salt route by the early 12th century, it belonged to the margraves of Brandenburg, joined the Hanseatic League and prospered from trade.

stendal.s: Stendal is a town in the Altmark region of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Granted market rights by Albert the Bear around 1160, it became the leading town of the Altmark and a member of the Hanseatic League, and its brick Gothic churches and town gates survive.

sodasa.s: Sodasa was an Indo-Scythian ruler of Mathura in northern India, son of the great satrap Rajuvula, in the early 1st century CE. Inscriptions in Brahmi from his reign record donations including a temple and gateway to Vasudeva, among the earliest records of Vaishnavism, as well…

shaftesbury.s: Shaftesbury is a hilltop town in north Dorset, England. Founded as a fortified burh by Alfred the Great around 880, it grew around the wealthy nunnery of Shaftesbury Abbey, which Alfred established with his daughter Æthelgifu as abbess.

sarno-river.s: The Sarno is a short river in Campania, southern Italy, flowing from springs near the town of Sarno across a fertile plain to the Bay of Naples near Torre Annunziata. In antiquity Pompeii stood near its mouth and served as the port for towns of the valley such as Nuceria.

stabiae.s: Stabiae was an ancient town on the Bay of Naples, at modern Castellammare di Stabia. Destroyed by Sulla in 89 BCE during the Social War, it became a resort of large seaside villas, which were buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE.

sierra-madre-occidental.s: The Sierra Madre Occidental is a mountain range in north-western Mexico, running about 1,250 km from near the United States border to Jalisco. Cut by deep canyons such as the Copper Canyon, it is home to the Rarámuri (Tarahumara), Tepehuán and other peoples.

santiago-de-queretaro.s: Santiago de Querétaro is a city in central Mexico and the capital of the state of Querétaro. Founded in 1531 as an Otomi and Spanish town, it grew into a wealthy colonial centre whose historic core is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

saruj.s: Saruj, now Suruç in south-eastern Turkey, is an ancient town on the plain south-west of Edessa (Şanlıurfa), near the Syrian border. Known in antiquity as Batnae, it was a stage on routes across upper Mesopotamia.

starigard.s: Starigard, now Oldenburg in Holstein in northern Germany, was the main stronghold of the Wagrians, a West Slavic tribe of the Obotrite confederation. Its large ringwall fortress, built around the 8th century, enclosed princely halls and later churches, and it became the seat…

san-remo-conference.s: The San Remo conference was a meeting of the Allied Supreme Council held at Sanremo in Italy in April 1920. It assigned League of Nations mandates over former Ottoman territories, giving Britain Palestine and Mesopotamia and France Syria and Lebanon, and endorsed the Balfour…

seuthopolis.s: Seuthopolis was the capital founded around 320 BCE by the Odrysian king Seuthes III in the Kazanlak valley of central Bulgaria. Laid out on a regular Greek plan with a fortified royal residence and sanctuary, it was excavated in 1948–1954 before being flooded by the Koprinka…

south-hamgyong-province.s: South Hamgyong is a province on the north-east coast of North Korea, facing the Sea of Japan, with its capital at Hamhung. It was created in 1896 when Hamgyong Province was divided, and it combines a mountainous interior with a coastal plain around Hamhung and Hungnam.

scyles.s: Scyles was a Scythian king of the 5th century BCE whose story is told by Herodotus. The son of a Greek mother from Istria, he secretly adopted Greek dress and religion during his visits to the colony of Olbia on the Black Sea.

sungai-batu.s: Sungai Batu is an archaeological site in the Bujang Valley of Kedah, Malaysia, near the Merbok estuary. Excavations since 2009 have uncovered iron-smelting furnaces, a jetty and brick ritual structures dating at least from the early centuries CE, showing it was an early centre…

sneferu.s: Sneferu was the founder of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty, reigning in the 26th century BCE. He built the Bent Pyramid and the Red Pyramid at Dahshur and completed the pyramid at Meidum, developing the first true pyramids.

solimoes.s: Solimões is the name used in Brazil for the upper course of the Amazon from the Peruvian border to its confluence with the Rio Negro near Manaus. When Europeans first passed down it in 1542, its banks and islands were densely settled by peoples such as the Omagua.

samuel-fritz.s: Samuel Fritz was a Bohemian Jesuit missionary who worked among the Omagua and other peoples of the upper Amazon from 1686. He founded dozens of missions along the river, resisted Portuguese slave raids and claims to the region, and drew the first reasonably accurate map of the…

samuel-kirkland.s: Samuel Kirkland was an American Presbyterian missionary to the Oneida and other Iroquois nations. From 1766 he lived among the Oneida, converting many and helping keep them on the American side in the Revolutionary War.

sainte-marie-de-gannentaha.s: Sainte-Marie de Gannentaha was a French Jesuit mission and settlement built in 1656 on the shore of Onondaga Lake, near present-day Syracuse, New York, at the invitation of the Onondaga. About fifty French colonists and Jesuits lived there, but fearing an attack they secretly…

segontium.s: Segontium is a Roman auxiliary fort on the edge of Caernarfon in north-west Wales, founded around 77 CE after Agricola's conquest of the Ordovices. It controlled the Menai Strait and access to Anglesey and was garrisoned until the late 4th century, longer than most Roman forts…

snowdonia.s: Snowdonia, in Welsh Eryri, is a mountainous region of north-west Wales around Snowdon, at 1,085 metres the highest mountain in Wales. Its natural fortress sheltered the princes of Gwynedd, and it was the last area of Wales to fall to Edward I in 1282–1283.

santapollinare-nuovo.s: Sant'Apollinare Nuovo is a basilica in Ravenna built by Theodoric the Great in the early 6th century as his Arian palace church. Its nave mosaics show processions of martyrs and virgins, scenes from the life of Christ and a view of Theodoric's palace, from which figures of the…

shimazu-clan.s: The Shimazu were a samurai clan of southern Kyushu who ruled Satsuma from the late 12th century to 1871, one of the longest unbroken lordships in Japan. In the 1580s they nearly conquered all of Kyushu before submitting to Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1587.

suo-province.s: Suō Province was an old province of Japan in south-western Honshu, now the eastern part of Yamaguchi Prefecture. It was the home of the Ōuchi clan, whose town of Yamaguchi became a cultural centre in the 15th and 16th centuries.

shiroishi-miyagi.s: Shiroishi is a city in southern Miyagi Prefecture, Japan, which grew around Shiroishi Castle, held under the Tokugawa by the Katakura family, senior retainers of the Date lords of Sendai. In May 1868 delegates of the northern domains met there and formed the Ōuetsu Reppan…

seto-aichi.s: Seto is a city in Aichi Prefecture, Japan, east of Nagoya, which has been a leading centre of pottery for about a thousand years. Its glazed wares were so widespread that setomono, 'Seto things', became a general Japanese word for ceramics.

sumatra-treaty.s: The Sumatra Treaty was an agreement signed by Britain and the Netherlands in November 1871. Britain dropped its objection to Dutch expansion in northern Sumatra, which the treaty of 1824 had limited by recognising Aceh's independence, in return for equal trading rights there;…

syamsuddin-of-pasai.s: Syamsuddin of Pasai, also called Shams al-Din al-Sumatrani, was a Sufi scholar and the leading religious authority at the court of Iskandar Muda in Aceh. A follower of Hamzah Fansuri's mystical teaching of the unity of being, he wrote works in Malay and Arabic and also served…

second-macedonian-war.s: The Second Macedonian War was fought between Rome and Philip V of Macedon from 200 to 197 BCE. Rome, joined by Pergamon, Rhodes, the Aetolians and from 198 BCE the Achaean League, won it when Titus Quinctius Flamininus defeated Philip at Cynoscephalae in 197 BCE.

saturn-mythology.s: Saturn was an ancient Roman god of agriculture and wealth, identified with the Greek Kronos, whose festival, the Saturnalia, was held in December. His temple in the Roman Forum housed the state treasury.

sbeitla.s: Sbeitla is a town in central Tunisia, beside the ruins of Roman Sufetula. The ancient city flourished in the 2nd and 3rd centuries, and its forum has three well-preserved temples, probably dedicated to the Capitoline triad.

severan-dynasty.s: The Severan dynasty ruled the Roman Empire from 193 to 235. It was founded by Septimius Severus, a native of Leptis Magna in Africa, who won the civil wars after 193, and continued under his sons Caracalla and Geta and then Elagabalus and Severus Alexander, relatives of his…

siva-singha.s: Siva Singha was king of the Ahom kingdom of Assam from 1714 to 1744, the eldest son of Rudra Singha. Under the influence of a Shakta guru from Bengal he favoured Shaktism and built many temples and tanks around Sivasagar.

sivadol.s: The Sivadol is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva in Sivasagar, Assam, built in 1734 by Ambika, queen of the Ahom king Siva Singha, on the bank of the great Sivasagar tank. Its tall central spire is one of the landmarks of the town, and it stands in one compound with the…

sivasagar.s: Sivasagar, formerly Sibsagar, is a town in Upper Assam, India, and the headquarters of Sivasagar district. It grew around the great tank dug in the 1730s under Ahom royal patronage, and lies close to the former Ahom capitals of Garhgaon and Rangpur.

swargadeo.s: Swargadeo, "lord of heaven", was the title of the kings of the Ahom kingdom of Assam, rendering the Tai Ahom title Chao-pha. Ahom tradition traced the kings' descent from the founder Sukaphaa and through him from heavenly ancestors, and a ruler had to be of the royal line and…

somali-region.s: The Somali Region is the easternmost regional state of Ethiopia, inhabited mainly by ethnic Somalis and bordering Somalia, Djibouti and Kenya. Its capital is Jijiga.

sambida.s: Sambida was a leader of the Alans in Gaul in the fifth century. According to the Gallic Chronicle of 452, in 440 the Roman general Aetius granted deserted lands around Valence to the Alans under Sambida, part of a policy of settling barbarian groups to secure the Roman…

sarosius.s: Sarosius was a ruler of the Alans in the North Caucasus in the mid-sixth century, known from the Byzantine historian Menander Protector. A friend of the Byzantine Empire, he helped the first Avar envoys reach the court of Justinian I around 558, and he later received the…

serapio.s: Serapio was an Alemannic king of the fourth century, a nephew of Chnodomar. His father Mederichus, held as a hostage in Gaul, had been initiated into Greek mysteries and renamed his son, originally Agenarichus, after the god Serapis.

severus-alexander.s: Severus Alexander was Roman emperor from 222 to 235, the last ruler of the Severan dynasty, who came to the throne as a boy under the guidance of his mother Julia Mamaea. He fought an inconclusive war against the new Sasanian Empire, then moved to the Rhine to meet Germanic…

sant-joan-de-caselles.s: Sant Joan de Caselles is a Romanesque church in the parish of Canillo, Andorra, built in the eleventh and twelfth centuries. It has a single nave, a semicircular apse and a Lombard-style bell tower of three storeys, and preserves a sixteenth-century painted altarpiece and a…

sant-julia-de-loria.s: Sant Julià de Lòria is the southernmost of the seven parishes of Andorra and the name of its main town, on the Gran Valira near the Spanish border. It contains the main road crossing to Spain and the University of Andorra, and it was long the centre of Andorran tobacco growing…

salaman-and-absal.s: Salaman and Absal is an allegorical poem in Persian by Jami, one of the seven narrative poems of his Haft Awrang, dedicated to the Aq Qoyunlu sultan Ya'qub. It tells of a prince, Salaman, born without a mother, and his love for his nurse Absal, a story read as an allegory of…

sultan-khalil.s: Sultan Khalil was the eldest son of the Aq Qoyunlu ruler Uzun Hasan and briefly his successor in 1478. Formerly governor of Fars, he took power on his father's death, but within months he was defeated and killed by his brother Ya'qub, who then ruled until 1490.

saenz-pena-law.s: The Sáenz Peña Law was the Argentine electoral law of 1912, promoted by President Roque Sáenz Peña, which established secret, universal and compulsory male suffrage for citizens and representation for minorities. It ended the electoral fraud of the conservative order and…

santiago-derqui.s: Santiago Derqui was an Argentine lawyer and politician who served as president of the Argentine Confederation from 1860 to 1861. His attempt to reconcile Buenos Aires with the other provinces failed, and after Bartolomé Mitre's victory at the Battle of Pavón he resigned,…

socrates.s: Socrates was an Athenian philosopher who wrote nothing himself but questioned his fellow citizens about justice, virtue and knowledge, a method of inquiry known through the dialogues of his pupil Plato and the writings of Xenophon. In 399 BCE he was tried for impiety and…

semmering-railway.s: The Semmering Railway is a mountain railway in Austria crossing the Semmering Pass between Gloggnitz and Mürzzuschlag, built between 1848 and 1854 to designs by Carl von Ghega. With its tunnels, viaducts and steep curves it was the first true mountain railway in Europe and…

sylvester-patent.s: The Sylvester Patent was a set of decrees issued by Emperor Franz Joseph I on New Year's Eve, 31 December 1851, which revoked the Austrian constitution of March 1849 while keeping the abolition of peasant servitude and equality before the law. It opened the period of…

sixtus-affair.s: The Sixtus Affair was the secret attempt by Emperor Karl I of Austria-Hungary in 1917 to make a separate peace with France, using his brother-in-law Prince Sixtus of Bourbon-Parma, an officer in the Belgian army, as intermediary. When the French prime minister Georges…

strategikon-of-maurice.s: The Strategikon is a Byzantine military manual written around 600 and traditionally attributed to Emperor Maurice. In twelve books it covers the organisation, training and tactics of an army based on mounted archers, and it describes the fighting methods of the empire's…

samo.s: Samo was a Frankish merchant who, according to the Chronicle of Fredegar, led the Slavs of Central Europe in a revolt against the Avars around 623 and was then chosen as their king, ruling for some thirty-five years. In about 631 he defeated the Frankish king Dagobert I at…

savaria.s: Savaria was a Roman city in Pannonia, founded as a colony under Emperor Claudius around the middle of the first century CE on the Amber Road, on the site of modern Szombathely in western Hungary. It later became the capital of the province of Pannonia Prima and was the…

siyam-nikaya.s: The Siyam Nikaya is the largest order of Buddhist monks in Sri Lanka, founded in 1753 when King Kirti Sri Rajasinha of Kandy invited monks from Ayutthaya, led by Upali Thera, to restore the higher ordination, which had lapsed on the island. Its main chapters are based at…

suriyothai.s: Suriyothai was a queen of Ayutthaya, wife of King Maha Chakkraphat. According to the Thai chronicles, during the Burmese siege of 1548 she rode into battle on an elephant disguised as a warrior and was killed defending her husband.

sepphoris.s: Sepphoris is an ancient town in Lower Galilee, north-west of Nazareth, with springs that made it an important stopping point. It was a leading Jewish and Roman city in antiquity, later the Crusader village of La Sephorie and the Arab village of Saffuriya.

seosan.s: Seosan is a city in South Chungcheong Province, South Korea, on the Taean peninsula facing the Yellow Sea. Near it is the Rock-carved Buddha Triad of Seosan, carved into a cliff in the late Baekje period, around the early seventh century, and known for the warm smiles of its…

seven-branched-sword.s: The Seven-Branched Sword is an iron sword with six side branches kept at Isonokami Shrine in Japan. Its gold-inlaid inscription, usually dated to 369, records that it was made for a ruler of Wa and is generally read as a gift from a king of Baekje.

shah-nimatullah-wali.s: Shah Nimatullah Wali was a Persian Sufi master and poet, born in Aleppo, who settled at Mahan near Kerman in Iran, where his shrine stands. He founded the Nimatullahi order, one of the major Sufi orders of Iran.

saint-helier.s: Saint Helier is the capital and largest town of Jersey, on St Aubin's Bay on the island's south coast. It is named after Helier, a sixth-century hermit venerated as the island's patron saint.

states-of-jersey.s: The States of Jersey is the legislature of the island, which grew from around 1500 out of meetings of the jurats, the rectors of the twelve parishes and the parish constables. An Order in Council of 1771 confirmed that laws were to be made by the States rather than by the…

subiya-people.s: The Subiya are a Bantu people living along the Chobe and Zambezi rivers where Zambia, Namibia and Botswana meet. In the nineteenth century they were subject to the Lozi kingdom of Barotseland and paid it tribute, though their own chiefs, centred in the eastern Caprivi, kept a…

shah-muhammad-sagir.s: Shah Muhammad Sagir was a Bengali poet, probably of the reign of Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah around 1400, and one of the earliest known Muslim poets of the Bengali language. His Yusuf-Zulekha retold in Bengali verse the Persian romance of Joseph and Potiphar's wife, opening the long…

sanatana-goswami.s: Sanatana Goswami was a theologian of Gaudiya Vaishnavism, one of the six Goswamis of Vrindavan and elder brother of Rupa Goswami. He served Sultan Alauddin Husain Shah of Bengal as a minister, was imprisoned when he tried to resign, and escaped to join Chaitanya.

shamsuddin-muhammad-shah-ghazi.s: Shamsuddin Muhammad Shah Ghazi, born Muhammad Khan Sur, was the governor of Bengal for the Sur Empire who declared independence after the death of Islam Shah Suri in 1554. He founded a short-lived Afghan line of Bengal sultans.

sikandar-shah-bengal.s: Sikandar Shah was sultan of Bengal from 1358 to about 1390, son of Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah. He withstood a second invasion by Firuz Shah Tughluq of Delhi in 1359, which ended in a negotiated peace confirming Bengal's independence.

sri-krishna-vijaya.s: The Sri Krishna Vijaya is a Bengali narrative poem on the life of Krishna by Maladhar Basu, based on the Bhagavata Purana and composed between 1473 and 1480 under Sultan Rukunuddin Barbak Shah of Bengal. It is the earliest Bengali work that can be dated securely, and it was…

sur-empire.s: The Sur Empire was an Afghan state founded in northern India by Sher Shah Suri, who drove the Mughal emperor Humayun out of India in 1540. Sher Shah reformed administration, revenue and coinage, issuing the silver rupiya, and built the Grand Trunk Road.

saraswati.s: Saraswati is the Hindu goddess of knowledge, learning, music and the arts, also identified in the Rigveda with a sacred river. She is usually shown dressed in white, seated on a lotus or accompanied by a swan and playing the veena.

sikandar-adil-shah.s: Sikandar Adil Shah was the last sultan of Bijapur, placed on the throne as a small child in 1672. His reign was marked by feuding among the nobility, the loss of southern conquests to the Marathas and local commanders, and growing Mughal pressure.

saumacus.s: Saumacus was a Scythian who led a revolt in the Bosporan Kingdom around 108 BCE, in which the last Spartocid king, Paerisades V, was killed. The rising is known from an inscription honouring Diophantus, the general of Mithridates VI of Pontus, who crushed it, captured Saumacus…

sauromates-ii.s: Tiberius Julius Sauromates II was king of the Bosporan Kingdom from about 174 to 210 CE, ruling as a client of Rome. Inscriptions credit him with victories over the Scythians, Siraces and Tauri and with making the sea safe for shipping.

spartocus-iii.s: Spartocus III was king of the Bosporan Kingdom in the eastern Crimea and the Taman peninsula from about 304 to 284 BCE, succeeding his father Eumelus. He maintained close relations with Athens, which honoured him with a decree granting him citizenship and statues.

satyrus-ii.s: Satyrus II was the eldest son of Paerisades I and briefly king of the Bosporan Kingdom in 310/309 BCE. Challenged by his brother Eumelus, who was supported by the native king Aripharnes, he defeated them at the river Thatis but was mortally wounded while besieging their fortress.

satyendranath-tagore.s: Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to join the Indian Civil Service, selected in 1863 and serving mainly in the Bombay Presidency until 1897. An elder brother of the poet Rabindranath Tagore, he was also a writer, translator and composer and a member of the Brahmo Samaj.

sharif-ali.s: Sharif Ali was the third sultan of Brunei in the traditional list, reigning in the early fifteenth century. Brunei tradition holds that he was a descendant of the Prophet Muhammad who came from Ta'if in Arabia, married into the royal family and succeeded his father-in-law.

syair-awang-semaun.s: The Syair Awang Semaun is a traditional epic poem of Brunei recounting the deeds of the legendary hero Awang Semaun and his brothers, among them Awang Alak Betatar, remembered as the first sultan, Muhammad Shah. Preserved in oral tradition and later manuscripts, it tells of…

shams-al-dawla.s: Shams al-Dawla was the Buyid ruler of Hamadan and the surrounding Jibal from 997 to about 1021, a son of Fakhr al-Dawla. He governed at first alongside his brother Majd al-Dawla at Ray, then independently, and fought the Kurdish Hasanwayhids.

samsam-al-dawla.s: Samsam al-Dawla was a Buyid emir, a son of Adud al-Dawla, who succeeded his father in Iraq in 983. His brother Sharaf al-Dawla took Baghdad from him in 987 and had him imprisoned and partly blinded.

shabankara.s: The Shabankara were a Kurdish tribal confederation of southern Iran that rose to power in Fars in the eleventh century. Their chief Fadluya overthrew and killed the last Buyid prince of Fars in 1062.

story-of-wenamun.s: The Story of Wenamun is an ancient Egyptian text, preserved on a papyrus found at el-Hiba and now in Moscow, describing the journey of Wenamun, an official of the temple of Amun at Karnak, to Byblos to buy cedar for the god's sacred barque. Set at the end of the Twentieth…

sixth-dynasty-of-egypt.s: The Sixth Dynasty of Egypt was the last major dynasty of the Old Kingdom, with kings including Teti, Pepi I, Merenre and Pepi II, whose reign was among the longest in history. Its officials led expeditions to Nubia and the Levant, and objects of Pepi I were dedicated in the…

sanchuniathon.s: Sanchuniathon was a Phoenician author whom Philo of Byblos claimed as the source of his Phoenician History, dating him to before the Trojan War. No original work survives, and he is known only through Philo's Greek version as quoted by Eusebius.

selymbria.s: Selymbria was an ancient Greek city on the northern shore of the Sea of Marmara, founded by colonists from Megara in the seventh century BCE, and like its neighbour Byzantium it guarded the sea route to the Black Sea. It was a member of the Delian League in the fifth century BCE.

saqaliba.s: Saqaliba, 'Slavs', was the Arabic term for slaves and freedmen of European origin in the medieval Islamic world, many taken from Slavic lands. In al-Andalus they served as palace officials and soldiers of the Umayyad caliphs of Córdoba, and some rose to high command.

supreme-court-of-canada.s: The Supreme Court of Canada is the highest court of Canada, established in 1875 and sitting in Ottawa. Until 1949 its decisions could be appealed to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London; since then it has been the final court of appeal.

salomon-gessner.s: Salomon Gessner was a Swiss poet, painter and engraver from Zürich. His prose Idylls of 1756, pastoral scenes of innocent shepherds, were translated into many languages and made him one of the most widely read German-language authors of his day.

second-helvetic-confession.s: The Second Helvetic Confession is a Reformed statement of faith written by Heinrich Bullinger and published in 1566, after it was adopted by the Elector Palatine Frederick III. Accepted by the Swiss Reformed churches and by Reformed churches in Hungary, Poland, Scotland and…

second-peace-of-kappel.s: The Second Peace of Kappel, concluded in November 1531 after Zürich's defeat at the Battle of Kappel, ended the second religious war of the Old Swiss Confederacy. It left each canton free to choose its religion but protected Catholic worship in the common lordships, halting…

sihl.s: The Sihl is a river in central Switzerland, about 73 kilometres long, which rises in the canton of Schwyz, flows through the Sihlsee reservoir and runs north to join the Limmat in the city of Zürich. In 1443, during the Old Zürich War, the confederates defeated the Zürich…

stafa-affair.s: The Stäfa affair was a dispute of 1794–1795 in which villagers of Stäfa on Lake Zürich drew up a memorial demanding the restoration of old rural liberties and equal economic rights with the city of Zürich. The city government treated it as sedition, occupied Stäfa with troops…

stafa.s: Stäfa is a municipality on the north-eastern shore of Lake Zürich in the canton of Zürich, Switzerland. In the eighteenth century it was a prosperous village of vine-growers and textile workers, and in 1794–1795 it was the centre of the Stäfa affair, when its petition for…

saint-catherines-monastery.s: Saint Catherine's Monastery is an Eastern Orthodox monastery at the foot of Mount Sinai in Egypt, built by order of the Byzantine emperor Justinian I in the mid-sixth century. It is among the oldest continuously inhabited Christian monasteries and holds one of the great…

segobriga.s: Segobriga was a Celtiberian and then Roman town on a hill near Saelices in the province of Cuenca, Spain. It became a Roman municipium under Augustus and grew rich from the mining of lapis specularis, a transparent gypsum used as window glass.

strattis-of-chios.s: Strattis was the tyrant of Chios under Persian rule. Herodotus lists him among the Ionian tyrants who guarded the bridge over the Danube during Darius I's Scythian campaign around 513 BCE and kept it intact for the king's return.

shora-nogmov.s: Shora Nogmov was a Kabardian scholar, poet and officer in Russian service who laid foundations for the written study of the Kabardian language. He compiled a grammar and dictionary of Kabardian and wrote a History of the Adyghe People based on oral traditions and songs,…

shapsugs.s: The Shapsugs are a Circassian people of the north-western Caucasus who lived along the Black Sea coast and the northern slopes of the mountains between Anapa and the Sochi area. Among the largest western Circassian communities, they broke the power of their nobles in the late…
