svans.s: The Svans are a people of Svaneti, a high valley region of north-western Georgia in the Greater Caucasus, counted as a subgroup of the Georgians. They speak Svan, a Kartvelian language distinct from Georgian.

surb-karapet-monastery.s: Surb Karapet, the Monastery of the Holy Forerunner, stood near Muş in the historic Armenian district of Taron. Tradition holds that Gregory the Illuminator founded it in the 4th century to house relics of John the Baptist, and it became one of the most revered pilgrimage sites…

spree.s: The Spree is a river in eastern Germany, about 400 kilometres long, rising in Saxony near the Czech border and flowing through Lusatia and the Spreewald marshes to Berlin, where it joins the Havel at Spandau. The medieval twin towns of Berlin and Cölln grew up on its banks,…

st-emmerams-abbey.s: St Emmeram's Abbey in Regensburg, Bavaria, was a Benedictine monastery founded in the 8th century over the grave of the martyred bishop Emmeram. For a thousand years it was a leading centre of learning and book production.

sviatopolk-i-of-kiev.s: Sviatopolk I, called the Accursed, was a son of Vladimir the Great who ruled Turov in his father's lifetime. After Vladimir's death in 1015 he seized Kiev, and the chronicles blame him for the murder of his brothers Boris and Gleb.

sviatopolk-ii-of-kiev.s: Sviatopolk II Iziaslavich was Grand Prince of Kiev from 1093 until his death. He took part in the Lyubech Congress of 1097, where the Rus' princes agreed to hold their fathers' lands, and joined Vladimir Monomakh in campaigns against the Cumans.

strait-of-otranto.s: The Strait of Otranto connects the Adriatic Sea with the Ionian Sea, separating the heel of Italy at Otranto from Albania. About 72 kilometres wide, it has long been a crossing point between Italy and the Balkans and a strategic choke point; in the First World War the Allies…

st-georges-cathedral-yuryev-polsky.s: St George's Cathedral in Yuryev-Polsky, Russia, was built between 1230 and 1234 by Prince Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich, the last great white-stone church of Vladimir-Suzdal before the Mongol invasion. Its walls were covered with carved reliefs of saints, beasts and plants.

satiru-uprising.s: The Satiru uprising was a Mahdist rising in 1906 at the village of Satiru near Sokoto, in the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria. The rebels destroyed a British-led company in February, but in March a larger force, supported by the Sultan of Sokoto, crushed them, killing many…

scorpion-macehead.s: The Scorpion Macehead is a decorated limestone ceremonial mace head found in the Main Deposit of the temple at Hierakonpolis in 1897–1898. It shows a king wearing the white crown of Upper Egypt, identified by a scorpion sign, performing a ritual with a hoe, perhaps opening a…

saco-maine.s: Saco is a city in southern Maine, United States, on the Saco River near its mouth, opposite Biddeford. English fishermen and settlers arrived in the 1620s and 1630s, and it formed part of Sir Ferdinando Gorges's Province of Maine before Massachusetts absorbed the region in the…

st-marys-city-maryland.s: St. Mary's City is the site of the first English settlement in Maryland, founded in March 1634 by colonists who arrived on the ships Ark and Dove under Leonard Calvert, near the mouth of the Potomac. It was the colony's capital until 1694, when the government moved to…

stamp-act-1765.s: The Stamp Act of 1765 was a British law requiring printed materials in the American colonies, such as legal documents, newspapers and playing cards, to carry a tax stamp. It was the first direct tax imposed by Parliament on the colonies and provoked riots, boycotts and the…

stamp-act-congress.s: The Stamp Act Congress met in New York City in October 1765, with delegates from nine British American colonies, to oppose the Stamp Act. It adopted a Declaration of Rights and Grievances asserting that only the colonists' own assemblies could tax them, and sent petitions to…

scotch-irish-americans.s: The Scotch-Irish, or Scots-Irish, are Americans descended from Presbyterian settlers from Ulster, most of them of Scottish origin, who emigrated in large numbers in the 18th century. Many landed at Philadelphia and moved into the backcountry of Pennsylvania, Virginia and the…

shackamaxon.s: Shackamaxon was a Lenape settlement on the Delaware River, in what is now the Fishtown district of Philadelphia. According to tradition, William Penn made a treaty of friendship with the Lenape leader Tamanend there under a great elm in 1682 or 1683.

south-australian-colonisation-commission.s: The South Australian Colonisation Commission was a British body set up under the South Australia Act of 1834 to organise the new colony on Edward Gibbon Wakefield's principles. It sold land in advance and used the proceeds to fund the passage of free emigrants, while a…

south-carolina-lowcountry.s: The Lowcountry is the coastal plain of South Carolina, with its tidal rivers, marshes and Sea Islands, centred on Charleston. In the colonial period enslaved Africans grew rice and indigo on its plantations, making its planters among the wealthiest people in British America.

stono-rebellion.s: The Stono Rebellion was a revolt of enslaved Africans that began on 9 September 1739 near the Stono River in South Carolina. Led by a man named Jemmy, many of the rebels came from Kongo; they killed about 20 colonists and marched towards Spanish Florida, which offered freedom,…

south-saskatchewan-river.s: The South Saskatchewan River is formed in southern Alberta by the meeting of the Bow and Oldman rivers and flows through Saskatchewan, past Saskatoon, to join the North Saskatchewan east of Prince Albert. Métis families settled river lots along its banks around Batoche and St.…

schleswig-holstein.s: Schleswig-Holstein is the northernmost state of Germany, between the North Sea and the Baltic, with its capital at Kiel. It takes its name from the duchies of Schleswig and Holstein, ruled by the Danish king for centuries, whose status provoked the Schleswig Wars of 1848–1851…

shanghai-french-concession.s: The Shanghai French Concession was a foreign concession in Shanghai under French administration from 1849 to 1943. Outside Chinese jurisdiction, it became a refuge for political activists: the Korean Provisional Government was founded there in 1919, and the Chinese Communist…

sittanavasal.s: Sittanavasal is a village in Pudukkottai district, Tamil Nadu, India, known for its rock-cut Jain cave temple, the Arivar Koil. The cave holds some of the finest surviving early Indian murals, painted in the 9th century under the Pandyas, showing a lotus pond with fish, birds,…

shashanka.s: Shashanka was a king of Gauda in Bengal in the late 6th and early 7th centuries, often described as the first ruler to unite much of Bengal. From his capital Karnasuvarna he extended his power into Magadha and Odisha, and around 606 he killed Rajyavardhana of Thanesar, making…

sharaf-al-din-qaraqush.s: Sharaf al-Din Qaraqush was an Armenian-born mamluk who carved out a domain in Tripolitania and southern Ifriqiya. A follower of Taqi al-Din, nephew of Saladin, he led Turkish and Ghuzz troops west from Egypt around 1172, seized Tripoli, Gabès and other towns, and allied with…

sukhra.s: Sukhra, also called Zarmihr, was a Sasanian nobleman of the House of Karen who dominated the Iranian court in the 480s. After King Peroz I was killed by the Hephthalites in 484, he restored order, raised Peroz's brother Balash and then Kavad I to the throne and governed as…

south-persia-rifles.s: The South Persia Rifles was a force of Iranian troops under British officers raised in southern Iran in 1916, during the First World War, by Sir Percy Sykes. Intended to counter German agents and pro-German tribes, it fought the Qashqai under Solat al-Dowleh among others.

samsi.s: Samsi was a queen of the Arabs in the 8th century BCE, known from the inscriptions of Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria. She succeeded Queen Zabibe, broke her oath of loyalty and sided with Damascus, but Tiglath-Pileser defeated her around 733 BCE, taking captives and great herds…

sozh-river.s: The Sozh is a river of eastern Europe, about 650 kilometres long, a left tributary of the Dnieper. Rising near Smolensk in Russia, it flows south through eastern Belarus past Krychaw and Gomel to join the Dnieper near the Ukrainian border.

sukkur.s: Sukkur is a city on the right bank of the Indus in Sindh province, Pakistan, opposite Rohri. Nearby lay Aror, capital of medieval Sindh.

santo-nino-de-cebu.s: The Santo Niño de Cebú is a small wooden statue of the Christ Child given by Ferdinand Magellan's expedition to the wife of Rajah Humabon of Cebu at her baptism in 1521. Found intact in a burned house by Spanish soldiers under Legazpi in 1565, it is the oldest Christian image…

saxo-grammaticus.s: Saxo Grammaticus was a Danish historian and cleric in the service of Archbishop Absalon of Lund. His Latin Gesta Danorum, in sixteen books, traces Danish history from legendary kings to the 1180s and preserves many Scandinavian myths and legends, including the tale of Amleth,…

svantevit.s: Svantevit was a god of the Baltic Slavs, worshipped above all by the Rani at the temple fortress of Arkona on Rügen. Saxo Grammaticus describes his huge wooden statue with four heads holding a drinking horn, a sacred white horse kept for divination, and tribute sent from other…

subotica.s: Subotica is a city in northern Serbia, in the Bačka part of Vojvodina, close to the Hungarian border. In 1526–1527 the Serbian leader Jovan Nenad held his court there.

szeged.s: Szeged is the largest city of southern Hungary, on the Tisza River near the Serbian and Romanian borders. A medieval royal town and then an Ottoman garrison from 1543 to 1686, it was almost destroyed by the great flood of 1879 and rebuilt to a planned design with ring boulevards.

sarolt.s: Sarolt was a Hungarian noblewoman, daughter of the gyula who ruled in Transylvania, who married Géza, Grand Prince of the Hungarians. She was the mother of Stephen I, the first king of Hungary.

santa-river-peru.s: The Santa River is a river of northern Peru that rises at Lake Conococha in the Andes, flows north through the Callejón de Huaylas and then turns west to reach the Pacific near Chimbote. Its valley was settled by the Recuay culture and other Andean societies, and today it…

srinatha.s: Srinatha was a Telugu poet who served the Reddi king Pedakomati Vema of Kondavidu in the late 14th and early 15th centuries. He is famous for the Sringara Naishadhamu, a Telugu rendering of Sriharsha's Naishadhacharita, for the Kasikhandamu and for popular occasional verses.

sicard-of-benevento.s: Sicard was the Lombard prince of Benevento from 832 to 839. He waged war on the Duchy of Naples, sacked Amalfi in 838 and carried many of its people off to Salerno, and he brought the relics of Saint Bartholomew from Lipari to Benevento.

sharur-district.s: Sharur is a district of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic of Azerbaijan, in the fertile plain of the Aras River near the borders with Turkey, Iran and Armenia. In 1501 Ismail I defeated the Aq Qoyunlu at the Battle of Sharur, a step towards founding the Safavid state.

san-miguel-bulacan.s: San Miguel is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, on the island of Luzon in the Philippines. In 1897 Emilio Aguinaldo's revolutionaries withdrew to the caves of Biak-na-Bato in its hills, where they proclaimed the Republic of Biak-na-Bato and adopted a provisional…

sansepolcro.s: Sansepolcro, formerly Borgo Sansepolcro, is a town in the upper Tiber valley in the province of Arezzo, Tuscany. Pope Eugene IV sold it to the Republic of Florence in 1440, a transaction whose loose wording left the tiny Republic of Cospaia unclaimed for centuries.

sierra-maestra.s: The Sierra Maestra is the highest mountain range of Cuba, in the south-east of the island, rising to Pico Turquino at about 1,970 metres. Its rugged forests sheltered rebels in the wars of independence and, from December 1956, Fidel Castro's guerrillas, who built there the…

singing-revolution.s: The Singing Revolution was the movement of mass, largely non-violent protest from 1987 to 1991 that led to the restoration of independence of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania from the Soviet Union. In Estonia it took its name from huge song gatherings such as the night song…

spinola-family.s: The Spinola were one of the great noble families of Genoa, rivals and at times allies of the Doria, Fieschi and Grimaldi. Oberto Spinola shared power with Oberto Doria from 1270, and later Spinolas served as doges, bankers to the Spanish crown and generals.

storming-of-the-bastille.s: The storming of the Bastille was the capture of the Bastille, a royal fortress and prison in eastern Paris, by armed crowds on 14 July 1789. Fearing a royal move against the National Assembly, Parisians seized weapons and attacked the fortress in search of gunpowder, and its…

sajudis.s: Sąjūdis, the Reform Movement of Lithuania, was a political movement founded in Vilnius in June 1988 that led Lithuania's campaign for independence from the Soviet Union. Headed by the musicologist Vytautas Landsbergis, it won a majority in the elections to the Supreme Council…

society-for-the-revival-of-kurdistan.n: Society for the Revival of Kurdistan
society-for-the-revival-of-kurdistan.s: The Society for the Revival of Kurdistan, known as Komala, was a secret Kurdish nationalist organisation founded in Mahabad in north-western Iran in 1942, during the Allied occupation of the country. It promoted Kurdish autonomy, language and culture.

somoza-family.s: The Somoza family ruled Nicaragua as a political dynasty from 1936 to 1979. Anastasio Somoza García, head of the US-trained National Guard, seized power in 1936 and, after his assassination in 1956, was succeeded by his sons Luis Somoza Debayle and Anastasio Somoza Debayle.

san-paragorio.s: San Paragorio is a Romanesque church in Noli, on the Ligurian coast of Italy, built in the 11th century on the site of an early Christian church. It served as the cathedral of the diocese of Noli, created in 1239, until the see moved to another church in the town.

sam-bellamy.s: Sam Bellamy, known as Black Sam, was an English pirate who in 1716–1717 became one of the most successful raiders of the Golden Age of Piracy, operating in the Caribbean and off North America. He began under Benjamin Hornigold and in 1717 captured the slave ship Whydah, which…

saint-marinus.s: Saint Marinus is the traditional founder of San Marino, said to have been a Christian stonemason from the island of Rab in Dalmatia. According to tradition he took refuge on Monte Titano from the persecution of Diocletian and founded a community there on 3 September 301, the…

statutes-of-sassari.s: The Statutes of Sassari are the municipal laws of the commune of Sassari in northern Sardinia, compiled in 1316 when the city was allied to Genoa. They survive in Latin and Sardinian versions and regulate the city's government, trade, farming and justice.

simone-martini.s: Simone Martini was a Sienese painter, a follower of Duccio and one of the most influential artists of the 14th century. His works include the Maestà fresco of 1315 in Siena's Palazzo Pubblico and the Annunciation of 1333, now in the Uffizi.

sharpeville-massacre.s: The Sharpeville massacre took place on 21 March 1960 in the township of Sharpeville, south of Johannesburg, when police fired on a crowd protesting against the pass laws in a campaign led by the Pan Africanist Congress, killing 69 people. The government declared a state of…

soweto-uprising.s: The Soweto uprising began on 16 June 1976, when thousands of Black schoolchildren in Soweto, near Johannesburg, marched against the compulsory use of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. Police opened fire, killing Hector Pieterson among others, and protests spread across…

sierre.s: Sierre is a town in the canton of Valais, Switzerland, on the Rhône at the boundary between French and German speech. It was one of the seven tenths (Zenden) that governed the Republic of the Valais from the 17th century until 1798.

simplon-pass.s: The Simplon Pass is an Alpine pass at about 2,005 metres between Brig in the Swiss canton of Valais and Domodossola in Italy. It was a medieval trade route, controlled in the 17th century by the Brig merchant Kaspar Stockalper.

serrata-del-maggior-consiglio.s: The Serrata del Maggior Consiglio ('closing of the Great Council') was a reform of the Republic of Venice begun in 1297 under Doge Pietro Gradenigo. It limited membership of the Great Council to men whose families had recently sat on it and a few co-opted families, and in the…

st-francisville-louisiana.s: St. Francisville is a small town on the east bank of the Mississippi River in West Feliciana Parish, Louisiana. In 1810 it served as the capital of the short-lived Republic of West Florida, proclaimed by Anglo-American settlers against Spanish rule.

santiago-iman.s: Santiago Imán was a Yucatecan militia officer who led a federalist revolt against Mexico's centralist government in 1839–1840, starting at Tizimín. He recruited Maya peasants with promises of lower church fees and taxes, and his success restored Yucatán's autonomy, leading to…

santiago-mendez.s: Santiago Méndez Ibarra was a politician from Campeche who served several times as governor of Yucatán in the 1840s and 1850s. He led the Campeche faction in a long rivalry with Miguel Barbachano of Mérida.

st-olafs-church-tallinn.s: St. Olaf's Church is a Gothic church in the old town of Tallinn, Estonia, first recorded in the 13th century. Rebuilt several times after fires and lightning strikes, its spire is thought to have made it one of the tallest buildings in Europe in the 16th century.

second-serbian-uprising.s: The Second Serbian Uprising was a revolt of Serbs against Ottoman rule, launched at Takovo in April 1815 under Miloš Obrenović. Combining fighting with negotiation, Miloš won a measure of self-government from the Ottomans, and the autonomous Principality of Serbia that emerged…

sandile.s: Sandile was paramount chief of the Rharhabe Xhosa from 1840, the son and heir of Ngqika. He led his people in the frontier wars of 1846–1847 and 1850–1853 against the Cape Colony, lost much of his land after the cattle-killing of 1856–1857 and was killed fighting the British…

siebengebirge.s: The Siebengebirge ('Seven Mountains') is a range of volcanic hills on the east bank of the Rhine south-east of Bonn, Germany. Its peaks include the Drachenfels, with its ruined castle, a landmark of Rhine Romanticism.

shigatse.s: Shigatse is the second-largest city of Tibet, in the Tsang region west of Lhasa. It grew around the fortress of Samdrubtse, seat of the Rinpungpa and Tsangpa rulers of Tsang in the 15th to 17th centuries.

shigatse-dzong.s: Shigatse Dzong, or Samdrubtse, is a fortress on a hill above Shigatse in the Tsang region of Tibet. It was seized by the Rinpungpa in 1435 and became the seat of their power and then of the Tsangpa kings, until the Khoshut Mongols captured it in 1642.

stavanger.s: Stavanger is a city in Rogaland on the south-west coast of Norway. It grew around its cathedral, begun around 1125 when the town became a bishop's seat, and later lived from fishing, canning and shipping.

saskatchewan.s: Saskatchewan is a prairie province of western Canada, between Alberta and Manitoba, with Regina as its capital. Formerly part of Rupert's Land and the North-West Territories, it was the scene of the North-West Rebellion of 1885 and became a province in 1905.

sitka.s: Sitka is a city on Baranof Island in south-east Alaska. Founded as New Archangel by Alexander Baranov in 1804, after the Tlingit had destroyed an earlier Russian fort in 1802, it became the capital of Russian America in 1808.

sedrata.s: Sedrata is a ruined medieval town in the Sahara near Ouargla, Algeria. It was founded by Ibadi refugees after the fall of the Rustamid imamate of Tahert in 909 and flourished on trans-Saharan trade, leaving remains of finely carved stucco decoration.

sho-shin.s: Shō Shin was king of Ryukyu from 1477 to 1527, the third ruler of the Second Shō dynasty. He centralised the kingdom by bringing the local aji lords to live at the capital Shuri, organised a hierarchy of priestesses under a royal high priestess, and brought the Yaeyama Islands…

sabina.s: Sabina is a historical region of central Italy north-east of Rome, between the Tiber, the Aniene and the Apennines, named after the ancient Sabines. It lies mostly in the modern province of Rieti in Lazio and is known for its olive oil.

saga-prefecture.s: Saga Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan in north-western Kyushu, with its capital at Saga. It covers the eastern part of the former Hizen province, including the lands of the Saga domain ruled by the Nabeshima until 1871.

samaratungga.s: Samaratungga was a king of the Sailendra dynasty in Central Java in the early 9th century. The Karangtengah inscription of 824 links him to the building of a Buddhist sanctuary, and Borobudur is generally thought to have been completed in his reign.

saint-barthelemy.s: Saint Barthélemy is a small island in the Leeward Islands of the Caribbean and an overseas collectivity of France. Settled by France in the 17th century, it was handed to Sweden in 1784 in exchange for French trading rights at Gothenburg, and Sweden made its town of Gustavia a…

saint-lucian-creole.s: Saint Lucian Creole, or Kwéyòl, is a French-based creole language spoken by most people in Saint Lucia. It arose under French colonial rule in the 17th and 18th centuries and survived more than 150 years of British rule after 1814, when English became the official language.

saint-lucia-labour-party.s: The Saint Lucia Labour Party is a social-democratic political party in Saint Lucia, founded in 1950 out of the trade union movement. It has alternated in power with the United Workers Party, governing from 1979 to 1982, under Kenny Anthony from 1997 to 2006 and from 2011 to…

saito-yoshitatsu.s: Saitō Yoshitatsu was a daimyo of Mino province in Japan, the eldest son, or by some accounts the adopted son, of Saito Dosan. In 1556 he rebelled against Dosan and killed him in battle at the Nagara river, taking control of Mino.

saka-haumavarga.s: The Saka Haumavarga were a Saka people named in Achaemenid Persian inscriptions of the late 6th century BCE, probably living in Fergana and the Pamirs. Their name is usually taken to mean 'hauma-drinking' or 'hauma-preparing' Saka, after the ritual drink of Iranian religion.

saka-tigraxauda.s: The Saka Tigraxauda, 'Saka with pointed caps', were a Saka people named in Achaemenid Persian inscriptions, probably living east of the Caspian Sea and along the Syr Darya. Darius I campaigned against them around 519 BCE and captured their chief Skunkha, who is shown in a tall…

skunkha.s: Skunkha was a chief of the Saka Tigraxauda, the 'pointed-cap' Saka of Central Asia, in the late 6th century BCE. Darius I of Persia campaigned against his people around 519 BCE, captured him and installed a loyal chief in his place.

sen-no-rikyu.s: Sen no Rikyū was a Japanese tea master from a merchant family of Sakai who shaped the tea ceremony into its classic form. He served Oda Nobunaga and then Toyotomi Hideyoshi, for whom he organised great tea gatherings, and promoted wabi, a rustic and simple aesthetic.

sakya-pandita.s: Sakya Pandita, Kunga Gyaltsen, was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and one of the five founding masters of the Sakya school. Famous for his learning in logic, grammar and poetry, he answered the summons of the Mongol prince Köten in 1244 and met him at Liangzhou in 1247,…

salur.s: The Salur, or Salghur, are one of the old Oghuz Turkic tribes listed by Mahmud al-Kashgari in the 11th century. Salur groups entered Iran with the Seljuks, and one of their chiefs founded the Salghurid atabegs of Fars in 1148.

sunqur-ibn-mawdud.s: Sunqur ibn Mawdud was the founder of the Salghurid dynasty of Fars in south-western Iran. A Turkmen chief of the Salghur tribe, he seized Fars from Seljuk officials in 1148 and ruled from Shiraz as atabeg, nominally guardian of Seljuk princes but in practice independent.

saman-khuda.s: Saman Khuda was the ancestor of the Samanid dynasty, a Persian landowner of the Balkh region in the early 8th century. According to tradition he converted from Zoroastrianism to Islam under the Umayyad governor Asad ibn Abdallah al-Qasri, after whom he named his son Asad.

samaleswari.s: Samaleswari, or Samalei, is a Hindu goddess, the presiding deity of Sambalpur in western Odisha, India. Her temple on the bank of the Mahanadi was built by the Chauhan rulers of Sambalpur, traditionally in the 16th century, and she is worshipped as a form of the mother goddess…

surendra-sai.s: Surendra Sai was a claimant to the throne of Sambalpur in western Odisha, India, who led a long armed revolt against British rule. Imprisoned at Hazaribagh from 1840, he was freed by mutineers in 1857 and fought a guerrilla war in the hills of Sambalpur until his surrender in…

stephen-w-kearny.s: Stephen W. Kearny was a United States Army officer who commanded the Army of the West in the Mexican–American War. In August 1846 he occupied Santa Fe without a battle and proclaimed New Mexico American territory before marching on to California, where he fought at San Pasqual…

saintes.s: Saintes is a town on the Charente in western France, in the department of Charente-Maritime. As Mediolanum Santonum it was the chief town of the Gallic Santones and the first capital of the Roman province of Aquitania, and it keeps the Arch of Germanicus and a large…

saintonge.s: Saintonge is a historic province of western France on the Atlantic coast north of the Gironde, centred on the town of Saintes, whose name derives from the Gallic Santones. In the Middle Ages it belonged to the duchy of Aquitaine and was contested between the kings of England…

sabzevar.s: Sabzevar is a city in Razavi Khorasan province in north-eastern Iran, west of Nishapur on the old road between Tehran and Mashhad. In the 14th century it was the capital of the Sarbadars, a Shia state formed in a revolt against Mongol officials after the break-up of the…

sibyl-hathaway.s: Sibyl Hathaway was the Dame of Sark, the feudal ruler of the Channel Island of Sark, from 1927 until her death in 1974. During the German occupation of 1940 to 1945 she stayed on the island and dealt firmly with the occupying officers on behalf of its inhabitants.

seiwa-genji.s: The Seiwa Genji are the branch of the Minamoto clan descended from Emperor Seiwa, who reigned in the 9th century. Settled as provincial warriors in eastern Japan, they produced the founder of the Kamakura shogunate, Minamoto no Yoritomo, and later the Ashikaga shoguns.

simuka.s: Simuka is named in the Puranas as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty of the Deccan, and his name appears in a label beside a now-damaged relief portrait in the Naneghat cave. The Puranic lists credit him with overthrowing the last Kanva ruler, but his date is uncertain,…

sopara.s: Sopara, ancient Shurparaka, is a town north of Mumbai in Palghar district of Maharashtra, India, now part of the Nala Sopara area. It was one of the chief ports of the Konkan coast from the Maurya period, when an edict of Ashoka was inscribed there, and remained an important…

satsuma-rebellion.s: The Satsuma Rebellion was a rising of former samurai of Kagoshima against the Meiji government in 1877, led by Saigo Takamori. Angered by the loss of their privileges and stipends, the rebels besieged Kumamoto Castle but were defeated by the new conscript army.

shuseikan.s: The Shuseikan was an industrial complex built in Kagoshima by Shimazu Nariakira, lord of the Satsuma Domain, in the 1850s. Inspired by Dutch books, it included a reverberatory furnace for casting cannon, a blast furnace, glassworks and workshops, making it one of the first…

saudi-aramco.s: Saudi Aramco is the state oil company of Saudi Arabia and one of the largest companies in the world. It began as the California Arabian Standard Oil Company, formed in 1933 under a concession granted by King Abdulaziz, struck commercial oil at Dammam in 1938 and was renamed…

sindhudurg-fort.s: Sindhudurg Fort is a sea fort built by Shivaji on the island of Kurte off Malvan on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra between 1664 and 1667. Its walls run for about 4 kilometres around the rocky islet and were intended to counter the Portuguese, the English and the Siddis of…

sindhudurg-district.s: Sindhudurg district is the southernmost district of the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India, bordering Goa, with its headquarters at Oros. It was formed in 1981 from the southern part of Ratnagiri district and is named after Shivaji's sea fort of Sindhudurg off Malvan.

sava.s: The Sava is a river of south-eastern Europe, about 950 kilometres long, which rises in the Julian Alps of Slovenia and flows east through Croatia and along the Bosnian border to join the Danube at Belgrade. Its valley was a major route between Italy and the Balkans, guarded in…

solokha.s: Solokha is a royal Scythian burial mound of the late 5th or early 4th century BCE near the lower Dnieper in southern Ukraine. Excavated by Nikolai Veselovsky in 1912–1913, it contained an intact royal burial with a famous gold comb crowned by a battle scene of three warriors,…

simferopol.s: Simferopol is the main city of the Crimean peninsula, on the Salhyr river. On its edge lie the ruins of Scythian Neapolis, the capital of the late Scythian kingdom in the Crimea from the 3rd century BCE.

skilurus.s: Skilurus was a king of the Scythians in the Crimea in the 2nd century BCE who ruled from Scythian Neapolis near modern Simferopol. He extended his power over the Greek city of Olbia, where coins were struck in his name, and pressed Chersonesus.

sphodrias.s: Sphodrias was a Spartan commander who, while governing Thespiae in 378 BCE, launched an unauthorised night raid into Attica aimed at the Piraeus. The raid failed, but his acquittal at Sparta through the influence of King Agesilaus II outraged the Athenians, who allied with…

saifuddin-azizi.s: Saifuddin Azizi was a Uyghur politician from Artush who served as a minister in the Second East Turkestan Republic and in the coalition government of Xinjiang from 1946. In 1949 he joined the Chinese Communist Party and supported the incorporation of Xinjiang into the People's…

sanation.s: Sanation was the political movement of Józef Piłsudski and his supporters, who took power in Poland in the May Coup of 1926 and governed until the German invasion of 1939. Its name came from its stated aim of restoring the moral health of public life after years of unstable…

second-battle-of-la-puerta.s: The Second Battle of La Puerta was fought on 15 June 1814 near San Juan de los Morros, Venezuela, between the patriot armies of Simón Bolívar and Santiago Mariño and the royalist llanero cavalry of José Tomás Boves. Boves won a crushing victory, opening the road to Caracas,…

simbar-shipak.s: Simbar-Shipak was a king of Babylon and the founder of the Second Sealand Dynasty, reigning from about 1025 to 1008 BCE. Of southern origin, he took the throne after the end of the Second Dynasty of Isin at a time of Aramean and Sutean raids.

spanish-constitution-of-1931.s: The Spanish Constitution of 1931 was approved by the Cortes on 9 December 1931 as the founding law of the Second Spanish Republic. It declared Spain a 'democratic republic of workers of all classes', separated church and state, allowed divorce and regional autonomy, and gave…

salduie.s: Salduie was an Iberian town of the Sedetani on the Ebro in north-eastern Spain, on the site of modern Zaragoza. It struck coins with its name in Iberian script, and horsemen from the town served Rome in the Social War, as recorded on the Bronze of Ascoli of 89 BCE.

salehuddin-of-selangor.s: Salehuddin of Selangor, born Raja Lumu, was the first Sultan of Selangor, recognised around 1766 with the sanction of the ruler of Perak. A son of the Bugis chief Daeng Chelak, he ruled from Kuala Selangor and turned the Bugis settlements on the Selangor coast into a sultanate.

sharafuddin-of-selangor.s: Sharafuddin Idris Shah is the ninth Sultan of Selangor, who succeeded his father Salahuddin in 2001. Born in 1945, he heads one of the nine Malay royal houses whose rulers take turns to serve as Malaysia's king.

sumbawa.s: Sumbawa is an island in Indonesia's Lesser Sunda chain, between Lombok and Flores. It was divided among several small kingdoms and sultanates, including Sumbawa, Bima and Dompu, which had close ties with Makassar.

strabo.s: Strabo was a Greek geographer and historian from Amaseia in Pontus, active under Augustus and Tiberius. His Geography, in seventeen books, describes the peoples, cities and lands of the Roman world from Iberia to India.

selpils.s: Sēlpils was the main hillfort of the Selonians, on the left bank of the Daugava in south-eastern Latvia. In 1208 Bishop Albert of Riga and the Livonian Brothers of the Sword besieged and took it, and the Selonians accepted baptism.

seminole-tribe-of-florida.s: The Seminole Tribe of Florida is a federally recognised Native American nation formed in 1957 by descendants of the Seminoles who stayed in Florida after the Seminole Wars. It holds several reservations, including Big Cypress, Brighton and Hollywood.

second-seminole-war.s: The Second Seminole War was fought from 1835 to 1842 between the United States and the Seminole of Florida, who resisted removal to Indian Territory. Led by chiefs such as Osceola and Micanopy, the Seminole waged a guerrilla war in the swamps that cost the United States…

samanta-sena.s: Samanta Sena was the founder of the Sena family of Bengal, a warrior said in the dynasty's inscriptions to have come from Karnata in southern India. He settled in the Radha region of western Bengal in the 11th century.

sendai-castle.s: Sendai Castle, also called Aoba Castle, was built from 1601 by Date Masamune on Mount Aoba above the city of Sendai in north-eastern Japan. It remained the seat of the Date lords of the Sendai Domain until 1871.

sendai.s: Sendai is the capital of Miyagi Prefecture and the largest city of the Tōhoku region in north-eastern Japan. It was laid out from 1601 by Date Masamune around his castle and was the seat of the Sendai Domain throughout the Edo period.

seneca-lake.s: Seneca Lake is the largest of the Finger Lakes of western New York, about 60 km long and over 180 m deep. It lay at the eastern edge of the Seneca homeland, which stretched west to the Genesee River.

sens.s: Sens is a town on the Yonne in Burgundy, France, known in Roman times as Agedincum, the chief town of the Senones. In the Middle Ages its archbishops were among the most powerful in France, and its cathedral, begun in the 1130s, is one of the earliest Gothic cathedrals.

spyridon-georgios-theotokis.s: Spyridon Georgios Theotokis was a Corfiot nobleman who became the first head of the Septinsular Republic, presiding over its senate from 1800. The republic, created by Russia and the Ottoman Empire, was the first self-governing Greek state of modern times.

serbian-progressive-party.s: The Serbian Progressive Party is a Serbian political party founded in 2008 by Tomislav Nikolić and Aleksandar Vučić, who broke away from the nationalist Serbian Radical Party. It has led Serbia's governments since 2012.

smederevo.s: Smederevo is a city on the Danube in Serbia, east of Belgrade. Despot Đurađ Branković built its huge fortress between 1428 and 1430 as the new capital of the Serbian Despotate, one of the largest lowland fortresses in Europe.

stevan-supljikac.s: Stevan Šupljikac was a Serbian officer in the Austrian army who was elected vojvoda, or duke, of the Serbian Vojvodina by the May Assembly at Sremski Karlovci in 1848. He led the Serb forces against the Hungarian revolutionary government for a short time.

simalungun-people.s: The Simalungun are a Batak people of North Sumatra, Indonesia, living mainly in Simalungun Regency around Pematangsiantar. They were divided among small kingdoms that came under Dutch control in the late 19th century.

seym-river.s: The Seym is a river of Russia and Ukraine, about 750 km long, the largest left tributary of the Desna. It flows from the Kursk region westwards past Kursk and Putyvl.

sula-river.s: The Sula is a river of north-eastern Ukraine, about 360 km long, a left tributary of the Dnieper. Romny and Lubny stand on its banks.

sokmen-al-qutbi.s: Sökmen al-Qutbi was a Turkish mamluk officer of the Seljuks who took Ahlat on Lake Van from the Marwanids in 1100. He founded the Shah-Armen dynasty, which ruled the region around the lake for over a century.

sokmen-ii.s: Sökmen II was the longest-reigning ruler of the Shah-Armen dynasty of Ahlat, from 1128 to 1185. He fought the Georgians and married into the Artuqid and Zengid families, making Ahlat a rich trading city.

sokmen-ibn-artuq.s: Sökmen ibn Artuq was a Turkmen commander, son of Artuq, who held Jerusalem with his brother Ilghazi until the Fatimids took it in 1098. In 1102 he seized Hisn Kayfa on the Tigris, founding the Artuqid line there.

saugor-and-nerbudda-territories.s: The Saugor and Nerbudda Territories were a British-ruled region of central India, formed from lands taken from the Marathas in 1818 around Sagar and the Narmada valley. Administered at times from Calcutta and Agra, they were enlarged by lands confiscated after the rising of 1857.

sagar-madhya-pradesh.s: Sagar, historically Saugor, is a city in the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh, India, set beside a large lake. Ruled by the Marathas in the 18th century, it passed to the British in 1818 and gave its name to the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories.

suddhodana.s: Suddhodana was a chief of the Shakya clan and the father of Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha. Early texts describe him as a leader of the Shakya assembly at Kapilavastu, while later tradition made him a king.

shambaa-people.s: The Shambaa are a Bantu-speaking people of the Usambara Mountains in the Tanga Region of north-eastern Tanzania. Farmers of the steep hillsides, they were united in the 18th century under the Kilindi dynasty, whose kingdom dominated the mountains until the German conquest.

shanghai.s: Shanghai is China's largest city, a port at the mouth of the Yangtze on the Huangpu River. Opened to foreign trade by the Treaty of Nanking in 1842, it grew around foreign concessions into East Asia's leading commercial and financial centre by the 1920s.

shanghai-municipal-council.s: The Shanghai Municipal Council was the governing body of the Shanghai International Settlement from 1854 to 1943. Elected by foreign ratepayers and dominated by British businessmen, it ran the settlement's police, public works, health services and volunteer corps with little…

sidi-ahmed-ou-moussa.s: Sidi Ahmed ou Moussa was a Sufi saint of the Sous region of southern Morocco who taught in the Tazeroualt and died there in 1563. His shrine and zawiya became a major pilgrimage centre, and his descendants, the sharifs of Iligh, built a regional state on its prestige in the…

samaritans.s: The Samaritans are an ethno-religious community of the Levant who follow a religion closely related to Judaism, based on their own version of the Pentateuch, and hold Mount Gerizim near Nablus sacred instead of Jerusalem. They trace their descent to the Israelites who remained…

shakhbut-bin-sultan-al-nahyan.s: Shakhbut bin Sultan Al Nahyan was ruler of Abu Dhabi from 1928 to 1966. His long reign saw the collapse of the pearl trade and the discovery of oil, which was first exported in 1962, but his reluctance to spend the new revenues frustrated his family and the British.

sharqiyin.s: The Sharqiyin are an Arab tribe of the east coast of the Oman peninsula, centred on Fujairah. Long subject to the Al Qasimi of Sharjah, their leaders asserted independence in the early 20th century, and in 1952 Britain recognised Fujairah as a separate Trucial State under the…

sabah.s: Sabah is a Malaysian state in the north of Borneo, with its capital at Kota Kinabalu. Long claimed by the sultanates of Brunei and Sulu, it was administered by the British North Borneo Company from 1881, became a British crown colony in 1946 and joined Malaysia in 1963.

sabah-i-bin-jaber.s: Sabah I bin Jaber was the first ruler of Kuwait, chosen as leader around 1752 by the Bani Utbah families who had settled on the bay. He handled relations with the Ottoman authorities in Basra and the surrounding tribes, while the town lived from trade, pearling and shipbuilding.

saqr-bin-mohammed-al-qasimi.s: Saqr bin Mohammed Al Qasimi was ruler of Ras al-Khaimah from 1948 until his death in 2010. He kept his emirate out of the United Arab Emirates at its founding in December 1971, hoping for oil revenues and angered by Iran's seizure of the Tunb islands, but joined it in February…

shilluk-people.s: The Shilluk, or Chollo, are a Nilotic people living mainly along the west bank of the White Nile in South Sudan, around Malakal and Kodok. Their kingdom, founded according to tradition by Nyikang, was ruled by a sacred king, the reth, from Fashoda.

shimazu-iehisa.s: Shimazu Iehisa was a samurai commander of the Shimazu clan of Satsuma, the youngest brother of Shimazu Yoshihisa. He won the clan's great victories over the Ryūzōji at Okitanawate in 1584, where Ryūzōji Takanobu was killed, and over the forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's allies at…

shimazu-toshihisa.s: Shimazu Toshihisa was a samurai commander of the Shimazu clan of Satsuma, the third of the four brothers who led the clan's conquest of most of Kyushu. He fought in the campaigns of the 1570s and 1580s and opposed submission to Toyotomi Hideyoshi.

shimazu-yoshihiro.s: Shimazu Yoshihiro was a samurai general of the Shimazu clan of Satsuma, brother of Shimazu Yoshihisa. He fought in the conquest of Kyushu, won a famous victory at Sacheon during Japan's invasion of Korea in 1598, and at Sekigahara in 1600 led his small force on a desperate…

shimazu-yoshihisa.s: Shimazu Yoshihisa was head of the Shimazu clan of Satsuma from 1566. With his brothers he conquered Osumi and Hyūga, defeated the Ōtomo at Mimikawa in 1578 and the Ryūzōji at Okitanawate in 1584, and by 1586 controlled most of Kyushu.

shamakhi.s: Shamakhi is a town in the mountains of eastern Azerbaijan, for centuries the capital of the Shirvanshahs and of the province of Shirvan. A centre of the silk trade, it was sacked in 1721 by Lezgin rebels, an event that helped prompt Peter the Great's Persian campaign.

shirvanshah.s: Shirvanshah, "king of Shirvan", was the title of the rulers of Shirvan in the eastern Caucasus. Used under the Sasanians, it was revived in 861 by the Arab governor Haytham ibn Khalid and borne by his Yazidid descendants and later by the Derbendi line until the Safavids…

sakata.s: Sakata is a port city at the mouth of the Mogami River in Yamagata Prefecture, Japan, on the Sea of Japan coast. In the Edo period it shipped the rice of the Shōnai plain and the Mogami valley to Osaka and Edo on the western sea route, and merchant families such as the Homma…

siak-sri-indrapura-palace.s: The Siak Sri Indrapura Palace, formally Asserayah Hasyimiah, is the palace of the sultans of Siak in Riau province, Sumatra, Indonesia. It was built in 1889 under Sultan Syarif Hasyim on the bank of the Siak river, in a mix of Malay, Arab and European styles.

sidetic-language.s: Sidetic was an Anatolian language spoken at Side on the Pamphylian coast of southern Turkey, related to Luwian and Lycian. It is known from a few inscriptions and coin legends of the 5th to 2nd centuries BCE, written in a distinctive alphabet of its own.

sierra-leone-creole-people.s: The Sierra Leone Creoles, or Krio, are descendants of the freed slaves who settled in Freetown from 1787: Black Poor from London, black Nova Scotians, Jamaican Maroons and tens of thousands of Africans liberated from slave ships by the Royal Navy. Protestant and…

sarbat-khalsa.s: The Sarbat Khalsa, "the entire Khalsa", was the general assembly of the Sikh community, which met at the Akal Takht in Amritsar, usually at Baisakhi and Diwali, during the 18th century. Leaders of the misls gathered there to settle disputes and plan joint campaigns, and its…

sukerchakia-misl.s: The Sukerchakia misl was one of the Sikh confederacies of 18th-century Punjab, based at Gujranwala and founded by Charat Singh. Under his son Maha Singh it grew strong, and his grandson Ranjit Singh used it as the base for capturing Lahore in 1799 and absorbing the other misls…

sanjan.s: Sanjan is a town in Valsad district, Gujarat, India, on the coast north of Mumbai. In the early Middle Ages it was a busy port trading with the Persian Gulf, and according to the Qissa-i Sanjan it was where Zoroastrian refugees from Iran, the ancestors of the Parsis, landed…

seokguram.s: Seokguram is an artificial cave shrine on Mount Toham near Gyeongju, South Korea, built in the mid-8th century under the Unified Silla minister Kim Daeseong. Its domed granite chamber holds a great seated Buddha surrounded by reliefs of bodhisattvas and guardians, a…

sextus-julius-frontinus.s: Sextus Julius Frontinus was a Roman senator, general and writer. As governor of Britain from about 74 to 78 he subdued the Silures of south Wales and founded the legionary fortress at Caerleon.

senlis.s: Senlis is a town in the Oise department of northern France, north of Paris. As Augustomagus it was the chief town of the Gallic Silvanectes under Rome, and its late Roman walls partly survive.

sunzha.s: The Sunzha is a river of the North Caucasus, a right tributary of the Terek, flowing east through Ingushetia and Chechnya past Grozny. Its valley was a centre of Chechen and Ingush settlement and, from the 19th century, of Russian fortresses and Cossack villages, including the…

siphnian-treasury.s: The Siphnian Treasury is a small Ionic building at the sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi, built about 525 BCE by the people of Siphnos from the wealth of their gold and silver mines. It housed their offerings to the god and is famous for its sculptured frieze, which shows scenes…

sinni.s: The Sinni is a river of Basilicata in southern Italy, rising in the Lucanian Apennines and flowing east into the Gulf of Taranto. In antiquity it was called the Siris, and the Greek colony of Siris was founded near its mouth around 680 BCE by settlers from Colophon.

shamsher-prakash.s: Shamsher Prakash was Raja of Sirmur, a princely state in the Himalayan foothills of present-day Himachal Pradesh, from 1856 to 1898. A loyal ally of the British, he modernised his small state from its capital Nahan, founding the Nahan Foundry, building roads, schools and…

sumy.s: Sumy is a city in north-eastern Ukraine and the centre of Sumy Oblast, on the Psel river close to the Russian border. It was founded in the 1650s by Cossack settlers from right-bank Ukraine under Herasym Kondratiev and became the seat of the Sumy Cossack regiment of Sloboda…

socialist-party-of-chile.s: The Socialist Party of Chile is a left-wing political party founded on 19 April 1933 by Marmaduke Grove, Eugenio Matte, Oscar Schnake, Salvador Allende and other veterans of the short-lived Socialist Republic of 1932. Allende was elected president in 1970 at the head of the…

sognefjord.s: The Sognefjord is the longest and deepest fjord in Norway, running about 205 km inland from the coast of Vestland in western Norway and reaching depths of over 1,300 m. Its steep-sided branches, such as the Nærøyfjord and the Lustrafjord, are lined with farms and old…

sylhet.s: Sylhet is a city in north-eastern Bangladesh on the Surma river and the centre of Sylhet Division. Conquered by Muslim forces from Bengal in 1303, it is known for the shrine of the Sufi saint Shah Jalal, and under British rule it became a centre of tea growing.

satgaon.s: Satgaon, ancient Saptagram, was a river port on the Saraswati, a branch of the Hooghly, in the Hooghly district of present-day West Bengal. From the 13th to the 16th century it was the chief port of south-western Bengal and a seat of governors and mints, trading with…

soppeng-regency.s: Soppeng Regency is a regency of South Sulawesi province in Indonesia, with its seat at Watansoppeng. It covers the lands of the former Bugis kingdom of Soppeng, a rice-growing realm that from 1582 was allied with Bone and Wajo in the Tellumpoccoe.

shen-yue.s: Shen Yue (441–513) was a Chinese historian, poet and statesman of the Southern Dynasties and one of the Eight Friends of Jingling. He compiled the Book of Song, the official history of the Liu Song dynasty, and with others formulated rules on the four tones of Chinese and the…

sicuani.s: Sicuani is a town in the Cusco Region of southern Peru, on the Vilcanota river at about 3,550 m, and the capital of Canchis Province. It lies on the route between Cusco and Lake Titicaca.

saipan.s: Saipan is the largest island and seat of government of the Northern Mariana Islands, a US commonwealth in the western Pacific. Under Japanese rule from 1914 it was developed for sugar cane with many settlers from Japan and Okinawa.

south-seas-development-company.s: The South Seas Development Company (Nan'yō Kōhatsu) was a Japanese colonial company founded in 1921 by the businessman Matsue Haruji to develop the South Seas Mandate. It built sugar plantations and refineries on Saipan, Tinian and Rota, worked mainly by migrants from Okinawa…

sam-nujoma.s: Sam Nujoma (1929–2025) was a Namibian nationalist leader and the first president of Namibia, from independence in 1990 to 2005. He co-founded SWAPO in 1960 and led its long struggle against South African rule from exile, including the armed struggle that began in 1966.

sutherland.s: Sutherland is a historic county in the far north of Scotland, now part of the Highland council area, a thinly peopled land of moors, mountains and lochs. Its Gaelic name, Cataibh, recalls the Cait of Pictish times, while the English name comes from the Norse 'southern land',…

smertrios.s: Smertrios was a Celtic god known from Roman-period inscriptions in Gaul and the Rhineland, including the Pillar of the Boatmen in Paris, where he is shown as a bearded figure raising a club against a serpent. Often compared with Hercules or Mars, he is thought by many scholars…

scheveningen.s: Scheveningen is a seaside district of The Hague in the Netherlands, originally a fishing village on the North Sea coast. On 30 November 1813, after the collapse of French rule, William Frederick of Orange-Nassau landed on its beach to return from exile and accept sovereignty,…

salah-rais.s: Salah Rais (c. 1488–1556) was an Ottoman corsair and admiral who served as beylerbey of the Regency of Algiers from 1552 to 1556. A veteran of Hayreddin Barbarossa's campaigns, he extended Algerian power into the Sahara and over Tlemcen and took Bejaia from Spain in 1555.

sevilla-la-nueva.s: Sevilla la Nueva was the first Spanish settlement in Jamaica, founded in 1509 by Juan de Esquivel on the north coast near present-day St Ann's Bay. It served as the island's capital, with a fortified house, a church and sugar works worked by Taíno labour, but its site proved…

saguia-el-hamra.s: Saguia el-Hamra is the northern region of Western Sahara, named after a seasonal river that crosses it to the Atlantic near Laayoune. Added to the Spanish possessions by agreements with France between 1900 and 1912, it formed the northern part of Spanish Sahara, with Río de…

stephen-f-austin.s: Stephen F. Austin (1793–1836) was an American empresario known as the Father of Texas. Taking over his father's grant from newly independent Mexico, he settled the first legal Anglo-American colonists in Texas from 1821 and managed a colony of thousands of families.

san-jose-de-oruna.s: San José de Oruña, now St. Joseph, was the first permanent Spanish town in Trinidad, founded in 1592 by Antonio de Berrío inland from the Gulf of Paria as a base for his search for El Dorado. Walter Raleigh attacked and burned it in 1595.

sri-jayawardenepura-kotte.s: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital of Sri Lanka, a city on the south-eastern edge of Colombo. As Kotte it was the capital of a Sinhalese kingdom from the fifteenth century until the late sixteenth century, when it was abandoned under Portuguese pressure.

shangcai-county.s: Shangcai County is a county in Zhumadian, in south-central Henan province, China. The ancient town of Shangcai, whose earthen walls partly survive, was the first capital of the State of Cai, founded after the Zhou conquest, until Cai moved under pressure from Chu.

shouchun.s: Shouchun, modern Shou County in Anhui province, China, is an ancient city on the Huai River. It became the last capital of the State of Chu in 241 BCE and fell to Qin in 223 BCE.

salt-lake-valley.s: The Salt Lake Valley is a basin in northern Utah, between the Wasatch Range and the Oquirrh Mountains, south-east of the Great Salt Lake. The first Mormon pioneers under Brigham Young arrived there in July 1847, then in Mexican territory, and founded Salt Lake City, which…

shen-buhai.s: Shen Buhai (died 337 BCE) was chancellor of the State of Han under Marquis Zhao for about fifteen years. He developed the doctrine of shu, the techniques by which a ruler assigns offices, checks officials' performance against their titles and keeps his own intentions hidden.

shandong.s: Shandong is a coastal province of eastern China on the lower Yellow River, with its capital at Jinan. In antiquity it was the land of the states of Qi and Lu, the homeland of Confucius and Mencius, and Mount Tai there was China's most sacred mountain.

san-juan-river-nicaragua.s: The San Juan River flows about 190 kilometres from Lake Nicaragua to the Caribbean, forming much of the border between Nicaragua and Costa Rica. With the lake it offered a natural route across Central America, guarded by the Spanish fortress of El Castillo, and during the…

solemn-pact-of-society-and-union.n: Solemn Pact of Society and Union
solemn-pact-of-society-and-union.s: The Solemn Pact of Society and Union between the Provinces that form the State of Quito was a constitution adopted by a congress in Quito in February 1812. It created a State of Quito with separate legislative, executive and judicial powers while still nominally recognising…

shaanxi.s: Shaanxi is a province of north-western China, centred on the Wei River valley, with its capital at Xi'an. The Wei valley, or Guanzhong, was the homeland of the Zhou and the Qin and the seat of the Western Zhou, Qin, Western Han and Tang capitals.

slovenia.s: Slovenia is a country in central Europe between the Alps, the Pannonian plain and the Adriatic Sea, with its capital at Ljubljana. Its lands, including Carniola, Lower Styria and part of the Littoral, were ruled by the Habsburgs for centuries before joining the State of…

shangqiu.s: Shangqiu is a city in eastern Henan, on the plain between the Yellow and Huai rivers. Linked by tradition with the early Shang, it was the capital of the State of Song, founded by Weizi Qi to continue the Shang sacrifices, and later served as the Southern Capital of the…

suizhou.s: Suizhou is a city in northern Hubei, on the corridor between the Han River valley and the Huai plain. It was the seat of the Zhou-period state of Sui, identified with the state of Zeng known from bronze inscriptions, and the tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng, with its famous set of…

shoumeng.s: Shoumeng was king of Wu from 585 to 561 BCE, the first ruler of the state recorded with firm dates. Under him Wu, on the lower Yangtze, opened relations with the central states and, with Jin's help through the Chu exile Qu Wuchen, adopted chariot warfare and began attacking Chu.

sun-tzu.s: Sun Tzu (Sunzi, Sun Wu) is the traditional author of The Art of War, the most famous Chinese work on military strategy. According to the Shiji he was a general from Qi who served King Helü of Wu around 500 BCE, though many historians doubt this and date the text to the Warring…

shaoxing.s: Shaoxing is a city in northern Zhejiang, south of Hangzhou Bay. As Kuaiji it was the centre of the ancient State of Yue, and nearby Mount Kuaiji is the traditional burial place of Yu the Great.

sword-of-goujian.s: The Sword of Goujian is a bronze sword of the State of Yue found in 1965 in a Chu tomb near Jiangling in Hubei. An inscription in bird-script names its owner as a king of Yue, identified as Goujian, who reigned from 496 to 465 BCE.

skomantas.s: Skomantas was a leader of the Sudovians, or Yotvingians, a Baltic people, in the later 13th century. He led raids on Rus' and Polish lands and resisted the advance of the Teutonic Order, but in 1283 he submitted to the Order, ending organised Sudovian resistance.

suwalki.s: Suwałki is a town in north-eastern Poland, in Podlaskie Voivodeship near the borders with Lithuania and Russia. It lies in the former land of the Sudovians and grew from a settlement of the Camaldolese monks of Wigry in the early 18th century.

semnones.s: The Semnones were a Germanic people living between the Elbe and the Oder in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE. Tacitus called them the oldest and noblest of the Suebi and described the human sacrifices held in their sacred grove.

soissons.s: Soissons is a town on the Aisne in northern France. As Augusta Suessionum it was the Roman centre of the Suessiones, and in 486 Clovis I defeated Syagrius, ruler of the Domain of Soissons, near the city.

sieg-river.s: The Sieg is a river in western Germany, about 155 km long, rising in the Rothaar Mountains and flowing west through the Siegerland to join the Rhine near Bonn. In Roman times its valley lay in the land of the Sugambri, and the Siegerland was later an important iron-mining…

suket-satyagraha.s: The Suket Satyagraha was a popular movement in the princely state of Suket, in the hills of present-day Himachal Pradesh, in February 1948. Activists of the Praja Mandal, among them Yashwant Singh Parmar, occupied parts of the state and forced the raja to hand over its…

sundernagar.s: Sundernagar is a town in Mandi district of Himachal Pradesh, India, set in a broad valley at about 1,170 m. Originally called Banaid, it was the last capital of the princely state of Suket.

saad-zaghloul.s: Saad Zaghloul was an Egyptian nationalist leader and founder of the Wafd party. His arrest and deportation by the British in March 1919, after he sought to put Egypt's case for independence at the Paris Peace Conference, set off the Egyptian Revolution of 1919.

sabr-ad-din-i.s: Sabr ad-Din I was a sultan of Ifat of the Walashma dynasty in the early 14th century. In 1332 he rebelled against the Ethiopian emperor Amda Seyon, who crushed the revolt, captured him and placed his brother Jamal ad-Din on the throne as a tributary ruler.

sakalava.s: The Sakalava are a people of western Madagascar. From the 17th century their Maroserana kings built the kingdoms of Menabe and Boina, which used firearms bought from European traders to dominate the west coast and traded cattle and slaves at ports such as Mahajanga.

samawah.s: Samawah is a city on the Euphrates in southern Iraq, the capital of Muthanna province, about midway between Baghdad and Basra. It lies near the ruins of ancient Uruk.

sumbawa-besar.s: Sumbawa Besar is the main town of western Sumbawa in the Indonesian province of West Nusa Tenggara. From the later 17th century it was the seat of the Sumbawa Sultanate, whose rulers intermarried with the royal families of Makassar and the Bugis and accepted the overlordship…

sumedang.s: Sumedang is a town in the highlands of West Java, Indonesia, north-east of Bandung. It was the centre of Sumedang Larang, a principality subordinate to the Sunda Kingdom that claimed the Sundanese royal heritage after 1579.

suphanburi.s: Suphanburi is a city in central Thailand on the Tha Chin river, north-west of Bangkok. An early Dvaravati settlement, it became the centre of the Tai polity of Suphannaphum, whose ruler Khun Luang Pa-ngua seized the Ayutthaya throne in 1370 and whose line later ruled Ayutthaya.

second-battle-of-panipat.s: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556 north of Delhi between the young Mughal emperor Akbar, under his regent Bairam Khan, and Hemu, the Hindu general who had taken Delhi for the Sur dynasty. Hemu had the upper hand until an arrow struck him in the eye;…

saramaka.s: The Saramaka are a maroon people of central Suriname, descended from Africans who escaped from plantations in the late 17th and 18th centuries and settled along the upper Suriname River. After decades of war they won a peace treaty with the Dutch colony in 1762.

susquehanna-river.s: The Susquehanna River flows about 700 kilometres from central New York through Pennsylvania to the head of Chesapeake Bay in Maryland, making it the longest river on the east coast of the United States. It takes its name from the Susquehannock, an Iroquoian people who lived…

saidu-sharif.s: Saidu Sharif is a town in the Swat valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, beside the larger town of Mingora. It grew around the shrine of the Akhund of Swat and became the capital of the princely state of Swat under his descendants, the Walis, who built schools, hospitals and…

sayyid-abdul-jabbar-shah.s: Sayyid Abdul Jabbar Shah was chosen as ruler of Swat by the Yusufzai tribes of the valley in 1915, in an attempt to unite them under a single authority. A descendant of the 17th-century saint Pir Baba, he struggled to keep the support of the tribal leaders and was removed in…

savonia.s: Savonia, Savo in Finnish, is a historical province of eastern Finland, a landscape of lakes and forests around Mikkeli and Kuopio. Its people practised slash-and-burn farming and spread far beyond the province, settling in central Finland, Värmland in Sweden and Ingria.

sami-al-hinnawi.s: Sami al-Hinnawi was a Syrian army officer who led the second military coup of 1949, overthrowing and executing Husni al-Za'im in August. He restored civilian government but favoured union with Hashemite Iraq, which alarmed other officers, and in December 1949 Adib Shishakli…

sintra.s: Sintra is a town in the hills west of Lisbon, Portugal. A castle built under Muslim rule crowns its ridge, and the town passed definitively to Portugal after Afonso I took Lisbon in 1147.

samuel-ibn-naghrela.s: Samuel ibn Naghrela (993–1056), known in Hebrew as Samuel ha-Nagid, was a Jewish scholar, poet and statesman of the Zirid kingdom of Granada. Born in Córdoba, he became vizier to King Badis and led Granada's armies in the field.

saltes.s: Saltés is an island in the marshes of the Odiel estuary opposite Huelva, south-western Spain. In the Islamic period it held the town of Shaltish, a seat of the Banu Bakr's taifa in the 11th century and a centre of iron working whose products were exported along the Atlantic…

sierra-de-segura.s: The Sierra de Segura is a mountain range in the north-east of Jaén province, Spain, part of the Prebaetic System, where the Segura river rises. In the 12th and 13th centuries its castles lay on the frontier between Muslim and Christian powers, and after the Castilian conquest…

segura-river.s: The Segura is a river of south-eastern Spain, about 325 km long, rising in the Sierra de Segura in Jaén and flowing through Murcia and Orihuela to the Mediterranean at Guardamar. Its valley and the huertas of Murcia and Orihuela have been irrigated since Islamic times by…

sagunto.s: Sagunto is a town in the province of Valencia, Spain, north of the city of Valencia. As Iberian and Roman Saguntum it was besieged and taken by Hannibal in 219 BCE, an event that led to the Second Punic War.

silves.s: Silves is a town on the Arade river in the western Algarve, southern Portugal. As Shilb it was the chief city of the Islamic Algarve, known for its poets and its red sandstone castle, and the seat of the taifas of the Banu Muzayn and later Ibn al-Mundhir.

sip-song-chau-tai.s: Sip Song Chau Tai ('twelve Tai lands') was the traditional name for the Tai principalities of the Black River region of north-western Vietnam. Each was ruled by hereditary Tai chiefly families, such as the Deo of Lai Chau, which at various times paid tribute to Vietnamese, Lao…

seediq-people.s: The Seediq are an Indigenous Austronesian people of the central mountains of Taiwan, in Nantou and Hualien. Traditionally hunters and farmers known for facial tattooing, they resisted Japanese colonial rule, most famously in the Wushe Incident of 1930 led by Mona Rudao.

shinto.s: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, centred on the worship of kami, spirits and deities present in nature, ancestors and places, at shrines served by priests. It was intertwined with Buddhism for over a thousand years until the Meiji government separated them in 1868…

sadriddin-ayni.s: Sadriddin Ayni (1878–1954) was a Tajik writer, poet and scholar, regarded as the founder of modern Tajik literature. Educated in the madrasas of Bukhara, he joined the Jadid reform movement and later wrote novels and memoirs of pre-revolutionary Bukhara.

shinano-province.s: Shinano Province was an old province of central Japan, now Nagano Prefecture, a mountainous land of river basins among the Japanese Alps. In the Sengoku period Takeda Shingen conquered most of it, fighting Uesugi Kenshin at Kawanakajima in the north.

samseonghyeol.s: Samseonghyeol is a site in Jeju City, South Korea, with three holes in the ground from which, according to legend, the three divine founders of Tamna, ancestors of the Go, Yang and Bu clans, emerged. A shrine was built there in the 16th century, and ancestral rites are still…

santarem-portugal.s: Santarém is a city on the Tagus in central Portugal, north-east of Lisbon, above a fertile river plain. As Roman Scallabis it was an administrative centre, and under Muslim rule a frontier fortress that changed hands several times.

santarem-para.s: Santarém is a city in the Brazilian state of Pará, where the Tapajós river meets the Amazon. The area was the centre of the Tapajó chiefdom, whose finely decorated pottery, known as Santarém style, dates from about 1000 to 1600 CE.

siege-of-pelium.s: The Siege of Pelium was fought in 335 BCE when Alexander the Great attacked the Illyrian king Cleitus at the fortress of Pelion on the western border of Macedon. The arrival of the Taulantian king Glaukias threatened to trap the Macedonians, but Alexander withdrew by a bold…

sextus-pompey.s: Sextus Pompey was a Roman general, the younger son of Pompey the Great. After the murder of Julius Caesar he built a naval power based in Sicily, sheltering opponents of the triumvirs and cutting off Rome's grain supply.

second-swedish-crusade.s: The Second Swedish Crusade was a military expedition traditionally dated to 1249, in which a Swedish force led by Birger Jarl subdued the Tavastians of inland Finland. Known mainly from the 14th-century Erik's Chronicle, it brought Tavastia under Swedish rule and the Catholic…

solymi.s: The Solymi were an ancient people of southern Anatolia, placed by Greek writers in the mountains of Pisidia and Lycia. Homer names them as foes of the hero Bellerophon, and later tradition linked them to the city of Termessos, whose people called themselves Solymians.

saint-elie.s: Saint-Élie is a remote commune in the interior of French Guiana, which grew up as a gold-mining settlement in the late 19th century. Reachable only by river, forest track or air, it was the nominal capital of the territory of Inini, created in 1930 and merged back into French…

saraswati-mahal-library.s: The Saraswati Mahal Library is one of the oldest libraries in Asia, in the palace complex of Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India. Begun by the Nayak rulers of Thanjavur in the 16th century, it was greatly enlarged by the Maratha king Serfoji II, who collected books in many languages.

shin-arahan.s: Shin Arahan was a Theravada Buddhist monk who, according to Burmese chronicles, converted King Anawrahta of Pagan in the 11th century. Said to have come from Thaton, he became primate of the Pagan kingdom and served four kings, guiding the spread of Theravada Buddhism in Burma.

satyrus-i.s: Satyrus I was ruler of the Bosporan Kingdom from 433 to 389 BCE, of the Spartocid dynasty. He cultivated ties with Athens, extended Bosporan power along the Kerch Strait and fought to take the rival port of Theodosia.

sybaris.s: Sybaris was a Greek city on the Gulf of Taranto in southern Italy, founded by Achaean colonists around 720 BCE and so wealthy that its name became a byword for luxury. It was destroyed by its rival Croton in 510 BCE.

simla-convention.s: The Simla Convention was a treaty negotiated at Simla in 1913–1914 by representatives of Britain, China and Tibet on the status and borders of Tibet. It proposed dividing Tibet into an autonomous Outer Tibet and an Inner Tibet under closer Chinese control.

samye.s: Samye is the first Buddhist monastery founded in Tibet, built on the north bank of the Yarlung Tsangpo south-east of Lhasa around 779 under the emperor Trisong Detsen, with the Indian scholar Shantarakshita and, by tradition, Padmasambhava. Its plan forms a mandala, with the…

sanctuary-of-hercules-victor.s: The Sanctuary of Hercules Victor at Tibur, modern Tivoli, was one of the largest religious complexes of Roman Italy, built in the late 2nd and 1st centuries BCE. Raised on massive vaulted substructures over the road from Rome to the Sabine country, it combined a temple, a…

sabagadis-woldu.s: Sabagadis Woldu was a ruler of Tigray in northern Ethiopia during the Era of Princes, holding power from about 1822 until 1831. A lord from Agame, he sought European contacts and firearms to strengthen his position against the Yejju regents who dominated the court at Gondar.

semien.s: Semien is a mountainous region of northern Ethiopia, north-east of Gondar, containing the Semien Mountains and Ras Dashen, the country's highest peak. In the Era of Princes it was a province ruled by powerful lords, notably Wube Haile Maryam, who also controlled Tigray until…

segeda.s: Segeda was a Celtiberian city of the Belli in north-eastern Spain, near modern Mara in the province of Zaragoza. When it enlarged its walls and drew in the neighbouring Titti in 154 BCE, Rome treated this as a breach of treaty and declared war.

semi-subterranean-temple.s: The Semi-Subterranean Temple is a sunken rectangular court at Tiwanaku, near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, and among the oldest structures on the site. Its stone walls are studded with carved tenoned heads, and it held standing stone sculptures, among them the Bennett Monolith,…

surajkund.s: Surajkund is an ancient reservoir in Faridabad, Haryana, just south of Delhi, built like an amphitheatre with stone steps descending to the water on a semicircular plan. Tradition attributes it to a Tomara king named Surajpal in the 10th century, and it is thought to have been…

sakamoto-ryoma.s: Sakamoto Ryoma was a samurai of the Tosa domain who became a leading figure in the movement to overthrow the Tokugawa shogunate. He founded a trading and naval company in Nagasaki, brokered the alliance of 1866 between the rival domains of Satsuma and Choshu, and drafted a…

sergo-ordzhonikidze.s: Sergo Ordzhonikidze was a Georgian Bolshevik and close ally of Stalin who directed the Soviet conquest of the Caucasus, including the invasion of Georgia in 1921. His harsh treatment of Georgian communists who opposed the Transcaucasian federation sparked the Georgian Affair…

sitalces.s: Sitalces was king of the Odrysian Kingdom of Thrace from about 431 to 424 BCE, the son of its founder Teres I. He extended Odrysian power from the Aegean to the Danube, allied with Athens at the start of the Peloponnesian War and led a huge army into Macedonia in 429 BCE.

syrmus.s: Syrmus was king of the Triballi, a Thracian people of the plains south of the Danube, at the time of Alexander the Great's northern campaign of 335 BCE. When Alexander defeated the Triballi, Syrmus fled with the women and children to the Danube island of Peuce, which Alexander…

saint-paul-trois-chateaux.s: Saint-Paul-Trois-Châteaux is a small town in the Drôme department of south-eastern France, east of the Rhône. As Augusta Tricastinorum it was the Roman capital of the Tricastini, and from late antiquity it was the seat of a bishopric, with a fine 12th-century Romanesque…

suffolk.s: Suffolk is a county of East Anglia in eastern England, with Ipswich as its county town. In the Iron Age its land was divided between the Iceni and the Trinovantes, and from the 5th century it was settled by Angles and formed the southern part of the kingdom of East Anglia; its…

saronic-gulf.s: The Saronic Gulf is an arm of the Aegean Sea between Attica and the Argolid peninsula of the Peloponnese, bounded to the west by the Isthmus of Corinth. Its islands include Salamis, Aegina and Poros, and its shores held Athens' port of Piraeus, Megara and Troezen.

somali-youth-league.s: The Somali Youth League was the leading nationalist party of Somalia. Founded in Mogadishu in 1943 as the Somali Youth Club and renamed in 1947, it campaigned for the unity and independence of the Somali territories.

samoan-islands.s: The Samoan Islands are an archipelago of Polynesia in the central South Pacific, settled about 3,000 years ago. Rival chiefly titles competed for power there, with Tongan influence in some periods.

sonam-gyatso.s: Sonam Gyatso was a leading lama of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism and abbot of Drepung monastery. In 1578 he met the Tümed ruler Altan Khan near Kokonor, who gave him the title Dalai Lama; he is counted as the third, the title being given posthumously to two predecessors.

servatius.s: Servatius was a 4th-century bishop of the Tungri, with his see at Tongeren in present-day Belgium. He took part in church councils, including that of Serdica in 343, and opposed the Arian doctrine.

shendi.s: Shendi is a town on the east bank of the Nile in northern Sudan, near the ruins of ancient Meroë. In the 18th and early 19th centuries it was one of the largest markets of the Nile valley, a meeting point of caravans from Egypt, the Red Sea and the interior, described by the…

suluk.s: Suluk was khagan of the Turgesh, a Turkic people of the Western Tien Shan, from about 716 until 738. Allied with the Tibetans and Sogdian princes, he fought the Umayyad Arabs for control of Transoxiana, defeating them on the 'Day of Thirst' in 724 and inflicting heavy losses…

saqal.s: Saqal was khagan of the Turgesh, a Turkic people of the western Tien Shan, from 706 to 711. He succeeded his father Wuzhile, who had made Suyab the centre of a new Turgesh realm after the collapse of Western Turkic power.

sasamon.s: Sasamón is a village in the province of Burgos in northern Spain, on the site of the ancient town of Segisamo, the main settlement of the Turmodigi. In 26 BCE the emperor Augustus made it his base for the war against the Cantabri, and it later became a Roman town on the road…

siege-of-fort-neoheroka.s: The Siege of Fort Neoheroka was the decisive action of the Tuscarora War in North Carolina. In March 1713 a colonial force under Colonel James Moore of South Carolina, made up mostly of Yamasee, Cherokee and other Native allies, besieged the fortified Tuscarora town of…

siamun.s: Siamun was a king of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Tanis for about nineteen years in the 10th century BCE. He enlarged the temple of Amun at Tanis and built at Memphis.

shabaka.s: Shabaka was a king of Kush and pharaoh of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, who ruled in the late 8th century BCE. Succeeding his brother Piye, he conquered the Delta, ended the Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Sais and made Memphis a royal residence, uniting Egypt and Nubia under Kushite rule.

sebennytos.s: Sebennytos was a city in the central Nile Delta, on the site of modern Samannud in Egypt. It was the home of the Thirtieth Dynasty, the last native royal house, founded by Nectanebo I in 380 BCE, whose kings built a temple to the god Onuris-Shu there.

shepenupet-i.s: Shepenupet I was a daughter of Osorkon III and God's Wife of Amun at Thebes in the 8th century BCE, the first holder of the office to wield wide political power. Under Kushite pressure she adopted Amenirdis I, sister of Piye, as her successor, handing the Kushites a peaceful…

sochi.s: Sochi is a city on the Black Sea coast of Russia's Krasnodar Krai, stretching along the shore below the western Caucasus. Before the Russian conquest the area was home to the Ubykhs and other Circassian peoples, and in 1861 it hosted the Circassian assembly that appealed for…

shiban.s: Shiban was a Mongol prince, a son of Jochi and grandson of Genghis Khan, who fought in Batu's western campaign against the Rus', Poland and Hungary in the late 1230s and early 1240s. He was rewarded with lands east of the Ural mountains as an appanage within the Golden Horde.

sarsina.s: Sarsina is a town in the Apennine hills of Emilia-Romagna, Italy, in the valley of the Savio. In antiquity it was the town of the Umbrian Sarsinates, whose defeat by Rome in 266 BCE ended Umbrian resistance, and it became a Roman municipium.

shara.s: Shara was the patron god of the Sumerian city of Umma, worshipped in his temple there during the third millennium BCE. Sumerian texts call him a son of the goddess Inanna, and he appears in Umma's royal inscriptions and in the records of its long conflict with Lagash.

stele-of-the-vultures.s: The Stele of the Vultures is a fragmentary limestone monument erected around 2450 BCE by Eannatum, ruler of Lagash, to celebrate his victory over the neighbouring city of Umma. It shows the god Ningirsu holding Lagash's enemies in a net and Eannatum leading a phalanx of…

san-juan-province-argentina.s: San Juan is a province of western Argentina at the foot of the Andes, with its capital at the city of San Juan. Founded as a town from Chile in 1562, it belonged to the region of Cuyo and became a separate province in 1820.

societe-generale-de-belgique.s: The Société Générale de Belgique was a bank and holding company founded in Brussels in 1822 by King William I of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. After Belgian independence it financed railways, coal mines and steelworks, becoming one of the first great investment banks…

state-of-east-indonesia.s: The State of East Indonesia was a federal state created by the Dutch in December 1946 at the Denpasar Conference, covering Sulawesi, the Lesser Sunda Islands and the Moluccas, with its capital at Makassar. It became a member of the United States of Indonesia in December 1949,…

state-of-pasundan.s: The State of Pasundan was a federal state created by the Dutch in western Java in 1948, named after the Sundanese homeland, with its capital at Bandung. It joined the United States of Indonesia in December 1949, but it was widely seen as a Dutch creation.

sulzbach-rosenberg.s: Sulzbach-Rosenberg is a town in the Upper Palatinate in Bavaria, Germany. Seat of the counts of Sulzbach in the 11th and 12th centuries, it was a centre of the medieval iron industry, which with nearby Amberg made the region known as the 'Ruhr of the Middle Ages'.

sin-kashid.s: Sin-kashid was an Amorite king of Uruk in the 19th century BCE, founder of the dynasty that ruled the city independently as the power of Isin declined. He built a palace and restored temples at Uruk, and many of his inscribed bricks and clay cones survive.
